title: Reform activist suspended after reportedly saying Muslims cannot be British
description: The alleged comments were filmed by an undercover reporter for an ITV broadcast: Undercover a Year in Reform
body: Reform UK has suspended a party activist who reportedly said that you cannot be Muslim and British in footage recorded by an undercover reporter from ITV News. It is also investigating two of its councillors who appear to have advocated for the mass shooting of grooming gang members in the footage. The party's response follows the latest allegations from undercover filming by ITV News, external, which has led to Reform facing questions over its vetting procedures for candidates. A party spokesperson told the BBC it was pursuing legal action against ITV and the documentary's production company which had used undercover reporting to obtain its material. In the ITV documentary Undercover: A Year in Reform - set to be broadcast on Sunday - party activist Jason Powell reportedly says: "You cannot be Muslim and British, it's like oil and water." In the footage, Powell, who has applied to be a Reform parliamentary candidate, also says he believes migrants who arrive illegally should be kept in "concentration camps" if they cannot be returned to their country of origin. Reform said Powell has been suspended from party membership while an internal investigation takes place. Reform is also investigating two councillors who represent the party in the London borough of Hounslow. In the footage, Councillor David Kerr advocates machine gunning thousands of grooming gang members. His colleague Councillor Adam Parkins suggests if he became prime minister he would conduct Sunday morning executions in the Downing Street rose garden. Mr Parkins told the BBC that advocating the death penalty for men who "systemically groomed and raped young girls" was a perfectly legitimate opinion. Mr Kerr has been contacted for comment. In a statement to ITV, Reform said there is "no room for racism" in the party, and added that it has opened investigations where activists or members had "clearly behaved inappropriately". Reform UK has said it has prioritised and improved its vetting procedures. On Wednesday night, ITV News broadcast undercover filming which showed some of Reform's councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language. Responding to the broadcast, Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick said all political parties had "bad apples". Speaking to the BBC's Today programme, he said he "didn't like what I heard in the documentary" but argued that the party had acted quickly, removing or suspending those in the undercover film. title: No further action against government adviser's wife over Palestine Action post, police say
description: Sarah Helm, who is married to Jonathan Powell, was responding to a discussion about the author Sally Rooney.
body: Police say no further action will be taken against the wife of the government's national security adviser after she posted on social media referencing Palestine Action. Sarah Helm, who is married to Jonathan Powell, wrote on X on Thursday: "God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action." She was responding to a discussion about the author Sally Rooney, whose novels will not be supplied to booksellers in the UK following her announcement that she intends to use her royalties to support the proscribed organisation. On Saturday, the Metropolitan Police said Helm's post was "assessed by specialist officers and it was determined that it did not meet the criminal threshold". "No further police action will be taken," the force added. On Friday, the Met Police had said it was "in the process of being assessed to determine whether any further police investigation may be required" after it was "made aware of an X post on Thursday, 15 October referencing Palestine Action". Palestine Action was proscribed as a terrorist organisation in July 2025. Support of the group is a criminal offence and punishable by up to 14 years in prison. Best-selling author Rooney said she would donate earnings from her books to the group, which has a stated goal of "ending global participation in Israel's genocidal and apartheid regime". As a result, Rooney's publisher, Faber, determined it could not sell her novels, including Normal People and Conversations with Friends, in the UK. title: Wirtz delivers but remains Liverpool's conundrum
description: Florian Wirtz is instrumental as Liverpool return to winning ways in the Premier League, but does he remain boss Andoni Iraola's great conundrum?
body: This video can not be played Liverpool come from behind to beat nine-man Brentford Florian Wirtz was instrumental as Liverpool returned to winning ways in the Premier League at Brentford on Saturday, but does the German playmaker remain boss Andoni Iraola's greatest conundrum? Wirtz has come in for criticism amid his struggles to replicate the form which persuaded the Reds to pay Bayer Leverkusen what was a club record £116m in June 2025. Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard even said this week that the 23-year-old could benefit from being taken out of the team altogether, to overcome what the club's former captain perceives as a lack of confidence. The key dilemma facing Iraola was again evident in west London on Saturday. Liverpool bounced back from their first league defeat of the season against Manchester City last weekend by scoring twice in the second half against a Brentford side reduced to 10 men before half-time. The visitors produced plenty of chances, particularly with their man advantage in the second half when they registered 14 of their total 21 attempts. Wirtz was at the heart of things in the final third. The Germany international created more chances from open play (nine) than any other player has managed in a Premier League game over the past six seasons. The last player to create as many chances in a single game in the competition was Sadio Mane, for Liverpool against Burnley, in January 2021 (also nine). In an away game, he is the first player to reach that tally in more than 15 years, since Samir Nasri registered 10 for Manchester City against Tottenham in August 2011. Florian Wirtz completed 53 of the 65 passes he attempted (81.5%) - including a match-leading 38 inside the final third Despite answering his critics with those standout statistics, the impact of his playing style on the dynamic of the team continues to come under scrutiny. BBC Sport pundit and former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy believes a midfield which features Wirtz as the number 10 remains a problem as it makes Iraola's side too easy to play against. "They got the job done. First and foremost, that's another win on the road, which is always positive," Murphy said of Liverpool's performance. "But I thought they looked too easy to play against. The spaces are too big. "They're playing with two wingers and Wirtz at 10, so they're relying heavily on the two midfield players to try and cover so much space. "It was too easy for Brentford to play out and to get in behind. That would be the biggest concern today for me." Liverpool stage comeback to win at nine-man Brentford Haaland scores twice as Man City beat Ipswich Injured Martinez taken to hospital as Chelsea beat Everton Following his latest performance, no player has created more chances in the Premier League this season. He is level with Brighton's Pascal Gross on 18. He played in Munoz to begin Liverpool's fightback, meaning Wirtz has assisted in back-to-back games for Liverpool across all competitions for the first time - although this was only his second goal involvement in seven league games this term. He was at the heart of Liverpool's attack, with a match-leading 12 final-third entries and 37 passes in the final third. However, only Milos Kerkez (20) lost possession on more occasions than Wirtz (19) among Liverpool players, and he won just one of his nine duels. "They don't look solid and don't look together in terms of shape," Murphy said. "Instead of a number 10, where Wirtz is struggling to impact games, put three midfielders in. "Always, the priority is foundation, defence, stability, being hard to beat. The other stuff can follow from there. "At the moment, it just looks a little bit open. Against better teams, you're going to get hurt." This video can not be played Liverpool players in 'delicate' situation over 'demanding' schedule - Iraola Victory took Liverpool up to fifth in the table, with three wins from their first seven league games under Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer. The Spaniard oversaw the Reds' first away league win after conceding first since December 2023, ending a run of 19 winless away games when going 1-0 behind. But, while striker Alexander Isak returned from injury, Iraola was dealt fresh blows as Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong suffered injuries on Saturday. Iraola told BBC Sport: "When you come here, you see the results of Brentford at home and you have to be ready for this kind of battle. "We had a lot of chances. Even at the end, we had some counters where we were three against one and need to finish. When we go 2-1, every throw-in and every free-kick can be a problem. "We are in a delicate situation with some of the players. We were talking about this run of four games in 10 days, it's very, very demanding. "We have to rest again because we have another big, big game against Villarreal [in the Champions League on Tuesday]." title: At least 17 dead in crush at Hindu festival event in India
description: Many more have been injured at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark a Hindu festival.
body: At least 17 people have been killed and many more injured in a crush at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark the Hindu festival of Durga Puja, officials say. The incident occurred during sudden rainfall, which witnesses say prompted a surge of people to try to seek shelter. West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and that 25 people were being treated for injuries. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the regional government was providing help to affected families. Six of the dead have been identified, Adhikari said. A senior police official told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining and the crowd started "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.". Deadly crowd incidents, including during religious festivals, are not uncommon in India due to poor management and lack of adequate safety precautions. Two years ago, 121 people were killed in Uttar Pradesh during a Hindu religious gathering. title: Tributes to Andrews before Champions Cup matches
description: Lions and Sale Sharks are among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31.
body: Several Lions players were visibly emotional during a minute's silence in memory of their late team-mate Hyron Andrews Lions and Sale Sharks were among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31. Former Sale lock Andrews died at the Lions' team hotel on Friday, a day before their Champions Cup pool game against La Rochelle in France. The Lions, who said they would fulfil the fixture in Andrews' honour, lost 31-14. Asked before the match why the Lions had chosen to play, head coach Ivan van Rooyen said: "It's been a tough 24 hours and we've decided to celebrate Hyron, show respect to his wife and his children, and celebrate life. It gets taken away so quickly. "We've had hundreds and thousands of messages from all over the world. "It's not about winning or losing today. It's not about rugby. "We want to show the respect to Hyron, who was an unbelievable guy, an unbelievable player, a world-class dad and a world-class husband. "Us arriving for the game shows how much he means to us and how much it means to everyone." There was prolonged applause from La Rochelle supporters as the Lions players entered the field, and also after the minute's silence that was observed before kick-off. Both sides wore black armbands and several players shed tears during the period of silence, while Andrews' number five jersey was laid out on the turf in front of the Lions' team. Three South African players in La Rochelle's squad - Dillyn Leyds, David Kriel and Salmaan Moerat - then presented a commemorative jersey to their opponents. Hyron Andrews spent just over two years with Sale before departing at the end of last season There were pre-match tributes before all of this weekend's Champions Cup and Challenge Cup fixtures, including at Andrews' former club Sale. Andrews spent just over two years with the Prem club before departing at the end of last season and returning to his native South Africa. Speaking after their 47-27 loss to Glasgow Warriors, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I am really impressed with how the lads have come together, looked after each other and got tighter in the trauma of it. "It is a good indication of the strength of the squad and the depth of the culture, how much they want to get around each other and get through it together. "Hyron represents a large portion of the squad, in that he came here under-rated and got opportunities to show what he is capable of. "He forwarded his career, made Manchester his second home, settled with his wife and had another child. "He left with a lot of good mates and people who consider him as one of their best mates. His impact and what he gave off the field was far more from what he gave on it. It is still really raw to process. "His two boys are too young to really fathom what is going on but I know the lads close to Hyron have been speaking to his two boys already this morning. "We will help their family get through it." title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
description: The Israeli military condemns the violence but the prime minister's office says it is part of a "smear" campaign.
body: Masked settlers are accused of attacking the convoy A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys and called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating. But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened and suggested it was part of a "coordinated campaign to smear Israel". The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank. The diplomats - from Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church - had come to the largely Christian village of Taybeh near Ramallah. They were there to assess the situation on the ground after almost near daily attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to bring in their olive harvest. Video footage from the scene showed masked settlers confronting the convoy. Reports suggest stones were thrown. The Belgian authorities said a car from its consulate had a window smashed and a French mayor was assaulted. Video showed a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a vehicle. Belgium's foreign minister Maxime Prevot condemned the attack and said Israel had a responsibility to bring those responsible to justice. "Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said. "As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice. "Impunity for violent settlers must end. Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them." Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, said he strongly condemned the violence by what he called "Israeli rioters". He said the foreign ministry was in contact with the ambassadors of the countries involved. But he added: "Without detracting from the severity of the incident, it is unfortunate that the visit was not coordinated with the IDF in advance. Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors' security." The IDF said they "strongly condemn the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters." "According to a preliminary inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene at the time of the attack," they added. Netanyahu's office named the injured French official as Bernard Baudoux, the left-wing mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries But Netanyahu's office urged "caution before drawing conclusions" from reports about the attack. It said the images on social media "do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility". A statement continued: "Those circumstances remain under investigation. Israeli police and forensic investigators have launched an investigation to establish the facts and identify those responsible." It added that "these reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest, relying on sensational headlines before the full facts emerge". Netanyahu's office named the injured French official as Bernard Baudoux. The left-wing mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France told the AFP news agency the attack showed a tolerance by Israel's right-wing government for settler violence. The mayor said the settlers kicked him and beat him with iron bars, throwing him to the ground. "It's the gratuitous nature of the violence that stuns me," he said. "They arrived completely enraged." "The whole world needs to know what's happening there. For me, I'll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here," he said. title: Swinney's emotional explanation for his commitment to independence
description: BBC Scotland's political editor Glenn Campbell reflects on John Swinney's SNP conference speech.
body: This video can not be played John Swinney said son is 'reason' for independence This was a more emotional speech than we are used to from John Swinney. His voice quivered as he explained that his personal commitment to the cause is for the future of his 15-year-old son, Matthew. Then the autocue stalled and the SNP leader is heard saying under his breath "oh, come on". A period of silence was broken by the conference crowd who came to his rescue with a standing ovation. Without the prime minister's name being mentioned, this section of the speech seemed to be a response to Andy Burnham's emotional appeal for the union in memory of his father at the Labour conference in Liverpool. Andy Burnham has called for greater devolution in Scotland earlier this week There was a more obvious dig at the prime minister, who visited Motherwell this week to promote regional devolution within Scotland and drew on his experience as mayor of Greater Manchester. Again, without mentioning Andy Burnham by name, the first minister said: "Some think we should just be like Manchester. Well, I'm afraid I disagree. "Scotland is no city. We are no region. We are a nation and soon we will be an independent nation." That went down well in the conference hall - even if the first minister is perfectly prepared to work with the prime minister on plans to create a regional level of government in Scotland, with powers transferred from both Westminster and Holyrood. Swinney also claimed that independence is "very close" in the full knowledge that there will not be another referendum unless there is a sustained surge in public support for Scottish statehood. Part of his strategy for achieving that is to demonstrate delivery in devolved government on issues of everyday concern. That's why he highlighted the roll out of the Scottish government's £2 bus fare cap as an example of cost of living support. It is already in place in the Highlands and across west central Scotland, and now he has confirmed its extension across north east Scotland from April. It should be available everywhere in Scotland by the end of this parliamentary term, by which time he said the Scottish government would, through franchising and regulation, have taken the bus network under public control. John Swinney, pictured with his son Matthew and wife, Elizabeth Quigley, at the SNP conference Announcements on making misogyny a specific criminal offence and new funding for community groups to fight racism are also designed to demonstrate a sense of immediate purpose. His speech seemed to energise those in the hall who are already with him. He also hopes it will engage those across Scotland who might be open to considering independence. Earlier this week, Swinney told me he is loving being first minister and intends to lead the SNP into the next Scottish Parliament election in 2031. However long he stays in office, this will always be a special conference for him - his first since leading his party through a successful Holyrood campaign and the one where he put the personal into his political commitment to independence. title: Boos and bananas on day of defiance at Man City
description: Manchester City fans boo the Premier League anthem before watching their side move six points clear at the top of the table.
body: This video can not be played Haaland nets double as Man City go six points clear at the top It started with Manchester City supporters booing the Premier League anthem and ended with Phil Foden taking an inflatable banana into his Match of the Day interview after helping see off Ipswich to pull six points clear at the top of the table. On a day of defiance in east Manchester, City's fans made their feelings crystal clear in their first top-flight home game since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. Tens of thousands inside Etihad Stadium booed and jeered when the Premier League anthem was played over the speakers shortly before kick-off, then they started chanting 'City, City, City'. The anger did not last. There was a chant about playing Stockport away and the gallows humour continued when City fans sang 'You're going down with the City' to Ipswich's travelling support. City boss Enzo Maresca, who is the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge, said afterwards he felt the air of defiance from the stands even before kick-off. "The environment was very good," said the Italian after a game watched by 60,817, a new record crowd at Etihad Stadium. "The fans, the club and the players are all together on this journey." This video can not be played Manchester City manager Maresca reacts to win against Ipswich Town City's best start since 1897 - but injuries a concern City fans arrived at the ground to find hundreds of inflatable bananas had been placed on seats in the home sections for fans to wave throughout the game. They were visible in the away end at Liverpool last week but this was on a different scale and the Etihad was turned into a sea of yellow. The inflatables are a flashback to the late '80s when what began as a light-hearted joke soon turned into one of the most memorable fan crazes in English football. They are enjoying a revival at a time when City have appealed after being found guilty of charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and creating 'sham contracts' to inflate sponsorship deals by £830m. There were surreal scenes at one point on Saturday as fans jeered during the Premier League anthem while waving the inflatables in the air. "You can tell they are behind us and they're pushing us," Phil Foden said when asked about the fans after scoring on his return to the side following suspension after being sent off against Manchester United on 13 September. Foden's 19th-minute opener was his first goal of 2026. "It's nice to play at home and you can hear how loud they are," he added. "They're giving us that extra boost that we need." This video can not be played Taking over from Pep Guardiola - 20 trophies during 10 seasons in charge - was always going to be a big challenge for Maresca. Seven matches in, City's Premier League record remains flawless. No points dropped, seven wins out of seven despite falling behind against Bournemouth and playing for more than an hour with 10 men at Manchester United. "For sure I didn't expect to win seven out of seven," said Maresca. "We are working well and working good. "I'm very happy especially with the situation in general. "Today we controlled the game for 95 minutes. We created chances, we scored. "We finished with a little bit of suffering together but overall, it is good." On Foden's impressive return to action, Maresca added: "I said since day one that I love Phil. I know him from years ago and I know how good he is. "It's a matter of helping him to again be one of the best players in the Premier League." Despite the off-field turmoil, this is City's best start to a league season in 129 years. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight) have ever won the first seven matches of a Premier League campaign. Both went on to win the title. "First of all, I am very happy because it's a matter of winning games in this business," said Maresca after the game. "We were able to win seven in a row and what made me very happy was day by day with the players, the way they are working and how I can see them improving. "Today I thought we controlled the game, created chances and [were] good off the ball. We are doing well and I think that's the most important thing." On his players dealing with the events surrounding the club off the field, Maresca said: "They are not worried about people who judge from outside because they know people are trying to judge them. "Inside, I promise the players are happy. They're getting credit and I give credit to them." title: Alligator kills 71-year-old man fishing in Florida
description: The 3.7m (12ft) alligator reportedly dragged the man into the water where he was fishing near Orlando.
body: This video can not be played Watch: Police issue warning after fisherman killed by alligator in Florida A 71-year-old man has been killed by an alligator while fishing in a park in central Florida, police have said. The man was fishing near Lake Apopka in the town of Winter Garden when the 3.7m (12ft) alligator came up to the shoreline and attacked him, police captain Michael Mason said on Friday night. The attack happened at around 17:00 local time (22:00 BST) on Friday in Dr Bradford Memorial Park, a few miles west of Orlando. Alligator attacks in Florida are relatively rare, despite a population of about 1.3 million across the state, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC). "Lake Apopka has tonnes of alligators in it, so that's not uncommon to see alligators in this part of town at all," Mason said. The alligator population of Florida has remained steady for many years (file photo) The alligator was "removed as a danger to the public" and "dispatched" by trappers, he said. "Always be aware of your surroundings, always be safe. Local wildlife - respect it, keep your distance," Mason said. "It looks like it's docile, it looks like your Florida emblem, but it can be dangerous." After attacking the man on shoreline, the alligator then dragged him into the water, the FWC said, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. The attack is the second alligator death in Florida this year, after a 31-year-old woman was killed in June while swimming with her friends near Orlando. Alligators are a common site in many parts of Florida, particularly in and around lakes, rivers, and grassy areas. Between 1948 and 2025, there were 32 fatal alligator attacks in the state, out of 500 total incidents, according to the FWC. The BBC has reached out to the FWC for more information. title: Chelsea's Martinez taken to hospital for 'precautionary tests'
description: Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was taken to hospital as Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton on Saturday meant they secured their first clean sheet in nine months.
body: Emiliano Martinez joined Chelsea from Aston Villa for £7.5m Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests" after suffering what boss Xabi Alonso said was a concussion during Chelsea's win at Everton on Saturday. Martinez had earlier played his part in the Blues securing a first Premier League clean sheet in nine months, a run stretching back 23 matches. But the incident overshadowed an important 2-0 victory for Alonso's side at Hill Dickinson Stadium, secured by two goals from Pedro Neto. Martinez collided with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in the 68th minute while attempting to claim a cross from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's free-kick. There was an eight-minute stoppage before the Argentina international was replaced by Mike Penders, who made his Premier League debut for Chelsea, and saw out the remainder of the match. Asked about the incident after the match, Alonso said: "It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait. "What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests. "We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait." There are now doubts over whether Martinez will be fit for Chelsea's next three matches - they face Tottenham and Manchester United in the Premier League, with a Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool in between. This video can not be played Neto scores twice as Chelsea win at Everton Martinez injured as Chelsea beat Everton Neto stars but who was subdued? - player ratings for Everton v Chelsea Chelsea recorded their first Premier League clean sheet for nine months, since a 2-0 win against Brentford in January. Although Alonso said he was "not obsessed" with keeping a clean sheet, his side, who had conceded a league-high 13 goals before kick-off, were keen to address that record after a much-improved 5-1 win over Bournemouth following the international break. There had also been discussion about Chelsea being a "soft" team, particularly away from home in the north of England, having lost 19 of their previous 41 matches north of Luton over the past four years. Last season, Chelsea lost 3-0 at Everton during Liam Rosenior's five-match winless run, a sequence that ultimately cost him his job. The Blues had also won just one of their past nine matches at the Toffees. This time, however, Everton managed just six shots, their fewest in a Premier League game since recording five against Arsenal last December. Chelsea also conceded only one clear-cut opportunity and allowed their lowest expected goals against (xG) figure against top-flight opposition this season at 0.45. They started with a back three of Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill, while goalscorer Neto and Jorrel Hato, who provided the assist, operated as wing-backs. The midfield pairing of Moises Caicedo, returning from international duty, and new signing Jordan Henderson also brought much-needed solidity and experience. It was £117m club-record signing Morgan Rogers, however, who set the tone for a combative display, squaring up to Everton defender James Tarkowski during an eventful first half. "We needed to show that we can win in this way," Alonso added. "We looked solid, we played solidly, we were strong and we stayed in control. "In the first half there were difficult periods with throw-ins, corners and pressure from Everton. You have to overcome those moments. "In the Premier League it is very hard to have complete control in an away game, but you cannot lose your shape or your conviction." Penders has made 81 senior appearances in his career to date With difficult matches to come, there will be questions over whether Penders, who became Chelsea's youngest goalkeeper to play in the Premier League at the age of 21, is ready for the demanding run of fixtures ahead. That concern would be heightened if tests confirm Martinez suffered a concussion, with Premier League protocols typically requiring a minimum 14-day return-to-play process. Chelsea signed Penders from Genk for £17m in 2024 before loaning him back to the Belgian club. He then spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg, where he impressed in both the Conference League and Ligue 1. Genk have developed a reputation for producing elite goalkeepers, and Penders is frequently compared to Thibaut Courtois by those who know him best. Like the Real Madrid goalkeeper, Penders stands at 6ft 7in and has recently served as his understudy in the Belgium national team set-up. He has worked with the same legendary youth goalkeeping coaches, Guy Martens and Gilbert Roex, who also helped develop Koen Casteels, Maarten Vandevoordt, now at RB Leipzig, Lucca Brughmans, who will join Liverpool next summer from Genk, and Nordin Jackers of Club Brugge. They specialise in developing goalkeepers who are good with their feet, including Penders, who recorded the highest average position while playing out from the back under Rosenior at the Ligue 1 club early last season. Roex, who has known Penders since his academy days, believes he is capable of matching Courtois' level of success at Chelsea, Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid. He said: "We have produced a lot of great goalkeepers, but Mike is the one with the potential to reach the same level as Thibaut. His sense of calm is gold in goalkeeping." title: Clayface star says uncomfortable prosthetics helped his performance
description: Tom Rhys Harries says he spent half his time on set with the make-up team.
body: Tom Rhys Harries says wearing malleable prosthetics was a "steep learning curve" Actors are often said to be the face of the film, but in Tom Rhys Harries' breakout role in DC's latest blockbuster, that part of the body becomes the focal point to chart the character's descent into villainy. Rhys Harries plays the lead in Clayface as Matt Hagen - a handsome, successful actor. When his face is mutilated in an attack, he volunteers for trials of a new treatment with horrifying side effects that transform his face into living clay. The Welsh actor said he spent about half of his time on the set with the special effects make-up team, transforming into the mutant villain. Despite the difficulty of wearing extensive prosthetics during filming, Rhys Harries said it helped him portray the distress of his character in a film that has been described as a body horror psychological thriller. "There was a benefit to having it, because the character is in discomfort," he said. Clayface first appeared in DC comics in 1940 as a Batman villain, however the character has never been adapted for cinema, until now, and it is the first major studio movie role for Rhys Harries. Harries also wore mouth "plumpers" - also used by Marlon Brando in The Godfather - which are inserted into the mouth to change the shape of the face "Time will tell if I'm prepared for it," the Cardiff-born actor said. "I think it feels like a real privilege to be allowed into that sandbox, it's a cultural thing that is fairly significant in the West certainly. "So I just feel really grateful to be able to put my stamp on Matt and Clayface for the first time." Where possible, the creative team used malleable physical effects to better reflect the consistency of a clay-like substance, something Rhys Harries said was a "steep learning curve". The former Plasmawr pupil shot the entire film with a torn ACL Tom Rhys Harries from Cardiff talks to Lucy Owen about his role in the new DC film Clayface as Matt Hagen - a handsome, successful actor. "You've got these artists who've created this piece of work that happens to be on you and the inclination is not ruin their work, but this stuff really works when you're able to interact with it. "Because you would - if there was something on you that was mutating or morphing - you would go to touch it." Clayface follows the psychological descent of the character Matt Hagen, after his face is transformed into living clay The film is described as a body horror psychological thriller, but Rhys Harries insists the story is relatable. "He's an actor who happens to have lost one of his tools and it would be much the same as if a violinist had lost the use of his hands. "It's just what any of us would do where your means of making a living has been taken away and I think there's a relatability in that." The film's director James Watkins is known for directing horror films including Woman in Black and Speak No Evil Rhys Harries, who has been acting professionally for the past 15 years in English and Welsh, believes Welsh cultural traditions have played a part in his success. "I was taking part in the Eisteddfod when I was five and doing recitals in front of two, 300 people, so it didn't feel alien to me to be pursuing a career within that field. "And I think that's a great strength of us as a nation, our cultural output. "It's fairly ridiculous given the size of the country how impactful I think we are on a global stage, culturally, and I think that's something we should foster within Wales." title: McDermott seeks fix as England fight to save their World Cup
description: Brian McDermott says he can fix the errors that led to England's Rugby League World Cup defeat by Tonga - but is it already too late?
body: The Tongans are ranked fifth in the world rugby league standings, with England third As Tonga's deliriously happy supporters celebrated in their thousands in Perth, England knew they only had themselves to blame. They had passed up plenty of chances to win their 2026 Rugby League World Cup opener and had arguably been the better side for the opening 20 minutes of both halves. But a succession of mistakes - handling errors, needless offloads, sloppy penalties – allowed Tonga to control the momentum for much of the game. By the time Haumole Olakau'atu crashed over for Tonga's fourth try in their 30-12 victory, it was all over. The question is whether England's World Cup hopes are also over already. Not so, insists coach Brian McDermott. "It was a really good contest, when it wasn't it was down to us and the errors we made," he told his post-match media conference. "We stood toe to toe for nearly all the game, but we made errors chasing the scoreboard. I'm not going to say it's an easy fix, but it's something I can change. "We know what is in front of us now. We have to win the next two games. I have seen enough to say we are heading in the right direction. "We were not strategically outdone. There are tonnes of positives to take out of tonight, but one or two things we must get rid of, like losing possession." 15 October - 15 November Australia, Papua New Guinea, New Zealand Listen to live commentary on every men's match, and key women's matches - with coverage on BBC Radio 5 Live, BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app A Tonga side packed with players from the Australian National Rugby League had too much for England Due to the vagaries of the international rugby league calendar, this was McDermott's first match in charge of England since being appointed in April as Shaun Wane's successor. Wane had his critics, many of them justified, but he organised a defensively solid England team who whitewashed Tonga on their tour of Britain in 2023. He left in January after England were well beaten in last year's Ashes, and McDermott has had to piece together a team with minimal preparation. England did not play a single warm-up match; this was their first game since losing to Australia at Headingley in November 2025. They have not won a match since November 2024, against Samoa. A much more assured Tonga side started the evening with a spine-tingling Sipi Tau battle dance and ended it with victory for the first time in seven meetings with England. The relative lack of preparation is out of McDermott's control. Team selection and tactics are not, and that is where the former Leeds Rhinos coach will be questioned. "You cannot play with freedom at international level, you have to keep hold of the ball," McDermott said after the game. His side looked nervous with ball in hand, too willing to pass up the chance to run at the Tongans and pass the buck. As for selection, McDermott chose a central pairing of Harry Smith and captain George Williams. They were found wanting, with Williams enduring one of his poorest games in an England shirt. AJ Brimson was chosen ahead of Jack Welsby at full-back. Although Brimson scored England's first try, he was also caught out of position for Tonga's fourth. McDermott said he will "have a look" at options regarding selection. Expect changes when the team to face France is named on Tuesday. "You have to give Tonga credit for the scramble, but I reckon we left three or four [opportunities] out there early doors," said Williams. "We lost our way, we were erratic, we must find that balance to improve the team. "We can't be kicking stones. We have a great group of lads, and one loss does not change how we think." England stunned by Tonga in World Cup opener Tonga were cheered on by a large and noisy crowd in Perth on Saturday But will one loss cost England a place in the semi-finals? The complicated group phase makes that possible. There are six nations in the combined Group B-C, but all the teams play just three opponents - think a scaled down version of the league phase in football's Champions League. The top two in the overall table reach the semis. If sides are level on points, head-to-head is the first tiebreaker that will be considered, rather than points difference. But because not everyone in the group plays each other, it may yet be that points difference becomes crucial. England must win their next two games, against France next Saturday and Papua New Guinea on 30 October, to stand a realistic chance of progression. If they do, results elsewhere then become a factor - and it could get complicated. And there is the strong possibility that England will not know their fate for certain until two days later, when Tonga face 2022 finalists Samoa in their last group game. England's best bet, it seems, is to rack up huge wins in the next two games and hope for the best. "We want to rack up some points," England wing Dom Young said. "You know, we're good enough to do it." Maybe England are good enough – but not if they keep making the same mistakes again and again. title: Low-cost clinic helps pet owners with vet bills
description: RSPCA Medway West launches its clinic for the pets of people with low incomes.
body: Christine Gardner described support from the clinic as "amazing" A reduced-cost veterinary clinic has treated 160 pets in its first 11 days, according to the RSPCA. The animal charity's Medway West branch has launched to offer cut-price care for the pets of people on low incomes or receiving benefits. "Your pet would come first. You'd have a bit of toast yourself and pay out for your pet," said Chatham cat owner Christine Gardner. "Having somewhere like this is amazing." She told the BBC it was "just really good to have something nearby that I can get to" with her six cats. Angela Adams said her pets were her "babies", adding: "I would rather starve than they starve." She said she had eight cats, two rabbits, four guinea pigs, two African land snails and a tortoise, and that she did not know what she would do without the animals, as she was unable to work for health reasons. "It's very expensive. Seven of my cats were due for vaccine this month and you can imagine the cost of that," she told the BBC. "That's a lot of money." "I've had friends messaging me struggling, so this place is brilliant for people." The RSPCA's Imara Ó Niocail says some people can longer afford to care for their much-loved pets RSPCA branch account manager Imara Ó Niocail said that "a lot of people who were more than capable of affording to have these animals" were no longer able to care for them due to the cost of living or a change in circumstances. "We would like to keep the animals at home with the owners and treat them there," Ó Niocail told the BBC. The low cost clinic meant that pet owners in Medway could "seek the treatment that they need and then take the animals home", without having to pay the full vet costs, she added. Medway West branch manager Kevin Morton said the charity's centres were "full-to-bursting" with animals and some people "give their animals up because they can't afford to look after them". "Some people might think that if you can't afford to feed it, then don't have it, but if it's your only companion you have, they can keep people going," he said. The branch has supplied 18,909 food items, 1,294 treats and 919kg of biscuits so far in 2026 through its pet food bank. title: Two people due before court following arson attack deaths
description: A man and a woman, arrested after four family members died in an arson attack, are due in court.
body: Four family members of the English famliy died in the arson attack at the home in Waterford on Tuesday Two people who were arrested in connection with an arson attack which killed four family members in Waterford have been charged by gardaí (Irish police). Kim English, Philip English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue was set on fire on Tuesday. Two other children who were also in the house at the time were critically injured and were taken to hospital in Crumlin in Dublin. The suspects, a man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s, were arrested on Thursday and are due to appear in court in County Tipperary on Saturday afternoon. They are expected to be brought before a special sitting of Clonmel District Court at about 16:30 local time. title: Husband calls for PM to intervene after wife detained in Egypt
description: Eman el-Shazly has been held by authorities in Egypt for two months, allegedly due to her sister's activism.
body: Eman el-Shazly from Birmingham has been detained by Egyptian authorities, allegedly in relation to her sister's online activism The husband of a woman who was detained by the Egyptian authorities has called for Prime Minister Andy Burnham to get involved and help with her release. Eman el-Shazly, from Handsworth Wood, in Birmingham, was taken from her mother's house in Cairo two months ago, allegedly in relation to her sister's online activism. Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, said that their family felt "very helpless" and that their "only possible solution" was for Burnham to "make a phone call to Egypt" to end the detainment. The BBC has approached the Egyptian consulate in London for a response. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office said it was in contact with authorities in Egypt. Moustapha said he had had "no contact whatsoever" with his wife, but had heard from her mother that her health had deteriorated due to a lack of food and medical assistance. "It's not a five-star hotel, there's 30 individuals sleeping in a cell with one toilet and one shower," he said. He told the BBC that his wife had travelled to Egypt to look after her elderly, sick mother, who had been undertaking 18-hour round trips to take food to el-Shazly's two brothers in detention. Zeesharn Moustapha (left) said the past two months without his wife had been "horrible" The 46-year-old claimed his wife had been detained due to her sister's online posts from the UK targeting the Egyptian leadership, "How somebody can make videos abroad knowing it's causing direct consequences to people abroad, what kind of person can sleep at night doing that," he said. Her sister told the BBC that she was sorry that her family had been detained. She said this was a tactic used by the Egyptian government to silence critics. But she would not stop posting her videos, because she felt it was her duty to make a stand. Moustapha said their four children were "distraught" without their mother Moustapha described support from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) as "useless" with no calls or updates from them. "We are very angry, we feel that the government isn't doing anything to secure the release of a British citizen," he said, adding that his wife had held a British passport for 20 years. Moustapha, who has four children, said there was no evidence against his wife, who was being left "to rot in jail" and that it was a "clear example of collective punishment". "The kids are very distraught, they are suffering, they've lost their mother at the moment and we genuinely don't know what to do about it," he said. A spokesperson for the FCDO said: "We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt, and are in contact with the authorities." title: Pope discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery
description: The pontiff will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing in St Peter's Square on Sunday.
body: Pope Leo XIV has been discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. The 71-year-old walked unaided to his waiting car, stopping to speak to well-wishers. The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter's Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery. On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff. A statement from his doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed "steady improvement" following his operation. The surgery on Tuesday, which lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The results of further tests to check for any sign that the cancer has spread have not yet been announced. The Pope also spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, in their first call since June 2025. The Vatican said the call was to urge "dialogue and peace". It came as Russia's bombardment of cities across Ukraine intensifies, with a growing number of civilian casualties and no sign of Putin being ready to halt the invasion. The Pope also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshkiy, occupied by Russia and under constant shelling, to allow people to be evacuated and for the urgent delivery of food and medicine. The BBC recently reported on residents there being forced to eat garden weeds to survive. The Pope's schedule has been cleared completely until 20 October, so his reappearance in public so soon is a surprise and will be some relief for Catholics around the world. Those close to the Pope said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America, planned for early November and which includes a visit to Peru, where he was a missionary for many years. It is not yet clear whether he might be fit to travel or require further treatment. title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records
description: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust says a new system will be brought in to protect records.
body: Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were stabbed to death by Valdo Calocane Further members of staff have been sacked by an NHS trust for inappropriately accessing medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims. Nottingham students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020. In May, Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust confirmed it had dismissed 11 members of staff and, in an update on Friday, said a total of 15 people had now been sacked as part of its investigation. The families of Barnaby, Grace and Ian previously welcomed the action taken by the trust but called the development in May a "kick in the teeth". Dr Manjeet Shehmar, medical director at NUH, said: "There is simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason and I hope this sends a really clear message – we will investigate and we will take action. "To lose a loved one in the way that the families of Ian, Grace and Barnaby have is heartbreaking enough. "I am so sorry that they have had this further compounded by the actions of these staff members." Valdo Calocane is currently serving an indefinite hospital order in a high security facility As well as the dismissals, NUH said 15 final written warnings and two first written warnings have also been issued in total. Two cases were found to have no case to answer and no action was taken. The trust said action had been taken against "doctors, nurses, registered healthcare professionals and other staff" and that independent regulators such as the Nursing and Midwifery Council and General Medical Council, the Information Commissioner's Office, and Nottinghamshire Police had been informed. A new system, currently under testing, is being implemented to protect patient records in future and alert the trust of potential breaches. A Your Responsibility, Your Actions, Their Privacy campaign has also been carried out to educate staff about data protection and the "serious consequences" of not following the rules, it added. Shehmar said: "We will continue to investigate inappropriate access to these records and take action as and where necessary. "Alongside this, we are doing all we can to educate our staff on appropriate access and how to keep the records of our patients safe. We are also introducing a new system which acts to detect possible data breaches. "While the actions of these staff members are disappointing, we know that this represents a small number of our wider workforce. "We know staff across the trust are listening, learning and doing what they can to ensure that only lawful and justified access takes place in our hospitals." NUH said investigations were continuing, including into inappropriate access of the files of the surviving victims of the attacks - Wayne Birkett, Sharon Miller and Marcin Gawronski. The Nottingham Inquiry examined decisions made in the lead-up to fatal attacks on 13 June 2023 and the aftermath The first dismissals were made public amid a statutory public inquiry examining the lead-up to the attacks and decisions and actions taken in the aftermath. The judge-led Nottingham Inquiry, external heard from 164 witnesses during 14 weeks of harrowing evidence between February and June 2026, as well as two days of closing statements from core participants in September. The findings of the inquiry, which is being led by retired senior judge Deborah Taylor KC, will be published by May 2027. The hearings scrutinised authorities that had interactions with Calocane in the years before the attacks, laying bare failures and missed opportunities by agencies, including the NHS and police. The inquiry heard Calocane had been sectioned four times under the Mental Health Act and had a history of police interactions linked to violent incidents before the killings. Calocane is serving an indefinite hospital order, after pleading guilty to manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility, due to his paranoid schizophrenia, in January 2024. Barnaby and Grace were walking home from a night out in the early hours of 13 June 2023 when they were killed NUH is among a number of organisations in which staff inappropriately viewed records or information related to the fatal attacks. In December 2024, an investigation opened into allegations Ministry of Justice (MoJ) staff illegally accessed computer files related to the Nottingham attacks. The public inquiry has since heard court workers also inappropriately accessed information about the case in January 2024. Amy Holmes, the interim director general for the chief operating group of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), told the inquiry she could not detail what information was accessed due to the ongoing police investigation. The inquiry also heard seven probation service officers were identified as having accessed the information. HM Prison and Probation Service found four of those officers accessed files legitimately, but three did not have a legitimate reason to do so. However, it was deemed by the probation service and the Ministry of Justice's data protection unit that the breaches were not serious enough to warrant further action. Footage and images related to the attacks were also viewed numerous times by Nottinghamshire Police staff without a legitimate policing purpose. The force confirmed it would carry out an audit of how many times the information was viewed and whether it was appropriate, following a complaint by Barnaby's mother, Emma Webber, in March. title: Violent clashes between police and protesters in Albania
description: Police in Albania's capital Tirana have fired tear gas and water cannons onto crowds gathered outside the Ministry of Education where students are among those protesting.
body: This video can not be played Student protests have continued for a fifth day in Albania's capital Tirana as students gathered outside the Ministry of Education to continue to demonstrate against poor education facilities, rising living costs and alleged government corruption. The protests quickly turned violent with footage showing protesters throwing molotov cocktails towards police. In response, riot police have clashed with the protesters, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse them. The protesters have demanded the resignation of the country's Prime Minister Edi Rama, but he is reported to be resisting demands to step down. title: UK must protect against Russian 'hybrid attacks', ex-national security adviser says
description: Lord Ricketts says more should be spent on improving the resilience of energy, transport, air traffic control and defence sites.
body: The government must do more to protect key infrastructure against "hybrid attacks" from Russia, a former national security adviser has told the BBC. Lord Ricketts said more money should be spent on the defence budget, as well as improving the resilience of energy, transport and air traffic control. He warned hybrid attacks were becoming "more reckless, more dangerous" and that people could end up being killed. It comes after MI5 chief Sir Kevin McCallum said in his annual speech earlier this week that threats from foreign states, including Russia and Iran, had quadrupled in the last decade. Lord Ricketts told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that ministers had to warn British people about what might be coming. "Not only is [Russian President Vladimir] Putin trying to break morale in Ukraine, he's also trying to undermine morale in European countries," he said. He said there had been a stark warning from the head of MI5 that there could be worse to come in terms of hybrid attacks in the UK or on other Nato territory. Responding to a question about the impact of disruption by Russia, Lord Ricketts said: "I'm not saying there's going to be industrial war with tanks rolling across the north German plain. "But yes these hybrid attacks are getting more reckless, more dangerous...people are going to end up getting killed somewhere." Hybrid attacks tend to use non-military methods, such as hacking, in an attempt to destabilise a country. Moscow is suspected to be behind many such attacks in Europe since the start of the war in Ukraine, but it has always denied involvement. As well as cyber-attacks, hybrid attacks can include attempts at sabotage and efforts to spread misinformation. Lord Ricketts's warning comes after US President Donald Trump blocked sanctions on Russia. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said the decision "only encourages him [Putin] to keep attacking" Ukraine. The former national security adviser, who also previously ran the Foreign Office, said the UK's focus should be on putting more effort into the coalition of the willing, rather than attempting to act as a bridge between Zelensky and Trump. "I don't think in Trump's current mood there is any influence Britain can have in the short term," he said. A growing number of European leaders have warned that Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine. Last month, Germany said Russia was responsible for a drone attack on an airport in Leipzig, in which an explosive failed to detonate close to Ukrainian cargo planes. French President Emmanuel Macron warned in September that the threat of hybrid attacks by Russia against Europe and France had intensified. title: Ex-Reform politician likens party's response to criticism to an abuser
description: Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, who defected to Plaid Cymru, says she is "not surprised" by new allegations.
body: Sarah Cooper-Lesadd defected from Reform UK to Plaid Cymru in September An ex-Reform UK politician has likened her former party's response to criticism as being "like an abuser in a domestic abuse relationship". Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, who defected to Plaid Cymru last month, also said she was "not surprised" by recent allegations of sexism and misogyny within the party, claiming she had personal experience of such behaviour. Reform UK says Cooper-Lesadd should resign and called her claims "outright fabrications". An ITV undercover investigation, due to be broadcast on Sunday evening, has filmed several of the party's supporters and candidates over a 12-month period, with several making racist and sexist comments. Reform UK said all those featured in the programme were under investigation, with some having resigned, while others were suspended. Cooper-Lesadd was elected as a Member of the Senedd for Pen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg in May as a Reform UK member before switching to Plaid Cymru in September. In an interview with BBC-produced Newyddion S4C, she claimed there was a sexist and misogynistic culture within the party when she was a member and said she was "on the receiving end" of such comments. Pointing to two separate incidents, she claimed a prominent party member told her she "looked like a screamer" during a political rally. She alleged the same member also told her she "did not need to be elected as she could be replaced by a 60-year-old man." She said there was a wider culture of sexism and misogyny which meant she "did not feel empowered to report" these instances and claims they "would not have been taken seriously" by the party. When asked whether Reform supporters had some justification in labelling criticism levelled at them as being part of a "woke agenda", Cooper-Lesadd replied that such comments were "straight out of the Reform playbook", likening the blaming of the establishment to an abuser in a domestic abuse relationship. "Reform's playbook is if they can't defend the indefensible, they turn it on the person actually finding and making the allegations," she said. "I think ultimately Reform needs to play within the rules other parties play by." Reform UK said Cooper-Lesadd's comments were "outright fabrications from an individual who lied her way into Welsh Parliament". "If Ms Cooper-Lesadd had an ounce of integrity or respect for her office, she would resign immediately and return the seat to a Reform representative. Instead, she invents wild stories to smear her former colleagues. "The fact the media is taking these fantasies seriously without a shred of evidence is frankly astonishing." title: Watch: 'Mood has really shifted' as Paris protesters clash with police
description: The BBC is on the ground at the Place de la République, where protesters and police clash after weeks of students demonstrations.
body: This video can not be played There was widespread tension on the streets of Paris on Saturday as police deployed to the streets during demonstrations against against falling education standards, rising fuel prices and the cost of living. The protests began last ‌month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, falling standards in public services. Hundreds of protests were planned across France, with tens of thousands set to participate. The BBC's correspondent Adina Campbell reports live from the Place de la République in Paris. title: Nursery owner in China jailed for life after hundreds of children poisoned
description: She and five staff members were found to have used the inedible paint in meals to make them look more appealing.
body: Kitchen staff was instructed to use inedible paint to enhance the look of meals to attract more students, the court found A nursery owner and five members of her staff have been jailed after they were found to have poisoned more than 200 children with lead-tainted food. Li Huifang, who operated the Heshi Peixin Kindergarten in Tianshui, in the Gansu province, was sentenced to life in prison for producing and selling toxic and harmful food, according to Chinese state media. In July 2025, 247 pupils and staff at the nursery were found to have abnormally high blood lead levels after children began falling ill. A report into the incident found that chefs at Heshi Peixin had used inedible paint to "enhance the look" of its meals to attract more students - despite the paint being being clearly marked as such. In addition to the sentence, the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court also ordered the confiscation of 500,000 yuan (£56,200; $74,700) of Li's personal assets, state broadcaster CCTV reported. Nursery executive principal Zhi Jinglin was sentenced to 15 years in prison and fined 300,00 yuan. Four other members of staff who worked in the nursery's kitchen received sentences of between six to eight years, according to state media. The court found the four had been instructed by Li and Zhi to add toxic and harmful ingredients to food served to children and staff. Food samples were later found to contain lead 2,000 times in excess of China's national safety limit. The investigation into the poisoning began after 235 children from Heshi Peixin nursery had to be treated for lead poisoning after eating steamed red date cakes and sausage corn buns. Investigators found that the red date cake and the corn sausage rolls had lead levels of 1052mg/kg and 1340mg/kg respectively, both of which far exceed the national food safety standard limit of 0.5mg/kg. Lead poisoning is "particularly harmful to young children" and can "severely damage the brain and central nervous system", according to the World Health Organization. Officials later found that dozens of provincial officials and hospital staff attempted to cover up the incident by tampering with blood tests and accepting bribes from a nursery investor. China has since published a set of national guidelines for the provision of meals on campuses. Among the measures is the requirement for every new batch of food to be tested, and for flour, rice and cooking oil to be purchased from centralised procurement points only. title: Harry Styles debuts new track in memory of Liam Payne
description: The pop star performed the song on the second anniversary of Liam Payne's death.
body: The pop star made a moving speech to the crowd at Madison Square Garden before performing the unreleased song Harry Styles performed an unreleased song he wrote for his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne. The Grammy Award-winning star played the track, called What Is Enough, during his sold-out concert at Madison Square Garden, on the second anniversary of Payne's death. Styles is currently performing at the New York venue as part of a residency on his record-breaking Together, Together tour. Addressing the packed crowd on Friday night, the singer paid tribute to Payne as a friend and someone he "wouldn't have been able to do this without". As a spotlight shone over him, Styles made a moving speech, in which he honoured Liam Payne, who died two years ago after falling from a hotel balcony in Argentina. "I feel incredibly lucky to get to play these shows here in New York, and this building means a lot to me," said the artist. "There are so many people in my life, friends and people that I've worked with that I wouldn't have been able to do this without," he continued. "And two years ago today, I lost one of those friends." This was met with cheers from the audience, who were hearing What Is Enough for the first time. Wearing a royal blue jumper with a red collar, the musician then urged fans to keep an eye out for and support each other. "I'm sure a lot of you have been through similar things. I hope you haven't. "But really, it's just about looking after each other." He added that there were "so many more people who have touched my life in such special ways", thanking those who helped him get to where he is. "I'm gonna play you a song I wrote for my friend about two years ago, if that's all right." As he paused, passionate cheers and clapping could be heard from his fans. The singer then began to play his guitar and perform What is Enough, which featured emotional and reflective lyrics. As he sang out to the crowd, his band played a melodic accompaniment. Sharing their reaction to Friday night's performance on Instagram,, external Harry Styles' fans described What is Enough as "beautiful". Styles launched his solo career in 2017 after becoming a global star in One Direction. His first album and single were both UK number ones, while his record Harry's House won a Grammy and a Brit Award after its release in 2022. title: Recovery driver sentenced after runaway car crush
description: CCTV footage captured the vehicle rolling down the road, dragging driver Sean Baker along.
body: This video can not be played WATCH: The moment an unsecured Range Rover began rolling down the road in Bournemouth A vehicle recovery driver has been sentenced after he failed to secure a Range Rover that later rolled down a hill, dragging him along and crushing a member of the public who tried to help. Sean Baker, a driver for GRS Recovery Bournemouth, was sentenced to 14 weeks in prison, suspended for one year, at Bournemouth Crown Court on Friday. CCTV showed the two-tonne vehicle rolling down Exeter Crescent during a recovery operation on 22 March 2024, with Baker caught by a rear wheel. Kai Dransfield was on a break from his job at TGI Fridays when he saw Baker trapped under the runaway car "hanging on for dear life" and tried to help, only to be struck by the 4x4. Dransfield said: "He made eye contact with me, and my first thought was to just grab him to try and help him." But in his attempt to help, Dransfield was hit by the vehicle and pulled underneath it. The vehicle rolled over both of his legs, causing serious injuries including multiple broken bones in his legs and fractures to his spine, according to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE). Dransfield continues to suffer chronic pain more than two years after the incident, and has difficulty walking. Watch the latest episode of South Today Listen to the latest news from Dorset An HSE investigation found Baker had initially attached a winch to the front of the Range Rover, which would have prevented the vehicle rolling away if the handbrake was released or failed. But Baker later removed the winch, jacked up the vehicle and placed skates beneath the rear wheels, it said. Because the wheels were not secured with chocks, and no breakaway cables were attached, there was nothing preventing the vehicle from rolling backwards when it was lowered on to the skates. The investigation concluded Baker failed to take reasonable care for his own safety and that of others by not following established recovery procedures. The HSE also found his actions fell below the standard expected of a competent and experienced recovery driver. Baker later pleaded guilty to breaching Section 7 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. Speaking after the sentencing hearing, HSE inspector Alexander Ashen said: "Sean Baker was an experienced recovery driver. "Failing to properly secure a vehicle weighing more than two tonnes on a steep hill was a fundamental error. "This happened in a busy town centre, close to restaurants and car parks, with vehicles, motorcyclists and pedestrians regularly passing through the area. "Sean Baker's failings were substantial, they exposed everyone nearby to risk and resulted in a member of the public, who stepped in to help, suffering life-changing injuries." title: DIY SOS to be 'rested' next year to save money, BBC says
description: The long-running programme will be replaced by a "more cost-effective" spin-off show revisiting past projects.
body: The programme, presented by Nick Knowles, will be replaced by a "more cost-effective" spin-off show revisiting past projects The long-running home renovation TV series DIY SOS will be "rested" next year in the light of "savings challenges", the BBC has said. It will be replaced by a spin-off show featuring highlights from past episodes. Sources denied reports in the Sun newspaper the programme would be axed as part of a plan to make savings. Presented by Nick Knowles, DIY SOS sees a team transform the homes of families who are facing severe illness, disability, bereavement or building disasters. It was first broadcast in 1999 and is currently airing its 35th series on BBC One and iPlayer. The decision comes during the corporation's drive to save £500m over three years. It has already cancelled several well-known TV shows including Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live At The Apollo. A BBC spokesperson said: "In light of the BBC's savings challenges we have taken the decision to rest DIY SOS in 2027 and commission a new spin-off show instead from producers South Shore. "DIY SOS Rebuilt My Life will revisit successes from the show's past and expand the brand on the BBC in a more cost-effective way next year." Knowles, pictured in 2000, became a household name after the show's early success After initially concentrating on small-scale renovations, DIY SOS shifted focus to tackle a number of more ambitious projects throughout its multiple-decade run. Among them was a 2015 special that saw hundreds of volunteers work alongside Knowles, Prince William and Prince Harry to build housing for veterans in Manchester. William returned to the programme in 2018 for a two-part special supporting survivors and the community affected by the Grenfell Tower fire. The emotional episodes saw the team build a new community centre and restore the Dale Youth Boxing Club, which was destroyed in the disaster. Brothers William and Harry joined Knowles in a 2015 episode The programme's latest episode saw the team overhaul a family's property to allow their 17-year-old son Dan - who has complex disabilities - to receive treatment at home after spending more than three years in hospital. Dan's father, Nigel, told the BBC it was a "miracle". title: Rare pink diamond goes on display in France 100 years after amateur heist
description: The French royal jewel will be on public display for the first time since it was found hidden in an apple after a 1926 theft.
body: The nine-carat, pear-shaped gemstone was one of few royal jewels to survive the French Revolution A rare pink diamond is going on display in France for the first time since it was stolen almost 100 years ago to the day - the last time it was shown to the public. The nine-carat, pear-shaped gemstone known as the "Grand Condé" was pilfered in an overnight raid on the Château de Chantilly in October 1926 and concealed in a hollowed-out apple. The diamond - one of few royal jewels to survive the French Revolution - was recovered a few weeks later when a hungry maid at the hotel in which the thieves were staying took a bite of the apple. It will once again be on display in the Condé Museum at the Château de Chantilly until 3 January. The museum's director Mathieu Deldicque said that while the apple story may sounds far-fetched, it was widely covered by newspapers at the time. Deldicque has faced questions about whether the exhibition may be tempting fate, especially given the string of heists on European cultural institutions in the past 12 months, including the daring daylight robbery of jewellery from the Louvre museum in Paris. While he declined to reveal to CNN how much the diamond was insured for, he noted that extensive academic study into the properties of the diamond had taken place to make it uniquely identifiable. The results of this analysis, as well as previously unseen archive material about the gem's history and theft, form part of the exhibition, according to the museum. Naturally occurring pink diamonds are exceptionally rare and often sell for tens of millions of dollars. The highest price ever fetched for one at auction was $71.2m (£53.6m) in 2017, according to Sotheby's. The exact origins of the Grand Condé remain a mystery. It was first mentioned in 1740 in an inventory of Louis Henri de Bourbon, Prince of Condé, drawn up following his death, the Château de Chantilly said. It then became part of the collection of Queen Marie-Amélie of Bourbon-Sicily, the wife of French King Louis Philippe I, and then her son, Prince Henri of Orléans, the Duke of Aumale. He bequeathed it to the Institut de France, which now owns the Château de Chantilly, 50km (31 miles) north of Paris, along with thousands of artworks and manuscripts which became the Musée Condé collection. title: Boy, 16, and 80-year-old man die in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond
description: Emergency services were called at about 16:45 on Friday, and pronounced both dead at the scene.
body: A 16-year-old boy and 80-year-old man have died following a light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond. Emergency services were called to the scene of the crash at about 16:45 on Friday. The boy and man were pronounced dead and their next of kin have been made aware, police said. Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch conduct their inquiries. The light aircraft took off from Glasgow Airport, before crashing near Drymen The Piper Tomahawk II aircraft is registered to Leading Edge Flight Training in Renfrew, according to the Civil Aviation Authority's aircraft register, external. It took off from Glasgow Airport on Friday afternoon at 16:17. It stopped transmitting at 16:37, a few miles north east of Drymen in Stirling. Earlier the plane had taken off from Cumbernauld Airport at 11:46 on Friday morning, before flying 15 minutes to Glasgow Airport. It stayed there until about 13:00, before doing a two-hour flight north east to Newport on Tay before turning round and heading back to Glasgow. It was on the ground at the airport for just over an hour before it took off again and started its final flight. Gavin Birch-Williams, managing director of Glasgow Airport, said: "We are aware of an incident involving a light aircraft that departed from Glasgow Airport. "This is a deeply tragic event, and the thoughts and heartfelt sympathies from all at Glasgow Airport are with the friends and families affected."
