title: Man City's statement win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo
description: Manchester City record what they will view as a statement win at Liverpool - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo, asks Phil McNulty?
body: Liverpool fans express their disgust towards Manchester City during the Premier League game at Anfield Manchester City made what they will regard as a powerful statement in the most hostile territory against Liverpool at Anfield - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo? City's attention turned to on-field matters in their first game since being found guilty of 114 charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18. The fates, and fixture list, decreed it would be at Liverpool, whose fans nurse the most burning sense of injustice after finishing second to City in 2013-14, 2018-19 and 2021-22. Their argument centres on the belief those titles could have been theirs had City not possessed the high finance of their Abu Dhabi-based owners, using it in the manner that led to them being investigated. With this as the backdrop, City strode into this fevered Anfield atmosphere, with Liverpool fans high on adrenaline and determined to make their contempt for their rivals obvious - then outclassed Andoni Iraola's side in a 3-0 win. On another day, in other circumstances, the manner of City's victory would have fed the narrative that this was a performance of champions, a winning marker laid down to their rivals as they hold a three-point lead at the top of the table. Not here. Not in the Premier League's dysfunctional state. Instead, once the predictable sound and fury had been diluted by City's composure and the swift realisation they were not unnerved by Anfield or the storm raging around the club, this was a surreal experience. After the feast of excitement delivered when Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp presided over the greatest domestic rivalry of recent years, this was an occasion - remarkable as it seems - that seemed robbed of a sense of jeopardy by the circumstances surrounding it. Yes, it was a statement display and City celebrated wildly at the final whistle, but will it count for anything given they await potential sanctions suggested including Premier League relegation or a record points deduction? This video can not be played Highlights: Manchester City beat Liverpool to extend perfect start As Erling Haaland looked close to tears in front of Manchester City's fans, including his father Alf-Inge, and head coach Enzo Maresca pumped his fists in jubilation, Anfield's DJ slipped Fleetwood Mac's 'Little Lies' on to the loudspeakers in a final message of defiance. Maresca said: "We knew there was going to be noise but we need to make our own noise by winning games. We need to learn to deal with the noise but the message is to win games. "For me it's quite easy. I try to focus on things I can control. There are things that are not in my hands so I don't stress about them. "I cannot control things outside football, so why stress? I stress about gameplan, day-by-day training sessions, but the rest it's not in my hands." Haaland added: "For every single person part of Manchester City, every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough. It was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. "It's always tough to come here. If you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been. It was important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about. The thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do." City have appealed against the verdict, but until the dust settles and final decisions are made, this Premier League season is in a holding pattern. When City come to Anfield and win, especially as convincingly as they did here, it should be a win without qualification or questions. This does not apply amid the current uncertainty. Every victory, every league table, will come with a metaphorical asterisk until clarity and finality comes. No-one knows when this will be. Manchester City fans expressed support for chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at Anfield City's players did their jobs to perfection, victory secured by second-half goals from Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki. It is all they can do. There can be no escape, however, from the cloud hanging over Manchester City because every win will carry the same rider - producing a state of inertia that is not good for the Premier League. In the end, a day that promised huge discomfort for City ended in a stroll. City navigated the hostile reception awaiting them at Anfield by arriving through the staff and contractors' entrance - while an inevitable febrile environment awaited them. Even the derided half-and-half scarves were doing a roaring trade, until it was noticed the sky blue half read: 'Shamchester City - The Cheats'. The announcement of City's line-up was drowned out by deafening jeers, while banners around Anfield carried a variety of messages. They including 'A Generation Of Supporters Cheated', 'And After All You Really Robbed Us All' and - in a nod to the Oasis song Stop Crying Your Heart Out, written by Noel Gallagher who was at Anfield, 'All Of Your Stars Are Fading Away'. This was all watched by an impassive City chief executive Ferran Soriano, but any notion their fans would turn on the owners was dispelled by a flag reading: 'In Khaldoon We Trust. We've Won It All', a gesture of support for the embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. City's fans also waved hundreds of inflatable bananas, an old habit when they spent time in the lower leagues in reduced circumstances. There remains the possibility they will get the chance to wave them down the tiers once more in the near future. title: Legoland Windsor evacuated over burst water main
description: Some customers were forced to leave the theme park halfway through their visit on Sunday.
body: The theme park made tannoy announcements ordering customers to leave The Legoland Windsor attraction has closed abruptly due to a burst water main. Customers were told to leave rides and exit the resort at lunchtime on Sunday. Thames Water said it had to shut off the damaged main near St Leonards Reservoir to prevent flooding, which affected supplies to the theme park. It said some local residents had reportedly suffered flooded gardens and it apologised for the disruption. Merlin Entertainments, the operator behind Legoland, said it is continuing to work with local partners and thanked guests for their "patience and understanding". One Legoland visitor, who came with her children from Cornwall, said the sudden evacuation felt "surreal". The woman, who asked not to be named, said: "We were queuing for a ride and had got right to the front when, all of a sudden, everything stopped moving. "Then they came out and said, 'Right, come on, everybody off.' "Over the announcement system, they said there had been some sort of Thames Water disruption in the local area and they didn't have any water. "We'd booked a night in the hotel and stayed there last night, so we're absolutely gutted because we've just had to drive home. "It's a good five-hour drive to come up for a nice day, only to come back after half a day." Thames Water said supplies had been restored and repairs were under way. It said it would provide an update on Monday. A spokesperson for Merlin Entertainments said the resort was closed while Thames Water worked to restore normal service. "We apologise for the inconvenience and thank our guests for their patience and understanding," the group said. The BBC understands the resort will reopen on Monday under normal operating hours. title: Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?
description: Liverpool's struggles at Anfield continue as Iraola still awaits his first Premier League win at Anfield.
body: This video can not be played Highlights: Manchester City beat Liverpool to extend perfect start It is early days but Andoni Iraola will know that if his time at Liverpool is going to be a success, then he must make Anfield a fortress again. Right now, the struggle is real. Liverpool were impressive for the most part against a Manchester City side that arrived on Merseyside with a 100 per cent record. However, once Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the 62nd minute, they capitulated to a 3-0 defeat. As Iraola said post-match to Match of the Day: "We played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. "For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us." His unbeaten start is now over. This was actually his first Premier League defeat in 24 games (W10, D13) since January, including his time at Bournemouth. The Reds, though, are now winless in three Premier League home matches this season - although they have won at Anfield in the Champions League and Carabao Cup - for just the second time ever. That winless run in the league at Anfield stretches back to last season with Liverpool now winless in five successive Premier League home games (D4 L1). Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live: "The best teams in the world are also horrible to play against. Liverpool aren't horrible. "They're an easy touch at the moment. They have too many players that are nice and they have to change that part of things. "Liverpool have got a lot of work to do. "They don't have enough leaders at the moment, apart from Virgil van Dijk barking orders." 'Man City's Anfield win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo' Man City cruise to statement win over 10-man Liverpool Liverpool are winless in three Premier League home matches Going back to the start of the year, Liverpool have won just four games in 13 Anfield Premier League matches. In fact, they have won more matches away from home than at home during this period. A closer look at the stats clearly shows Liverpool's home form has dropped off season by season since 2023-2024, although it is important to note this season is still a very small sample size. Away sides have a lower win percentage at Anfield (12.5 per cent) than at any other stadium in Premier League history. However, is this reputation starting to dwindle? Ex-Man Utd midfielder Paul Scholes told The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast in September: "When you go to Liverpool, especially when Jurgen Klopp was there, the crowd played such a major part. It feels like that's gone… I don't think the fans are quite on board at the minute with what's happening there. "When we used to go there, I'd think, 'how are we going to get the ball?', because they were on top of you. Teams seem to have a lot more possession and look a bit more comfortable than they ever have." And Scholes' former team-mate Nicky Butt added: "The likes of Fulham five years ago are going to Anfield and they're beaten before they even go up the steps." This was Liverpool's joint-biggest defeat at Anfield in the Premier League While Liverpool have won twice on their travels this season, they now sit ninth in the league - and their main issue seems fairly clear. They have scored just seven goals this season - just twice at Anfield - and only seven teams have managed fewer. It was early on in the first half when the cameras panned to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai in the Main Stand at Anfield - all three of them were out with injuries. Among them, the trio have scored six of Liverpool's seven league goals this season and on a day when Man City's attack showed their class, Liverpool didn't show any quality in the final third. City (16) have scored more than double the goals Liverpool (7) have scored this season in the top flight. Across three league games at Anfield this season, Liverpool have failed to score in two of them. That must improve. In Isak's absence, Lewis Koumas put in a great shift. However, the 21-year-old lacks that killer edge in front of goal at this level. The focus must fall on Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. It is this kind of game where you need a match-winning moment and neither showed anywhere near the quality that is expected when you have a price tag of over £100m. There was one moment at 0-0 in the 55th minute when Wirtz had Milos Kerkez and Barcola in acres of space to his left, but chose to shoot and fired wide. "You learn a lot in games like today," Iraola said. "I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It's a loss and we didn't get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot." But deep down, Iraola will know there is a lot of work to do and getting the big money signings to deliver will be high on his agenda. title: Orangutans released back into Borneo forest after devastating fires
description: Rescuers moved the apes after their habitats were threatened by intense wildfires over the summer.
body: The apes were all rescued from wildfires over the summer that threatened their habitats Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer. Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said. Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September. Wildfires in the region are usual for the country's dry season but intensified this year. The apes are critically endangered. Around 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago, according to conservation group WWF. While Indonesia is among many countries to grapple with wildfires each summer, this year's were more intense due to the El Niño ocean warming phenomenon, which makes weather patterns more volatile and intense. Yiari CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said relocating the eight orangutans to the reserve was a "necessary step" when their habitats became unsafe. Among them was Mama Nopi and her offspring Nopi, Naufal and Nopan, who had been surviving in a coconut and rubber plantation before their rescue in early September, Yiari said. Fires had incinerated the surrounding forestry, restricting their access to food and bringing them closer to humans. Indonesian authorities rescued 46 of the critically endangered primates from fires in August and September Mama Lifa and her child Lifa were found in a patch of acacia trees entirely surrounded by oil palm plantations. The degradation of their habitat by wildfires as well as a lack of food sources prompted their rescue in mid-September. Mama Man and her baby, Man, had been monitored by animal rescuers since June, when they were found living in a plantation area adjacent to a small patch of forest. Fires that spread near to the site restricted their roaming area further, leaving them without a safe route to other forestry. The threat of exposure to the blazes led to them being evacuated in early September, Yiara said. The reserve these orangutans were released into was chosen because it there is food and water available and it is connected to other forested areas. Yiari's Argitoe Ranting said: "We want to ensure that rescued orangutans are not simply moved from one place to another, but actually have a chance to survive in their natural habitat." The orangutans were moved to a reserve connected with other forests and with plenty of natural resources Last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature warned that wildfires were burning in habitats containing 52% of Borneo's orangutan population. It says a large portion of the ape's habitat will become inhospitable to them if climate change continues at its current pace. This year's El Niño has become the strongest on record and is expected to have a knock-on effect on the climate into next year. Experts have also pointed to land-clearing practices used to make room for plantations as another factor facilitating the spread of wildfires in Indonesia, with naturally fire-resistant forests replaced by less dense and shaded vegetation. That the orangutan's original habitats had been burned and fragmented to the point they could no longer sustain the primates was the main driving factor behind relocating them, Yiara said. title: Hamilton apologises to Ferrari as Antonelli moves to brink of title
description: Lewis Hamilton's incorrect strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix means Kimi Antonelli can win the world title at the next race in Austin.
body: This video can not be played 'They've thrown away a double podium' - what went wrong for Hamilton? Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team after overriding the pit wall and choosing his own strategy during the Singapore Grand Prix. Ferrari were on course to finish second and third with Charles Leclerc and Hamilton, but instead the seven-time champion fell back to sixth in the closing laps as he fought a losing battle to hold off three cars while on fading tyres. Hamilton apologised to the team over the radio on the slowing-down lap after the race, saying: "Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one." Team principal Frederic Vasseur said: "Clearly we asked them to pit. Charles pitted. Lewis didn't want to pit because he... I don't know why. And then he realised it was the wrong call. It's why he apologised to the team. "Now it's not a drama for me that he made the wrong call. I'm making mistakes, he's making mistakes, we're all making mistakes sometimes. Now we have to look ahead and make mistakes positively." Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win Verstappen perfect and Antonelli hugely mature - driver ratings Hamilton did not speak to the media after the race after saying he felt unwell and being given permission to miss the interview zone, known as the media pen. In a statement released by Ferrari, he said: "Under the virtual safety car, the team called me in but I missed the entry. After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car. "A painful lesson, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I'm sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them. I'll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race." Ferrari called both cars in to the pits during a virtual safety car that was called mid-race. Stopping under the VSC saves about 10 seconds versus stopping under racing conditions. Hamilton said in the statement that his decision was based on his improved pace on the soft-compound tyre after he had been forced to make an earlier pit stop than planned because the medium tyre on which he started the race was not performing. "At a track [where it's] difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work," he said. "Unfortunately the medium didn't perform as well as the soft. I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn't make the progress I needed." His first stop was six laps before Leclerc's and when the Monegasque emerged on to the track, Hamilton was right behind him and initially faster. At one stage, he pointed out to the team that he had "lost two seconds on that lap", but the team decided not to invert the cars. Hamilton followed Leclerc within two seconds for a further 10 laps before slowly starting to lose ground a couple of laps before the VSC. Vasseur said the team decided to leave Leclerc in front because he had pitted later than Hamilton. "The tyre advantage was for Charles, that he pitted six laps later," Vasseur said. "I think it was the right call." However, that argument appears to be somewhat undermined by the fact that the medium tyre emerged as the worst option for the race - as Hamilton had found out in the first stint and other drivers later discovered. Leclerc was put back on the soft when he stopped under the VSC. Hamilton's error means Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli is in a position to clinch his first world title at the next race, the US Grand Prix in Austin, after finishing third behind race winner Max Verstappen and Leclerc. Antonelli's lead over team-mate George Russell, who finished ninth after starting from the back of the grid, has extended to 102 points and 111 over Hamilton. The Italian needs to leave Austin with an advantage of at least 125 points to clinch the title, with five races at most remaining after that. He will do so if he wins the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower at the Circuit of the Americas on 25 October. If he becomes champion this year, the 20-year-old will be the youngest in Formula 1 history. Asked if he would be daring to dream about the title on the flight home, he said: "For sure, but at the same time, I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can. "The mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can. "This weekend I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin. "But at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that." This video can not be played Do things change for 'Mr Consistent' Antonelli as he nears title? There is some doubt about the mathematics of the championship because it is not completely clear how many races are remaining. F1 is pushing ahead with the original schedule, which ends with two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, despite the war in the Middle East, having been reassured the countries are safe. But if the war intensifies before mid-November, those races will have to be cancelled. In that event, the season would end at Imola in Italy, on the same 6 December date as Abu Dhabi, after a two-week break following the Las Vegas race on 22 November. Me

title: Dolly Parton's niece wants to learn Welsh after singing with Bronwen Lewis
description: Dolly Parton's niece, Jada Star, from Tennessee who began learning Welsh during a visit to Wales.
body: Jada Star, a country singer from Tennessee, recorded a Welsh language version of Jolene, alongside singer Bronwen Lewis, from Blaendeulais Dolly Parton's niece wants to learn Welsh after recording a Welsh language version of one of her late aunt's most famous songs, Jolene. Jada Star, a country singer from Tennessee, said: "I truly believe anyone can speak Welsh; it's such a lovely feeling to speak the language, it's a comfortable language." The track was recorded before Parton's death on 25 August and features vocals from the legendary singer-songwriter herself, who sings alongside Star and singer Bronwen Lewis, from Blaendeulais. Since the songs release, Star has said she would like to "roam every inch of Wales" and perhaps visit the Eisteddfod one day, as she enjoys learning more about Wales and the Welsh language. Star and Lewis after recording in a studio in Southampton, while Parton recorded her parts in her studio in Nashville With Star having started learning Welsh on Duolingo, she said that some of her favourite Welsh words so far are Draig (dragon) and Pilipala (butterfly). "When I came to Wales to see Bronwen, I put a lot of effort into learning Welsh; I was on Duolingo all the time, though I need to pick it up again. "The app puts sentences together in such a beautiful way, and they're full of dragons," she laughed. "It's fun." Star explained that the first Welsh words she learned were shwmae and diolch, meaning hello and thank you, to allow her to "greet people in Welsh". Jada with her aunt, the late Dolly Parton Lewis and Star became friends after she saw a video on TikTok of Lewis singing the song in Welsh. After travelling to meet Lewis during Pride Cymru, she visited several places. She went from Cardiff to Caernarfon and Conwy, learning Welsh along the way. Lewis said she was inspired by Star's attitude towards the language: "I never wanted to push singing in Welsh on Jada; the fact that she wanted to and was interested was heartening, she was full of questions about phonetics and pronunciation. "Jada's attitude towards the language is so healthy; there are many Welsh artists who don't even release Welsh music, so the fact that Jada has done so is amazing." Lewis showing the Welsh countryside to Star The pair are currently receiving congratulations from both sides of the Atlantic after releasing their version of Jolene. "I'm so proud of the track," said Star. "I've been emotional all day and have received messages from Wales that mean the world to me, too. "I think people really like it; it's something they haven't heard before." title: Burnham to release details of Man City meetings
description: Andy Burnham has faced criticism for comments he made in the wake of Manchester City being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.
body: Andy Burnham is an Everton supporter Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will release details of his meetings with senior figures at Manchester City following criticism of his comments in the wake of the club being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations. Burnham's previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester has led to questions about his relationship with City's Abu Dhabi ownership, with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch demanding No 10 release all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club. "I've been asked by the leader of the opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I'm happy to do and I'm going to," Burnham told the Rest is Politics podcast. "I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester. "None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021." The prime minister initially told the BBC he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's owners decide to sell up following the guilty verdict before later denying his reaction had "downplayed the seriousness of the findings". However, some Premier League clubs were so "astonished" by Burnham's stance that sources told BBC Sport they were "concerned" about political interference in the appeal process. Sanctions are yet to be announced and City have lodged an appeal against the verdict. City returned to action for the first time since the guilty verdict when they played at Liverpool on Sunday, winning 3-0. Clubs fear political interference in Man City appeal Premier League: Man City face Liverpool at raucous Anfield in first game since guilty verdict Burnham was mayor of Manchester from 2017 until earlier this year and his tenure took place during a sustained period of success for City. As mayor, he championed investment from the Gulf as a way of growing Manchester's economy, a strategy which was initially pursued by the city's leaders before Burnham became the inaugural elected mayor of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. "I don't think I misspoke," said Burnham of his past comments on Man City's owners. "What I would say is my mind hadn't been on all of the issues. My mind had been on Labour Party conference and I was doing interviews in relation to it. "And also, I didn't link those two things. You know, the questions linked those two things. What I would say is they're very separate. "The football issues are different from the investment issues. People will try and conflate those two things, but they shouldn't, in my view. "The football issues, the findings of the independent commission are serious, as I said in the interview." The entire process involving the charges against Manchester City is independent of the Premier League. An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 which led to the verdict announced last month, with City also guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation. The commission's report said that "a number of important club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence". A separate independent appeal board will hear City's appeal. The club continues to deny any wrongdoing. title: PM says it is 'clear' Russia interfered with Brexit vote
description: He says voters were not "sufficiently" informed about how foreign actors sought to disrupt UK democracy.
body: Andy Burnham has said Russia did interfere with the Brexit referendum and warned that similar activities were taking place in France and Germany. The prime minister told The Rest is Politics podcast, external that upon arriving in No 10, he had asked about possible Russian interference in the 2016 vote, adding: "I've had the clear answer that, yes, there was." "I think we've been too much on the back foot on that actually and we haven't informed people sufficiently about the extent to which people are seeking to disrupt the political process from overseas," he added. Burnham did not provide further details about the type or extent of Moscow's activity during the Brexit referendum. Britain Unbound, a pro-Brexit campaign group, said Burnham's comments were "another crude attempt to undermine the legitimacy of the decision that the British people made in 2016". It said that foreign interference in UK elections was "obviously unacceptable" but added: "There is no good reason to believe that Russian intervention influenced the outcome of the referendum in 2016. "It is also insulting to suggest that voters were so easily duped." In his interview, due to be released on Monday, Burnham said he had discussed the problem of Russian interference with Chancellor Friedrich Merz during his visit to Germany earlier this week. "There is certainly misinformation, disinformation that is emanating from Russia into German politics," he said. He continued: "These things are important now to put clearly on the record and I believe help voters in Germany and France understand that some of this politics is instigated via our enemies, namely Russia." It is the first time a UK prime minister has said Russia sought to sway the 2016 Brexit poll but there have long been warnings about efforts by the Kremlin to exert influence on UK politics. In 2020, Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee published a report into Russian interventions in UK elections and referendums. It did not provide a definitive conclusion on whether Russia had attempted to influence the results of the EU referendum but did criticise successive governments for failing to fully assess or counter the threat. In response, the Russian foreign minister dismissed the report out of hand and called it "Russophobia". And a Kremlin spokesman said Russia did not meddle in other countries' elections. In the same year, however, the then-Conservative government said it was "almost certain that Russian actors sought to interfere" in the 2019 general election. BBC Verify has tracked Russian-linked disinformation campaigns including using AI to create fake videos which impersonate journalists and news organisations reporting on Ukraine. One fake news website falsely claimed that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had bought a mansion owned by King Charles at a discounted price. Earlier this year, Vijay Rangarajan, head of the UK Electoral Commission, told MPs that Russian deepfake videos had been "used extensively in elections around the world". "There is no reason to assume Britain would be an exception," he added. Last month, during his speech to the United Nations, Burnham accused Russian agencies of using "every means at their disposal to spread lies and disinformation and prey on people's fears". He announced that the UK would set up a new centre to "stem the poisonous tide" of disinformation. A Downing Street spokesperson said: "We are focused on ensuring our citizens and our institutions are protected from foreign powers and their proxies seeking to threaten lives and undermine our democratic values. "We are doing this by strengthening our powers through the National Security Act, strengthening the resilience of our institutions and critical national infrastructure, strengthening our borders, and strengthening our police and intelligence agencies." The AI videos supercharging Russia's online disinformation campaigns Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation? title: Sensational Smith, relentless quicks - Australia veterans serve reminder
description: The fearsome pace quartet and Steve Smith's brilliance serves as a reminder of Australia's quality as the tourists take charge against South Africa.
body: Steve Smith now has 223 catches in Test cricket, three more than Joe Root in second place for non-wicketkeepers First Test, Durban (day three of five) Australia 390 & 33-0: Maddinson 17* South Africa 284: Bedingham 49; Cummins 3-54 Australia lead by 139 runs Australia's modern Test side remain a fascinating one to unpick. Viewed by many in England as there for the taking in last winter's Ashes despite a 4-1 win, they are also labelled too old by many observers at home. The victims of recent shock defeats by West Indies and Bangladesh, they are still unbeaten in their past nine Test series. But while their struggling batting line-up was bailed out by Matt Renshaw across the first two days of the first Test in Durban, they took control over South Africa on day three in an all-too familiar way. Nine years after they first appeared together as Australia's bowling quartet, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon produced their latest relentless performance to dismiss South Africa for 284. There was even some magic from Steve Smith thrown in too. Cummins took three wickets, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon two apiece, in doing so brushing off any doubts about their effectiveness at the start of a run of Tests against the world Test champions, in-form New Zealand, India and England. At 82-1 in response to Australia's 390, South Africa appeared well in the Test on a relatively good surface. Australia's bowlers searched for early swing and Aiden Markram and David Bedingham countered with a second-wicket partnership which progressed at almost 4.5 runs per over. It was then, at the 20-over mark, captain Cummins reverted to Australia's tried and tested - Lyon one end, the quicks rotating at the other. Having bowled 34% of their deliveries full in the first 20 overs, Starc, Hazlewood and Cummins dragged back their lengths. There were only 19 deliveries pitched fuller than six metres between the 20th and 60th overs. With deliveries easy to hit scarce, Markram and Bedingham attempted forced back-foot drives and edged to slip for 37 and 49 respectively. South Africa were 82-1 after 20 overs (left graphic) but were 214-8 after Australia dragged their lengths back between the 21st and 60th overs (right graphic) Wiaan Mulder was caught in two minds and bounced out by Cummins. Tristan Stubbs top-edged the Australia captain to fine leg. In Australia's first innings, Renshaw, who ground out a superb 190, faced 52 deliveries pitched as short and played a pull or hook shot to four of them. He scored runs with only one of those shots - when he had 176 runs to his name and had faced 368 balls. The contrast to Renshaw's application could not have been greater. Six overs after Stubbs was caught, Marco Jansen, who had struck six fours in quickly reaching 26, also tried to pull Hazlewood off a fuller length and was tamely caught at mid-off. The quality of the bowling and fact the Proteas are playing their first Test since November were other factors in South Africa's slide. At the other end, off-spinner Lyon bowled 19 overs at less than three runs per over. The 39-year-old had a more worn pitch to utilise than South Africa's spinners and found significantly more turn and threat. He also had the sprawling Steve Smith to his advantage. Both of Smith's catches off Lyon, first to dismiss Temba Bavuma and then Kyle Verreynne, were feats of anticipation. He saw both right-handers shape to reverse sweep, gambled and clung on at close range. The first was good. The one-handed second was spectacular. "He's an absolute freak," said Lyon. "He practices that in training. "He is an incredible thinker of the game but the way he moves, premeditates, for those types of catches. "There are not many people in the dressing room that would be able to pull off those two catches." In between, Smith's leaping catch at second slip after Cummins found Bedingham's edge took the 37-year-old back above Joe Root as the non-wicketkeeper with the most catches in Test history on 223. While he ended the day with three more catches than Root, he still has a catch percentage about 77%, which sits below the format average. He creates, and occasionally drops, chances such as these - chances others would not have created. The result is Australia's fabled foursome now have 607 wickets in Tests in which they have played as a quartet. The next most successful bowling four-pronged attack is James Anderson, Stuart Broad, Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali, who took 415 wickets in their 31 Tests together for England. "Each of these players will go down as a legend of Australian cricket," said former Australia bowler Jason Gillespie on ABC Radio. "Starc got hit for a few early but I didn't mind that. "Hazlewood was very good, as he always is. Cummins was hostile. He looked fresh." Much has been made of Australia's ageing side and a perceived lack of succession planning. At 37, Starc is the oldest of the three quicks but his average pace of 141.21km/h in 2026 is higher than any of his past three years. He is also averaging his most swing in a calendar year since 2015. The concern for Australia comes when they are not fit, with Hazlewood having missed all five of last winter's Ashes Tests and Cummins four. Australia's issue right now is keeping each of their quartet on the field, because they appear as good as ever. At 33-0, Australia lead South Africa by 139 runs. Even with bad light halting play early again, they should have the time to press home an advantage across the Test's final two days. title: Who 'simply has to do better'? Liverpool v Man City player ratings
description: How Liverpool and Man City's players rated following their Premier League match.
body: Rayan Cherki scored the third goal for Man City Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored as Manchester City inflicted a first defeat for Liverpool on Andoni Iraola. Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below. Premier League: Man City cruise to statement win at 10-man Liverpool - reaction What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean? Alisson: Could do nothing to keep out Erling Haaland's strike then beaten by a beauty from Jeremy Doku and some solid footwork from Rayan Cherki. 5 Ronald Araujo: Got a cheap yellow card early on and will be annoyed that the first two Man City goals came from his side. 5 Virgil van Dijk: Often pushed out of position to help Liverpool deal with getting outnumbered in midfield. Perhaps could have closed Haaland down quicker. 6 Jeremy Jacquet: Wasn't a bad display from a young talent who is very impressive but this must have been a real eye-opener against a quality City attack. 6 Milos Kerkez: Battled well with Iliman Ndiaye and pushed up regularly but lacked quality in the final third. 5 Alexis Mac Allister: Grew into the game and put in a good shift but struggled once Liverpool went down to 10 men. 5 Ryan Gravenberch: Came in for the injured Dominik Szoboszlai and was Liverpool's best player until he got sent off for a second yellow card. Naive on his part. 6 Victor Munoz: Played with such a fearlessness and was an absolute nuisance for Man City, causing Nico O'Reilly all sorts of problems. 7 Florian Wirtz: Simply has to do better, particularly in games of this magnitude. Was largely ineffective and made some poor decisions. 4 Bradley Barcola: Sharp on the ball and did his defensive duties but, like Wirtz, must to do more in the final third. 5 Lewis Koumas: Making his first Premier League start and the 21-year-old got stuck in from the outset in an energetic display that was loved by the Anfield crowd. 7 Nyoni (on 66, Wirtz): 6 Frimpong (on 75, Araujo): 5 Ngumoha (on 75, Koumas): 5 Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, McConnell, Gianluigi Donnarumma: Had a shaky start but made a string of good saves early in the second half to deny Koumas and Gravenberch and keep the game level. 7 Matheus Nunes: An impressive display and made a great tackle in the box to deny Barcola in the first half. 7 Ruben Dias: Did well to weather the early storm and keep Liverpool out. 7 Marc Guehi: Like Dias, a strong performance at centre-half and can take satisfaction from the way they defended, especially when Liverpool attacked The Kop end. 7 Nico O'Reilly: Solid going forward but had his work cut out against Munoz and was inevitably booked when he fouled the Spaniard in the second-half. 6 Elliot Anderson: Always showed for the ball and constantly involved but lucky not to get booked for pulling Gravenberch back. Got the assist for Doku. 7 Enzo Fernandez: Forced Alisson to make a good stop in the first half but didn't really grow into the game until Gravenberch was sent off. 6 Iliman Ndiaye: Dangerous on the ball and had a few threatening moments before he was replaced by Doku. 6 Rayan Cherki: Capped off a day to remember for Man City with a lovely goal. 8 Antoine Semenyo: Threatening all afternoon and part of an attack that was simply too good for Liverpool once City had the man advantage. 7 Erling Haaland: Had a quiet first half and missed a huge chance early on in the second half but finished emphatically to give City the lead. 8 Doku (on 56, Ndiaye): Came on and scored an absolute belter. 8 Gvardiol (on 66, O'Reilly): 7 Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Reis, Khusanov, Lewis After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users. title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk
description: Police received credible information about possible attacks against Donald Tusk and his defence minister.
body: Donald Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a man accused of plotting an assassination attack against him and his defence minister has been detained. The interior ministry earlier reported that police had received credible information about possible attacks against Tusk and Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz. Security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about the planned attacks, with a spokesman saying officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious". Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" in arresting the suspect. The suspect was arrested in the Lower Silesia region and is a Polish national, Jacek Dobrzynski, a spokesman for the Special Services Coordinator told local media. "In this case we are talking about a strong likelihood that these threats could actually be carried out," he said. The plan was uncovered when an email with information about the potential attack was forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Karolina Galecka said. Tusk has been Polish prime minister since 2023 after previously holding the office from 2007 to 2014. He served as president of the European Council from 2014 to 2019. title: Citroen revives the 2CV for an electric age
description: The French firm is reinventing the classic model as carmakers come under pressure from Chinese rivals.
body: French carmaker Citroen has brought back its 2CV brand in a bid to boost sales of electric cars in a difficult market. The new model, unveiled at the Paris Motor Show, is a small city runabout with retro styling which harks back to one of the company's most famous designs. As a "concept car" intended to show Citroen's direction of travel, it is not yet ready to go on sale but the plan is to have a version in showrooms by 2028. As they face mounting competition from Chinese manufacturers, Citroen and other European brands are exploiting their heritage as a means of selling modern motors. Citroen chief executive Xavier Chardon described the new car as "a modern, ingenious and refreshing response to the mobility challenges of tomorrow". The original Citroen 2CV was launched in 1948, as Europe was recovering from the ravages of World War Two. It was designed as a cheap, robust way for French farmers and country folk to get around. The car had high wheel arches and soft suspension, letting it travel across a ploughed field or rough roads - as legend would have it, without breaking a tray of duck eggs. Its high roof let drivers wear a hat at the wheel. It was easy to drive and simple to repair. The car was so popular, it remained in production for more than 40 years. Over time, it went from being a utilitarian tool for the countryside to a cult classic, and a favourite of hippies and counter-culturalists. Fans of Citroën's 2CV hold annual meet-ups such as this muddy gathering in Switzerland Now, Citroen wants to draw on that heritage to sell an electric, small city car that is expected to sell for less than £15,000. The look of the new 2CV may well evolve as Citroen develops its design. But as it stands, it shares plenty of styling features with its famous predecessor. The high, flared wheel arches, the tall, curved roof and the eye-like headlights are all reminders of the original "deux chevaux" or "two horses". By using memories of an old car to sell a new one, Citroen is following a well-travelled road. VW notoriously brought back the Beetle in the late 1990s, with limited success. BMW's Minis have always carried styling designed to hark back to the very British original. Fiat has been selling a retro-styled Fiat 500 for the past two decades. But the retro-nostalgia trend has accelerated recently, as carmakers have looked for ways to sell electric cars to sceptical consumers. Citroen's French rival, Renault, has led the charge. It started with the Renault 5 E-Tech, which visually echoed the distinctive boxy styling of the original Renault 5, once an ever-present sight on French streets. It has since revived the Renault 4 and Twingo brands as well. VW has the distinctive ID-Buzz minivan, a throwback to the classic T2 Transporter, while Ford is working on a new EV which is widely expected to be called the Fiesta. Rachel Burgess, senior editor of Autocar magazine, thinks it is a strategy that makes perfect sense. "It's a brilliant differentiator from all-new car brands", she says. "An older audience might remember the originals and feel warmly towards them, and a younger audience might find an appeal in the retro aspect." Finding new ways to make cars appealing has become more important than ever, at a time when European manufacturers are facing growing competition from Chinese brands. "Many in the industry believe the big automotive players in Europe…face a very serious existential threat from aggressive Chinese manufacturers," says David Leggett, automotive editor at Global Data. Back to the future: VW looked to the past when designing its ID-Buzz minivan In this hostile business environment, heritage and nostalgia could prove to be powerful weapons for more established brands, thinks automotive researcher and author Dr Paul Nieuwenhuis. "In a world where a wave of credible decent quality Chinese EVs are hitting Europe, linking European designs back to their history while using the latest powertrain technology is something the Chinese cannot do," he says. "The Chinese can establish new design trends, but there is limited history there." But Leggett thinks Citroen will need more than a heady whiff of nostalgia to turn its new car into a best-seller. "A reimagined Citroën 2CV should give a big nod to its ancestor - especially on price and design simplicity as well as visual cues," he says. "But it also needs to be a credible modern electric car in terms of functionality and features, with widespread appeal." title: Saudi capital airport hit by second Houthi strike in two days
description: The Yemeni group says it carried out attacks that killed 13 people in Riyadh over the weekend and targeted two airports and oil facilities.
body: This video can not be played Watch: The scene at Riyadh international airport after strike An international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh has been hit by a second strike in as many days, officials have said. A Saudi military spokesman said a projectile had hit King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, causing a fire in one of its passenger halls. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said there had been injuries. It comes a day after a strike on the same airport killed 13 people and injured 308 others, following similar strikes earlier this week. The Houthis in Yemen said they were behind the attacks and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi Arabian airports and airspace. The group said they had targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones in the past 24 hours. They also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said. He vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that all Saudi airports were potential targets apart from those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. The Houthis have said they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war, as well as an air strike on the airport in Sanaa. On Sunday Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition, said air defences had intercepted a missile near the airport in Riyadh, while authorities were dealing with the fire caused by an "unknown projectile" that hit Passenger Hall No 4. US President Donald Trump has said the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly" on whether to strike the Houthis, while UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting suggested the UK could "potentially" provide more support for Saudi Arabia. Riyadh airport attack another dangerous moment in already tense conflict Saturday's strike was the deadliest single attack on a Gulf Arab country since the war between Israel, the US and Iran began in February. The Saudi-led coalition vowed to respond, calling it a "war crime". Four Saudi nationals, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt were among the dead, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Sunday that an Indian man had succumbed to the injuries he sustained in the attack. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks and confirmed that a US citizen was killed in the strikes. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he was "appalled". The UK Foreign Office is advising against all travel to parts of Saudi Arabia, including areas within 10km (6.2 miles) of the border with Yemen, while other western embassies have warned their nationals about travel in the region. Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said "the Saudi enemy" had launched an air strike on Sanaa International Airport in Yemen's capital. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attack and the BBC has been unable to verify this claim. Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, vice-president of Yemen's internationally recognised government, called for "decisive actions" from regional and international partners. Riyadh's airport was struck on Thursday, an attack that killed three Saudi nationals. The Houthis claimed responsibility and said they had used cruise missiles to target the airport. There were two other deadly attacks on Saudi airports in Abha and Riyadh in the two days prior to that. Smoke and flames seen at King Khalid airport in Riyadh on 8 October The latest uptick in violence comes after a temporary ceasefire between the Houthis and Saudi-led forces, brokered in 2022, collapsed in July. The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive, prompting Saudi strikes. Yemeni pro-government forces later said they had secured the regions. The Houthis currently control around a quarter of Yemeni territory and as much as 80% of the country's population. The Iran-backed armed group hopes to eventually seize complete control. Saudi Arabia fears this would lead to the establishment of an Iranian satellite state on its southern border. title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says
description: The PM was speaking after violent attacks at Polish schools this week left one dead and others injured.
body: A 37-year-old caretaker was killed at a primary school in a town north of Warsaw this week Three violent attacks at Polish schools this week were driven by the "glorification of violence" online, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. The attacks have left one woman dead and others injured, including children. "These are very often spontaneous actions inspired by online activity," Tusk said on Sunday, during a crisis meeting with security services. Police have arrested 117 people across the country for possession knives or other weapons, or for threatening to attack schools or fellow students, after searching tens of thousands of schools. A woman was arrested on Saturday after injuring three people while attacking a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital, Warsaw. It came a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland, following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which led to the killing of a female caretaker. "We are not dealing with any group organized on a big scale," Tusk said on Sunday. "In the past years and months, we have noted - globally and in Poland - a rise in the fascination with violence," he added. The prime minister said the attacks were acts of "nihilistic violence" associated with the extreme right. "Some of the people detained are active in the ultraright environment," he said, adding that police had noticed a rise in online searches of Nazi content as well as of "mass killers who have become idols online". On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian. A day later, the 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in Leszczydół-Nowiny, north of Warsaw. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone". Thousands of Polish ‌police officers visited schools nationwide to try to reassure pupils after the stabbings sparked rumours of a "Bloody Friday" of more attacks stemming from a supposed online challenge. Meanwhile, Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said. A special services spokesman said officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious". title: Owners fear 'healthy' dog died due to orange substance exposure on contaminated land
description: Donna and Pete O'Brien say Misty's health declined after a walk.
body: Misty came back from a swampy pool covered in an orange substance A couple say their dog may have died after being exposed to an orange substance on contaminated land during a walk. Donna and Pete O'Brien noticed Misty's health deteriorating rapidly after wading through a swampy pool close to the Cefn Viaduct near Wrexham. She stated to cough up blood and then, around the time of her death, an ultrasound revealed that she had a heart tumour, which affects just 0.19% of dogs. Donna and Pete said they believe it was linked to the historical chemical dumping that was recently explored in the BBC's Buried documentary, and they are calling for the examination of pet records to see if there are any clusters of rare illnesses. Donna said they did not think much of it at the time after going for a walk near Ty Mawr in December 2019. Misty loved to run in the mud and swamps, but on this occasion, she came back "covered in a sort of greasy orange film". "At the time you think it might be copper or iron washing down through the landscape but it stank and it was sort of oily all over her coat," Donna added. They vowed not to go back after the orange substance stained Misty for weeks, but the four-year-old dog, who had always been an "really healthy dog", soon became sick. Vets records show that she started to have periodic diarrhoea and vomiting and by 2024, then aged nine, Misty was struggling. "She would get to the end of a walk and just stop for a while," said Pete. "It was unusual but I put it down to her wanting to stay out a bit longer." Misty started to cough up blood and expel it from her nose, with an ultrasound scan showing a growth – believed to be a tumour – on her heart and potentially others on her stomach and lungs. Misty loved to splash about in the pools near the Cefn Viaduct Pete said they were watching the Buried documentary, which premiered in August 2026, when they saw something that made them "sit up and take notice". "People were describing substances similar to what we washed off Misty – greasy, oily orange deposits. "Then we went to the meeting of the Monsanto Contamination Action Group and heard more stories that resonated." He said it was worrying for the many visitors that go to Ty Mawr who might be unaware of the risk, and it has left them with "so many questions" about Misty's health. "That's why we feel that as well as human medical records, pet medical records need to be examined for clusters of rare illnesses," Pete added. Donna seen here on a walk with Misty before her health started to decline Pete and Donna believe that due to many suspected or undocumented dump sites and water run-offs being in public rural areas, pet health data may provide more evidence of the impact of "forever chemicals" on communities. "Illnesses that take decades to develop in humans often progress much quicker in animals," said Pete. "There are so many sites. Who knows what we and they are being exposed to. "That's why we need clear answers." Pete says he would like "clear answers" as he is still unsure what caused Misty to become unwell Their concerns were raised at a Wrexham council meeting by councillor Derek Wright. He called for significant changes to monitoring and management of the contaminated sites that were "just a stone's throw" from the Ty Mawr Country Park. During the meeting he questioned why the areas have a fence that is "only three foot" with no sign saying that chemicals are there, or why it was fenced off. He said one of the ponds has since become a public footpath and that dog walkers and family frequently walk across them, despite no "publicised tests of what is in those lagoons, or what used to be lagoons". A spokesperson for Wrexham council said investigations indicated deposits came from mining activity. "We have inspected the area with Natural Resources Wales and they have undertaken liaison with the Coal Authority – we are satisfied there is no requirement for any further action to be taken," he said. title: Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win
description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen secures his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli.
body: Before this weekend, Max Verstappen had not won a race in Singapore Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second dominant victory within a week as he secured his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix. Verstappen fought off an attack from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc off the start line to control the race from start to finish. The win followed his and Red Bull's maiden victory of the year in Malaysia last weekend and sprint race success in Singapore on Saturday, confirming the team's re-emergence as a major force. Leclerc took second as team-mate Lewis Hamilton finished sixth after a baffling strategy that was a consequence of the Briton choosing not to pit when asked. Hamilton, trying to last out on a set of soft tyres for a mammoth 44 laps, lost out in the closing laps to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli's third place combined with team-mate George Russell finishing only ninth after starting from 19th extends the Italian's championship lead to 102 points. That means it is possible for Antonelli to clinch his first world title at the next race, the United States Grand Prix on 25 October. To become champion in Austin, he would need to win the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. The key stories of the race were: Verstappen's dominance reviving memories of his pomp during his title-winning era A confusing day at Ferrari with regard to strategy Antonelli closing on the world title Verstappen knew he needed to get into the first corner first to try to win the race, given the difficulty of overtaking in Singapore, and he fought tooth and nail to make sure he did. Leclerc got a better start than Verstappen off the line and challenged down the inside as they approached Turn One. But Verstappen squeezed him tight towards the pit wall and with their entry to the first corner so compromised, Leclerc eventually backed off and the four-time champion could claim the corner. Verstappen, Leclerc and Hamilton ran nose to tail for the first four laps before the seven-time champion began to drop back from about lap five. Leclerc stuck within a second of Verstappen for a further five laps before the Red Bull began to edge away from him as well. From then on, Verstappen continued to build his lead and never looked like being beaten as he motored away into the distance. "I think the last few races have been really positive for us and it is just great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results," said Verstappen. "It is a really good group of people - I really enjoy working with them and hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year." In the interviews immediately after the race, Antonelli was told he can win the title in Austin and responded: "Can I? Really? Let's not worry about that, let's try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job." Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' championship by 102 points with a maximum of 150 available from the six races remaining in the season Hamilton had started on the medium tyres while Verstappen and Leclerc chose the softs. Despite his theoretically more durable tyres, the Briton pitted on lap 18 to switch to the softs, while Leclerc waited until lap 24 to swap his softs for mediums. Leclerc came out of the pits from his stop just ahead of Hamilton, who had stronger pace on his softer tyres. Yet Ferrari chose not to order Leclerc to let Hamilton through to maximise his pace, a decision that was questioned by Hamilton from the car. A virtual safety car was called on lap 39 and Leclerc and Antonelli, who had chased the Ferraris closely from the start from his fourth place on the grid, took the opportunity for a cheap pit stop - it takes 10 seconds less to stop under a safety car than under racing conditions. Yet Hamilton, despite having older tyres, did not stop, a decision that promoted him to second behind Verstappen. As Leclerc was catching Hamilton, the Briton was told he needed to stop again; he pushed back to suggest he try to go to the end, but was told they were six laps short to make it in terms of tyre life. Leclerc soon caught Hamilton and passed him on lap 46 and set off after Verstappen, but could get no closer than 7.3 seconds to the Red Bull. Hamilton never did stop, but as his tyres lost grip he fell back into the clutches of Norris and Antonelli. A passing attempt by Norris on lap 54 with eight to go saw Hamilton run off track and take to the escape road at Turn One, but as he did, Antonelli grabbed the chance to pass the McLaren, and then Hamilton later on the same lap. Norris followed him through, and now Hamilton fell back towards the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri, who passed him on the final lap after a resolute attempted defence from Hamilton. It was Hamilton's call not to stop and he apologised for it on the slowing down lap. Russell's fight back through the field took him up to seventh as he delayed his pit stop as long as possible. But after dropping back to 10th behind Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Alpine's Pierre Gasly, he passed Gasly after trailing him for 10 laps or so, but could not make it past Hulkenberg, who was himself chasing Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar took the final point in 10th after starting from the back. 1. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 7. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) 10. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) It's off to the Circuit of the Americas in Austin for the United States Grand Prix, from 23-25 October, where 20-year-old Antonelli has his first opportunity to become the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history. title: Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
description: It is the third time this week that Ukraine has targeted Russian tech giant Yandex, forcing the company to suspend its operations.
body: Yandex's data centres have been targeted three times this week - like this one in Sasovo on Thursday Yandex has been forced to pause its operations at a data centre near Moscow after the facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone strike - the third attack on the Russian tech giant's sites this week. The company - dubbed "Russia's Google" - said no one was injured at the centre in Vladimir, east of the capital, but some of its services were unavailable to users. Earlier this week, Yandex said it was struggling to maintain its services after two of its five data centres were hit in Ukrainian strikes. Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months as the war between them continues in its fifth year following Russia's full-scale invasion. Kyiv said it was targeting places that provide revenue streams for Moscow's war machine, and that the attacks could force Russia to divert its resources to repair the damage at Yandex. Sunday's attack came hours after US President Donald Trump warned that Ukraine should "damn well stop" attacking Russia's oil refineries so Moscow could release more diesel to the global market - a deal that has drawn criticism from Europe and sparked a diplomatic row with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky. 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices Yandex confirmed on Telegram that its data centre in Vladimir had been damaged and that operations had been "completely suspended", although it said it was working to restore connectivity. The other strikes against Yandex facilities were on Thursday in Sasovo and Friday in in Kaluga, south-west of Moscow, causing problems for some of its services, such as its AI chatbot and smart home devices. The tech company - which also runs a food-ordering and taxi app used by tens of millions of people - said at the time that its data centres were critical for the normal operation of its services, and that it was "very difficult to predict" when they would be back online. Meanwhile, Russian strikes on Ukraine have continued through the weekend. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine said six people were injured in Russian attacks overnight on four districts in its south-eastern Dnipropetrovsk region. On Saturday, at least 20 people including four children were killed in Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia, local officials confirmed. Russia has previously also struck Ukrainian data centres, causing internet outages and prompting some firms to move their servers abroad. title: Jonathan Ross's daughter Honey is learning Welsh and practising on her dog
description: YouTuber Gav Murphy said Honey Ross has been learning his native language via the Duolingo app.
body: Gav Murphy and Honey Ross met on Instagram and fell in love over their passion for films A Welsh content creator has shared how his girlfriend Honey Ross, daughter of TV presenter Jonathan Ross, is learning Welsh. YouTuber Gav Murphy, 41, said Honey, 28, has been learning his native language via the Duolingo app and has been practising speaking it to their dog, Coco. The pair met on Instagram, but immediately hit it off after discovering their shared love for films. "We just talked about films for six or seven hours, and we haven't stopped talking about films since," he said. Speaking on the BBC Radio Cymru's 'Beti a'i Phobol', Murphy, originally from Caerphilly, said that he often speaks about Wales with his girlfriend's family. He said that Honey, the youngest of Jonathan Ross and his wife Jane Goldman's three children, has an "incredible" memory, which helps when learning a new language. "It's really good because she's so clever and has this memory - her memory is bonkers," he said. Jonathan Ross and Honey Ross pictured at The Conjuring: Last Rites premiere The couple live in London, so opportunities to practise are scarce, but Murphy encourages Honey, who is a writer, podcaster and model, to practise speaking the language to their dog. He said: "She lacks confidence when it comes to speaking it. But because I speak Welsh with Coco, I try to get her to speak Welsh with Coco too." Adding: "'Well, if you speak Welsh with Coco, she's not going to tell you if you're wrong'." Video producer Murphy graduated in Film and Television Studies from Aberystwyth University in 2007. He has lived in London for years, working as a content producer and presenter of videos and podcasts, as well as a reviewer of games and films. He is now one of the best-known faces of the YouTube gaming channel, RKG, which he co-founded in 2019. Gav Murphy, with their dog Coco, has been helping Honey Ross with her Welsh pronunciation Honey Ross was raised in Hampstead, north London and is known as a feminist campaigner calling for respect for women regardless of their size, shape or skin colour. She was a co-founder of the Pink Protest movement in 2017, which campaigned for women's rights, including securing UK government funding to tackle period poverty. "She started doing that when she was really young, and I don't think she realised just how full-time it was," said Murphy. "She's changed laws. She was doing a lot of feminist work, and she was doing this stuff with a couple of other women and they were literally changing laws around it. "She was so good at doing stuff, but it takes up so much time and it takes up so much of your life." Gav and Honey recently took a trip to Universal Studios Florida Since meeting Honey, Murphy has got to know her family and gets on well with her father, as they are both "professional silly-billies" and like to laugh, he said. As one of Britain's best-known TV presenters for decades, Jonathan Ross has met many famous people, and Murphy loves hearing his stories. He said: "If we're watching films or something like that, I always ask him about Anthony Hopkins, Tom Jones, Welsh people and stuff like that. "He's met everyone and has stories about everyone, and I want to hear them." title: Children among 109 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
description: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 350 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.
body: The IOM says people taking this route has increased by 18%, with boats - like the above pictured from April 2026 - getting into trouble At least 109 migrants including 15 children have died and dozens more are still missing after a boat sank off the coast of Djibouti, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has said. The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 350 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night. Around 80 people were rescued, the IOM said. IOM's Djibouti mission chief Alexandre Coissac called the tragedy a "stark reminder" of the dangers migrants face while seeking a new life elsewhere. Tens of thousands of migrants from the Horn of Africa make the perilous journey each year hoping to reach Gulf countries for safety and work, according to the UN agency. In a statement on Friday, the organisation said 52 men, 42 women, nine girls and six boys were among the bodies recovered. "This is a devastating loss of life," Coissac said. "Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives," he added. Local authorities are also arranging burials for those who have died, while the survivors - all Ethiopian nationals - have medical care readily available to them. Yemen remains engulfed in a devastating civil war which has lasted more than a decade. Despite this conflict - and growing instability across the wider region - migrants still cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen driven by poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change. Since 10 September, the IOM said its Displacement Tracking Matrix has observed more than 20,000 "movements" from Ethiopia to Djibouti. The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen IOM said it is providing assistance to 64 of the survivors at its response centre in Obock, including healthcare and support to "restore contact with their families". The UN agency is working in "close collaboration" with local authorities to help migrants and "prevent deaths at sea and on land", it added. According to IOM figures, more than 900 migrants died or went missing taking the same route in 2025, with an 18% increase in the number of people attempting the journey. In March 2026, nine people were killed and 45 were missing after a similar incident. title: Wildlife park remains closed after fatal tiger attack
description: Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after a man entered the tiger enclosure and was fatally attacked on Saturday.
body: An eyewitness took this photograph of the tiger minutes before the incident Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after a man climbed into a tiger enclosure and was fatally attacked by the animal. Emergency services were called to the park near Doncaster, South Yorkshire, at about 13:30 BST on Saturday after reports of a man climbing down into the enclosure from a walkway. An eyewitness described seeing the man wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in and was attacked. Police said the man sadly died at the scene. A park spokesperson said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" remain with the man's family and confirmed the Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised. The spokesperson says many people had contacted them about the tiger and he was safe and well. Staff who were at the scene who were "deeply affected by events" would receive specialist support, they added. South Yorkshire Police said the man's family were being supported by officers. "Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time," the force said in a statement. It added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage." Earlier on Saturday, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened". The park said it would remain closed for the rest of the weekend Ella Ford, 24, from Moreton, Wirral, had visited the park with her boyfriend and filmed the tiger moments before the attack. She described seeing a man by the tiger enclosure "pacing around with his headphones in". A few minutes later, she saw the same man had "climbed up onto the barriers". A woman was close by talking to him, she said, before "he jumped in and crawled in front of the tiger, where the tiger was perched and just lay there". Ford said she then witnessed the tiger grab hold of the man, who she reported as "shouting for help". She estimates around 15 to 20 people were on the enclosure's raised visitor walkway before staff quickly evacuated the area, and shortly afterwards, the park. She described members of the public as being "confused, like what on earth's going on?" "I just know some man was obviously trying to bang on the fence to try and deter the tiger away, but it obviously wasn't doing anything," she said. This video can not be played Watch: What we know about the tiger attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, had been enjoying a family day out when park staff told them the site was being evacuated. She said she had heard what sounded like "gunshots" and an air ambulance had circled above. Pelham added: "There was a big, black tarpaulin over the tiger enclosure." She praised park staff for their handling of the incident, saying it had been "very, very well organised". Foreign Secretary and MP for Doncaster North Ed Miliband said he was "deeply saddened" to hear of the incident and sent his "thoughts and deepest condolences to the family of the individual who died." He added he was "very grateful to the emergency services and staff of the park who responded." Lee Pitcher, MP for Doncaster East and the Isle of Axholme, expressed his gratitude to emergency services for their response. In a statement shared to social media, he said he was "deeply saddened to hear about the tragic incident that has taken place at Yorkshire Wildlife Park today". Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with its Land of the Tigers area opening in 2011. The purpose-built two-acre reserve is home to Amur tigers, an endangered subspecies with around 500 left in the wild. Photos of the enclosure on the park's website shows a high walkway for visitors and fencing above the section where the tigers can roam.
