title: Man dies after tiger attack at wildlife park
description: It was reported the man entered the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster, police say.
body: Yorkshire Wildlife Park is closed for the remainder of the weekend, say management A man has died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have confirmed. South Yorkshire Police said it had been called at 13:35 BST to reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster. The tiger then attacked the man and he died at the scene, the force said. His family had been informed and were being supported by officers, it added. A park spokesperson said: "We are deeply saddened by today's tragic incident. Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies are with the family and loved ones of the person who has lost their life." They added: "We are working closely with the police and relevant authorities and would ask that the privacy of those affected is respected at this extremely difficult time. The park will remain closed tomorrow." Police said the tiger was uninjured, remained in the enclosure following the incident and there had been no wider risk to the public. The park was evacuated and officers remain at the scene. The force added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage." Earlier, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened". Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, was enjoying a family day out when park staff told them the site was being evacuated. She said she heard what sounded like "gunshots", and an air ambulance circled above. Pelham added: "There was a big, black tarpaulin over the tiger enclosure." She praised park staff for their handling of the incident, saying it was "very, very well organised". Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with its Land of the Tigers area opening in 2011. The purpose-built two-acre reserve is home to Amur tigers, an endangered subspecies with around 500 left in the wild. Photos of the enclosure on the park's website shows a high walkway for visitors and fencing above the section where the tigers can roam. title: The rock behind Chelsea's entertainers: Midfield duo key for Blues
description: The performances of Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo underpinned Chelsea's 5-1 victory at home to Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.
body: This video can not be played Highlights: Henderson stars as Chelsea put five past Bournemouth Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson were paired in midfield for the first time as Chelsea produced their most complete performance of the season. In a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth on Saturday, manager Xabi Alonso finally found the control and stability required behind his free-scoring attacking trio of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. The Blues have had no problems scoring goals this campaign, with 15 goals from six matches, but no team has conceded more than their total of 13. Against the Cherries though, Caicedo and Henderson provided the balance to suggest Alonso could finally have found an answer - despite still having to wait for their first clean sheet of the league campaign. Henderson stole the show by scoring his first two goals for the club. He opened the scoring with a curling effort after 66 seconds before adding a 25-yard free-kick to complete the victory. Having also set up Rogers for the second goal after just two minutes and 30 seconds, the 36-year-old became the third-oldest player to score and provide an assist in the same match for Chelsea, behind only Didier Drogba and Gianfranco Zola. Henderson's performance came after a shift in Chelsea's summer recruitment strategy. He arrived on a free transfer from Brentford to add experience to what had been the Premier League's youngest squad. Alonso said: "We signed him for everything. If he's able to score two beauties like today, we are more than happy for him. "But apart from the goals, he's done many, many good things. I think today was a very complete performance. We were in control for most of the game, so I'm happy with that. We had good stability in defence as well." Having not signed a player aged over 30 since Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang in 2022, Chelsea recruited three this summer, with goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez joining from Aston Villa and striker Danny Welbeck also arriving. Now, recovered from a broken arm sustained while jumping over an advertising hoarding during celebrations following England's win over Mexico at the World Cup, Henderson is showing he is more than just a vocal leader behind the scenes. Caicedo made his first start of the season for Chelsea in all competitions There is a strong argument that Chelsea find it easier to cope without the creativity of Cole Palmer than without Caicedo's ability in possession and his knack for breaking up play in midfield. In his 150th appearance for the club, Caicedo lasted 72 minutes. His withdrawal for Romeo Lavia was planned, but the Ecuador international still made a significant impact. Alonso deployed him in a deep role, dropping into the middle of the back three when Chelsea were in possession and allowing young defender Josh Acheampong to push forward. He misplaced just two passes and recorded the highest pass-completion rate of any Chelsea starter. He also made and won more tackles than any other Chelsea player on Saturday afternoon. With Caicedo in the side, Chelsea have won 48.1% of their Premier League matches. Without him, that figure drops to 25%. Alonso said: "You always want to have Moises on the pitch. With him, we have a better midfield area and when you are better in the middle, you have a more complete team. "I think that is something to build around. With the players that we have up front, they are solid in defence as well. So, I'm happy that Moises is feeling better because he's going to be a key player for us. We knew that." The alternative options in Chelsea's midfield include captain Reece James, who is able to play in defence, along with substitutes Romeo Lavia and Valentin Barco, who did not make the matchday squad. It is most likely James who will be attempting to re-take his place from Henderson when back, but the diagnosis on his knee issues remains uncertain. Chelsea remain a work in progress and conceded again through poor set-piece defending for Evanilson's goal. However, if Henderson and Caicedo can help eliminate the defensive lapses, Chelsea can begin to look up the table, with Pedro, Rogers and Palmer already helping to make them the Premier League's top scorers. Alonso said: "I think that they help each other well and they give presence, they give stability. "You know that they are going to be the ones that are going to be helping the rest, not just for their qualities because they understand the game. They can play in shorter spaces but as well defensively they give good balance." Former England striker Alan Shearer told BBC Sport: "Caicedo makes a difference. There's no doubt about it. He gives Chelsea a bit more solidity and stops the ball getting into the back four. "He and Henderson have worked really well, the opening goal being a good example. He definitely makes them more solid, I've been really impressed." This video can not be played Henderson reveals what Palmer said before he scored free-kick... title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
description: Ukraine's leader had said the deal with Russia to release diesel into the US would help Moscow fund the war.
body: This video can not be played Watch: 'Time for Ukraine to get a new president', says Trump US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia. Zelensky warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war in Ukraine, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Speaking as he left the White House on Saturday, Trump said the Ukrainian president "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries. "He'd better damn well stop," Trump said before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal". Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs. "We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," he said. "He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does." The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April. Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war. He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia. Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices The Ukrainian president spoke to several allies on Saturday to discuss the latest developments, calling for "real decisions to protect lives in Ukraine" and to protect European security. His criticism of the US-Russia diesel deal was echoed by EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas echoed Zelensky's criticism, saying suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't." She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday. The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war. That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation. The average price of diesel is currently $6.28 (£4.74) a gallon, according to the AAA – up from last month's $5.94 average, and $3.68 last year. Under the deal, Russia would release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace" followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November. A further million would follow, Trump wrote on Truth Social, and then another 3m tonnes "within a short period of time" – but he noted that this delivery will be "based on the condition of their diesel refineries". In the past 10 months, Russia experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country due to Ukrainian drones strikes on its oil refineries. Diesel production in the Russia dropped by an estimated 30%, according to the International Energy Agency. Trump had already called for new elections in Ukraine last December, external, saying Ukrainian voters should have the choice to replace Zelensky. Since the war broke out in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended. title: Verstappen building major momentum as 'no-one very happy' at McLaren
description: Max Verstappen's revival might not be a serious issue for Kimi Antonelli but it is for McLaren, who had a bad Saturday in Singapore, writes Andrew Benson.
body: Sunday's race will be Max Verstappen's 250th in Formula 1 Max Verstappen is too far behind, and Kimi Antonelli too far ahead, to consider that Red Bull's revival might create any real jeopardy in the championship fight - but the Dutchman is certainly building some major momentum as the Formula 1 season moves into its closing stages. Verstappen finished Saturday in Singapore with pole position for the grand prix to add to the sprint-race victory he had completed in tricky wet conditions earlier in the day. And that gives him a great opportunity to complete a second grand prix victory within a week if he can convert on Sunday. Verstappen has two eager Ferrari drivers right behind him, after Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton both felt that they had just missed out on a pole position that was possible. He also has concerns about Red Bull's inconsistent starts - he lost the lead off the line both in Malaysia last weekend and in the sprint. If he does drop back at the start in Singapore, it is the sort of track where overtaking is at a premium and he will not find it as easy to get back in front as he did on his way to his first victory of the season. And he is, as one would expect, not getting ahead of himself. "It was a good qualifying," Verstappen said. "It was always very close and we got ahead when it mattered and we are very happy with that. "All weekend the car has been in a good window and that makes it a lot easier to find your rhythm. Incredibly happy to start first. Still a long race ahead, a lot of things can go wrong but we have done everything up until now well so hopefully we can continue that tomorrow. "It's been a really positive last few races and we want to keep that momentum going." Verstappen beats Ferraris to Singapore pole Verstappen wins sprint after Russell crashes out Verstappen's maiden win of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend came after a run of three podium finishes in Italy, Spain and Azerbaijan, the last of which might very well have been a first victory had he not had problems in qualifying that left him eighth on the grid when he could have been on the front row. His upturn in form has come as a result of steady work from Red Bull in improving their car and getting it into a position where he feels he can predict its behaviour and therefore push to the limit. When a Red Bull is in that spot, Verstappen can be close to unbeatable. He proved that in his remarkable comeback last year, when he gave McLaren and Lando Norris nightmares with a quite brilliant second half of the season that saw him eat into a 100-point deficit to the championship lead and ultimately miss out on taking a fifth title by just two points. This year, Verstappen's deficit to Antonelli is even bigger than that. He is 129 points behind the Mercedes driver with only 175 still remaining, assuming the two end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi do actually take place in the context of the war in the Middle East. It would take some kind of miracle - involving not only a non-stop stream of wins for Verstappen and a highly unlikely run of poor form and bad luck for Antonelli - for him to turn that around. So the prospect can be realistically dismissed. But he certainly looks as if he will be a contender at the front for the remainder of the season. The McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris before they came together during the Singapore sprint race If that is not a major concern for Antonelli, it certainly is for McLaren. They had their own purple patch in the summer, when Lando Norris took consecutive wins in Hungary and the Netherlands, and would have won in Madrid had it not been for the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car. But the world champions have slipped from competitiveness in recent races, and before the Singapore Grand Prix they lie in third place in the constructors' championship, only 11 points ahead of Red Bull. Saturday in Singapore was a bad day at the office for McLaren. Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were heading for fourth and fifth places in the sprint when Norris made a dive down the inside of his team-mate at Turn Five on the final lap. This is not a common overtaking spot and from a McLaren point of view it was a move with no reward, only risk. The move might have made sense if it had come earlier in the race and enabled Norris to challenge Leclerc, struggling in front of them, for third. But on the last lap, Norris was not going to have a go at Leclerc even if he had got through - the only remaining overtaking place was at the end of the following straight into Turn Seven. If the McLaren drivers swapped places, it would make no difference to the team in terms of a collective points haul, but if it went wrong, the cost could be high. And so it did. Norris was in a position to make a legitimate move, but they came together, pirouetted in tandem, Piastri into the barriers and out of the race and Norris slipping down to eighth. Nine points had become one. The stewards took no action, feeling that "both drivers had contributed to the incident". Piastri had explained in the hearing that he did not expect Norris to try a move there, and attempted to leave space when he saw him. Norris argued that his his car was in a position that, according to the rules, entitled him to make an overtaking attempt, so expected to be left space and had braked and gone over the kerb when he realised he was not going to get as much as he expected. He said: "There are two sides, one is what the stewards say and that's a fair reasoning, no-one's to blame. But I did apologise because it was still me attacking, as I had the right to do. If I just sat there and was boring like I should be, nothing would have happened. So really it's still my fault but I deserved to go for the space and I still believe I had the right for it." Norris added: "As you probably expect, no-one's very happy. I'm not happy,

title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
description: Pike's lawyers say she is "grateful" to the medical team who cared for her after she survived two lethal injections last month.
body: This video can not be played How widely used is the death penalty in the US? US death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital following her botched execution at the end of last month, her lawyers have said. Pike, 50, has been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years and is continuing to receive medical care, according to a statement from her lawyers on Saturday. She survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September, which left her in a critical condition. Pike regained consciousness earlier this week and began speaking - stunning experts, medical staff and her lawyers. Her case is now in uncharted territory as she is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection. Pike's lawyers said in their statement that she was "grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances". It is unclear what medical care Pike is receiving now that she is back in prison but her lawyers previously said she faced a "long road to recovery". The Tennessee Department of Correction is yet to say why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used. I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's I interviewed Christa Pike 20 years ago - I can't stop thinking about her What happened in Christa Pike's failed US execution, and how did she survive? At a court hearing on Wednesday, Tennessee Assistant Attorney General Will Ayers told the judge he did not know whether the state intends to try to execute her again. The judge ordered the state to preserve all evidence related to the failed injections. That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state. Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people. Shipp was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison. Pike was the first woman scheduled to be executed in the state of Tennessee in over 200 years. Her lawyers have spent decades appealing her case. In the days leading up to her scheduled execution, both the US Supreme Court and Tennessee Governor Bill Lee declined to block the execution. Since it failed, Pike's lawyers have renewed their calls for her sentence to be commuted to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Colleen Slemmer was tortured and brutally killed by Pike and Shipp Pike lost consciousness and was taken to a local hospital following her botched execution. Her legal team believed for days that she was brain dead and expected her to be taken off life support at any moment. Pike eventually woke up and began talking again on Tuesday - her lawyer Randy Spivey said her first words were "Where am I?" and "Who are you?" At a press conference on Wednesday, her lawyers said she was shackled to the bed and suffering from pneumonia and significant swelling on her arms, while also being unable to swallow. "We don't know the toll all of this will take" Spivey said of her mental health, adding that Pike felt "angry and confused". title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended by Portuguese FA
description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo is a five-time Ballon d'Or winner Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month. The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark. In a lengthy statement, the Al-Nassr forward later explained he left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust". In a statement, the FPF said a "provisional suspension" was issued on 9 October and they had marked the case as "urgent". The FPF's rules state any player who fails to appear or walks out on international duties faces a ban of one to six months, as well as a fine. Pedro Proenc, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record:, external "This is a time for calm and composure. We are all sitting down together at the table. "There is a strong desire to have our captain back with us. There will be a normal disciplinary process." Ronaldo accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also confirmed he would not be retiring from international football as he continues to chase down 1000 career goals. Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice. He considered retiring from international football after the World Cup in the summer but opted to continue. Ronaldo returned to action last week, scoring his 980th career goal in a 3-0 win for Al-Nassr over Diriyah Club. Two icons, a glorious farewell and a potentially bitter ending This video can not be played Jesus fires back over Ronaldo question The Ronaldo saga has been rumbling on for some time, with many fans critical of former Portugal boss Roberto Martinez's insistence on starting Ronaldo at this summer's World Cup. Things came to a head on 4 October when Ronaldo was an unused substitute in the Nations League win over Norway. The player subsequently left camp after finding out he would also not start against Denmark in November. Ronaldo then published a near 2,000-word statement on Instagram slamming Jesus. He apologised to fans and team-mates while dismissing any suggestion that he had played his last match for Portugal. "We will have one or more farewell matches, there will be time for that," the statement said. Manager Jesus had said the door remains open for Ronaldo to return if he chooses to, but has not commented on his latest statement. Portuguese football journalist Jose Manuel Delgado told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I don't think there is a way back. In the statement, Ronaldo says he will return to the national team but at the same time he calls Jesus a liar three times. "In the polls in Portugal, only 15% of the Portuguese were on Ronaldo's side and people think we owe him a lot but his time is already done and he must understand it. "The problem is that Ronaldo does not understand it, he wants to keep playing as if he was 24, not 41. "Things will never be the same again. No matter what happens, no matter if he plays again or if you have a game to say goodbye to Ronaldo things will never be the same. "What Ronaldo did for Portuguese football is unique and incredible and we must thank him for all the service he gave to Portugal. But at 41, he has no place in the best XI of Portugal." title: Four key takeaways from the Drumcree dispute so far
description: BBC News NI's Political Editor Enda McClafferty assesses the fallout from the Drumcree dispute so far.
body: The secretary of state's decision will likely scupper any hope he had of fostering good relations with unionists For a number of years in the 1990s, the Drumcree parade dispute was one of the biggest stories in Northern Ireland - and then, for 28 years, it fell out of the public eye. However, that changed when the Parades Commission ruled that the march on Sunday 27 September could go ahead with restrictions in place. That parade did not happen and, after a series of legal challenges and talks between residents and Orangemen, the secretary of state banned the procession. On Saturday, a High Court judge said a legal appeal by Orangemen following the secretary of state's decision was not an emergency case and adjourned the hearing until Monday. BBC News NI's Political Editor Enda McClafferty assesses the fallout so far. Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant believed an agreement had been close As steep learning curves go, this one was off the scale. Less than three months into the job, Sir Chris Bryant has had to make what will be the biggest decision of his time in Northern Ireland. He will be forever remembered as the first secretary of state to ban what was a legal Orange parade. But he says he was left with no option in the interest of peace. The police had already ruled out forcing the parade through and when negotiations broke down, he had to step in. The secretary of state had the power to act alone, but it was politically easier to have the cover of a police request. Though making such a significant announcement late on Friday night was not ideal. He clearly wants to move on with Westminster returning from recess on Monday and legacy legislation to be fast tracked through the Commons. But the legacy of his Drumcree decision will follow him for some time and will likely scupper any hope he had of fostering good relations with unionists. History shows parties who walk away from Stormont pay a heavy price at the polls It could have been a moment of great jeopardy for power-sharing at Stormont. The moment when the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) bowed to pressure and effectively collapsed the Executive. But the party moved quickly to remove that threat within hours of the Orange parade being banned from the Garvaghy Road. Party leader Gavin Robinson insisted they "will not sacrifice the stability of Northern Ireland and plunge it into further crisis". To do so, he said, would allow "Sinn Féin an escape route from the spotlight and accountability". For the DUP, pulling down the institutions was high risk with an election on the horizon. History shows parties who walk away from Stormont pay a heavy price at the polls. Especially before a budget is agreed to approve public sector pay rises thus avoiding strikes. The DUP has opted instead to keep the focus on potential lawbreaking by Sinn Féin ministers. It allows for more tough talking in the chamber even though the punishment if convicted will result in fines. Though some in the DUP question if the institutions can be "sustainable" if First Minister Michelle O'Neill and her executive colleagues are found to have broken the law. That will be a calculation for another time and much will depend on the proximity of polling day. But the Drumcree dispute has delivered for Sinn Féin. It provided the platform to supercharge its election campaign and helped deflect from questions around delivery at Stormont. Though the court ruling clearing the way for the A5 has eased some pressure on the party. But it delivered on its promise to residents to ensure no parade down the Garvaghy Road. In truth any prosecutions they may face for standing with residents will be viewed by many within the party as a badge of honour. Allegations of two-tier policing have resurfaced The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) had five million reasons to bring the Drumcree dispute to an end. That's how much the policing operation has cost for the past fortnight at a time when the police budget is already stretched. A bill which would have been much higher had officers faced any violent disorder. But the true cost for the PSNI may come in its relationship with the Orange Order and wider unionist community. Allegations of two-tier policing have resurfaced but so far there have been no calls from unionist leaders for the chief constable to quit which is telling. Forcing the parade through was never an option for the police. Public safety risks aside, the potential to damage relations with nationalists was too great. With the latest PSNI recruitment campaign being launched on Monday, the service couldn't afford to further alienate potential Catholic recruits. The Parades Commission ruled that the march on Sunday 27 September could go ahead with restrictions in place despite objections from nationalist residents It was a body set up to resolve parading disputes, not to restart them. That has been the charge directed at the commission by many over the past fortnight. Its determination, allowing an orange parade down the Garvaghy Road for the first time in 28 years, caught everybody by surprise, including those in the loyal order. It also triggered a spat with the PSNI who tried to distance itself from the determination. The commissioners are now the first to have their decision reversed by a secretary of state, although they will say conditions and the police advice had changed. But there is no escaping the reality that public confidence in the body has been damaged. Restoring that trust won't be easy, nor will finding replacements for the current commissioners when their term comes to an end. title: Timely recognition or long overdue? How Gross is proving all-time bargain
description: Named the Premier League's player of the month for September, BBC Sport looks at Brighton star Pascal Gross' impact both this season and over the past nine years during his two spells at the club.
body: Only Joao Pedro has been involved in more top-flight goals than Pascal Gross this season Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross may be one of the best value-for-money signings in Premier League history. In fact the 35-year-old has effectively cost the Seagulls minus £3m - and been involved in 86 Premier League goals over two spells. Already in this campaign, Gross has been involved in seven Brighton goals in six games. His latest provided the opener in his side's 2-0 win at Sunderland on Saturday, a slide-rule pass finding Maxim de Cuyper to slot home. Gross became the oldest player to provide an assist in three successive Premier League games since a 38-year-old Ryan Giggs did so for Manchester United in February 2012. In 2026, only Bruno Fernandes and Dominik Szoboszlai have created more chances than the German - and that includes the 18 months he was away from the Premier League. Gross was Brighton's first Premier League signing in 2017 for a reported £3m from Ingolstadt. He left for his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in 2024 for £8m - but in a surprise move he returned to Albion in January for about £1.7m. So has Gross been underrated all this time? Former England midfielder, and BBC pundit, Danny Murphy doesn't think so. "The Premier League is shown worldwide, and he has been a part of that for so many years during a time when Brighton have been a shining light," he said. "You don't have to play for a big-six team to be appreciated in the Premier League. Gross is not under the radar, because people know how good he is." This video can not be played Pascal Gross is 'showing the Premier League's elite how it's done' A little-heralded German from relegated Ingolstadt, nobody could have anticipated the impact Gross, nor Albion, would go on to have. "There's an argument Gross is pound-for-pound the best value player in the Premier League over the last 10 years, especially when you look at his goal involvements," said BBC Radio Sussex commentor Johnny Cantor. "However, he also drives standards in training, sets a high bar and is a huge influence in the dressing room. "Technically he is excellent, has superb delivery but also possesses an awareness, popping up in spaces all around the pitch. Managers have leaned on him, team-mates respect him, and fans of all generations adore him. "He will surely be remembered as one of the best Albion players of the modern age." Since joining Brighton, Gross is seventh for Premier League assists with 52 to go with his 34 goals in 253 league games. All the more remarkable when you consider his journey with Brighton appeared over two years ago when he went home to join his beloved Borussia Dortmund. Albion supporter Maz Mirzadeh said: "When he left for Dortmund, it was like going through a heartbreak and seeing an ex go back to their childhood sweetheart. "He's outrageously good and massively underappreciated. "If you watch him play, you would think someone's put him in slow-motion settings, but what he lacks in pace, he makes up in superior football IQ, technical brilliance and working harder than any other player on the pitch." Follow Brighton & Hove Albion on BBC Sounds Pre-match, post-match and topical Albion content Subscribe and listen for everything you love about the Seagulls Gross has been key in Brighton climbing to third in the Premier League Gross played 66 times for Dortmund, scoring one goal and assisting 17 times, but on 2 January 2026, he came back to Brighton. Aged 34 at the time, many wondered if it was more of a romantic career swansong. "There may have been concerns that he may not have been able to recreate the impact of his first period at the Amex but that has been dispelled already," added Cantor. Only Chelsea's Joao Pedro can better Gross' goal contributions this season in the top flight. Pedro has five goals and three assists, to his former Brighton team mate's three goals and four assists. The midfielder - who retired from international football after the World Cup - has also played every single minute for Brighton in all competitions, nine games so far. Former Liverpool and Fulham midfielder Murphy said: "He's an intelligent footballer, with a great football IQ. "You can see that he has grown into that version of himself over the years. That happens in football - it happened to me - when you know what you can't do, as much as you know what you can do. "So, you don't see him trying to beat people on the outside with his pace. Instead he loves a little chop, or a Cruyff turn to give himself space and time, or to play a quick first-time pass around the corners. That's why he always seems to be in space. "His versatility tells you about his intelligence as well. He is able to play as a full-back, central midfield or, recently, as more of a 10. He is scoring and making goals. "I am sure this won't be his last season with Brighton but, even if it was, he is already going to be remembered as one of the Brighton greats by their supporters for what he has given so far to the club, especially with him coming back and doing what he is doing. It is nothing short of remarkable." This form led to Gross being the sixth oldest player to be named Premier League player of the month, for September. Seagulls fan Mirzadeh added: "Even in his 'unc' era, he's showing the Premier League's elite how it's done. "If he was called Pascal Silva and played for a top-six club he might get the recognition and respect he truly deserves." Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan A version of this feature was published on 2 October 2026. title: Northampton outgun Bath in 119-point thriller
description: Northampton win a high-octane 18-try thriller at home to Bath, the second highest-scoring game in English top-flight history.
body: Ollie Sleightholme scored three of Northampton's 11 tries Tries: F Smith, Sleightholme 3, Freeman 2, Dingwall, Pater, Kemeny, Mitchell, Coles Cons: F Smith 8 Tries: Carr-Smith, C Griffin, A Griffin, Green 2, Carreras, Bayliss Cons: Russell 5 Pens: Russell Northampton came out on top of a high-octane 18-try thriller at home to Bath, the second highest scoring game in English top-flight history. The two sides had surpassed 100 points on the scoreboard with 15 minutes remaining and continued to showcase unstoppable, attacking flair as the play went end-to-end. Northampton eventually streaked clear in the second half, with Ollie Sleightholme scoring a hat-trick and Tommy Freeman scoring twice as they finished with 11 tries and bounced back from defeat by Bristol a week ago. The loss is the first of the season for Bath, who made 12 changes for the match, with Arthur Green getting two of their seven tries and Charlie Griffin also scoring one on his Prem debut. The 119 points scored falls short of the record in the English top flight - the 127 points shared in Saints' 94-33 win over Bristol in May. Leicester battle back to beat Gloucester Rory Hutchinson fed Fin Smith to cross first for Saints and while Bath arrived with a younger-looking starting XV there was no evidence of inexperience, as a moment of world-class Finn Russell skill opened a gap for Green to break through and Tom Carr-Smith to cross. Bath hit Northampton again through 21-year-old Charlie Griffin before Saints slickly whipped the ball between their backs until it reached Sleightholme for their second try. Tommy Freeman dived under the posts for Northampton's third right after Bath's Josh Bayliss was shown yellow for repeated infringements but, again, there was nothing to separate the sides as Archie Griffin rolled over under two tacklers for the visitors' third. Kepu Tuipulotu barged through midfield and found Green to make it 26-19 to Bath, which was quickly cancelled out by Fraser Dingwall's score at the other end, leaving Russell's penalty on the stroke of half-time the only mark of difference. Arthur Green was making his first appearance of the season for Bath Green doubled his tally quickly after the restart, but Saints full-back James Pater pounced on Santiago Carreras' dropped ball to steal possession and sprint the distance to the line. Carreras made amends with a try of his own although Northampton started turning the screw despite Bath unloading their bench of big-hitters. Josh Kemeny scored in the corner, Alex Mitchell followed - collecting his own grubber kick in a solo showpiece - and Sleightholme capped a superb move that saw Saints turn the ball over by their own line and sweep up the field. Sleightholme completed his hat-trick four minutes later and while Bayliss kept Bath in touch to close the gap to 57-48, it did not last as Saints had more in the tank. Alex Coles barged over before Freeman rounded off a blockbuster day in the closing stages. Northampton Saints head coach Sam Vesty told BBC Radio Northampton: "Both teams took opportunities pretty quickly and I think both teams will be slightly disappointed in how they exited their end, in terms of when they've got the ball and got control of it. "We gave it up quite a lot to them and put ourselves defensively under pressure We're not happy with the 48 part of that scoreline. "We don't want it to be basketball. Obviously lots and lots of very good stuff but there's a good couple of areas for us to focus to be better - a more ruthless Bath and that's a very different game. [On the attack] "We were so clinical with our execution of what we were doing. Absolutely fantastic. "I thought our breakdown was very good, lots and lots of positives but we need to be better coming out of our end." Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan told BBC Radio Bristol: "It's dsappointing if you score 48 points away from home and lose the game. "I think we lost control between minutes 50 and 60. The back end of both halves we conceded a yellow card and against a team like Saints it's difficult to contain them. "But look at the positives, we played some fantastic rugby today." Replacements: Smith, Fischetti, Neculai, Lockett, Prowse, Taylor, McParland, Belleau. Bath: Carreras; Cokanasiga, Ojomoh, Redpath, C. Griffin; Russell, Carr-Smith; Kirk, Tuipulotu, A. title: King warns malicious online actors are evolving tactics
description: The King spoke of "threats to our international order" in a letter marking the 10th anniversary of the National Cyber Security Centre.
body: The King has previously warned of the "existential dangers" posed by AI King Charles III has warned of the challenges disinformation and other "hostile online activity" pose to trust and security in the digital age. The comments, made in a letter to the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to mark its 10th anniversary, spoke of "malicious actors" continuing to "evolve their tactics by using automated technologies". "From threats to our international order, to the need to balance the risks and opportunities of powerful new technologies, strong cyber security is fundamental to making the online environment safer and more resilient," he wrote. Last month, the King warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands. In the letter published on Saturday by NCSC, the King praised the government agency. He said its achievements over the past decade have included defending the country against cyber attacks, safeguarding democratic institutions and protecting "the critical infrastructure upon which daily life depends". "You have built resilience across our public services, businesses and communities, equipping us all to prosper in our ever-evolving digital world," the monarch added. The King said he was "acutely aware" that much of the work done by the NCSC cannot be praised publicly and that he was filled with "profound gratitude". The NCSC was established in 2016 as part of the Government Communications Headquarters to protect the UK against cyber threats. Earlier this week, the NCSC offered assistance to online shopping store Asos after customers received a notification from its app sent by hackers, the BBC understands. The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people. Asos said it was investigating "unauthorised activity" involving third-party platforms. The company told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the company's users - including names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth. It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed. The letter from the King to NCSC came after he spoke to AI executives at Dumfries House in Ayrshire last month on how the tech can be used to benefit security. King Charles met Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, at the event The meeting followed a series of recent warnings from people inside the industry about the rapidly evolving capabilities of advanced or "frontier" AI models and the regulation needed to keep them in check. "Those who have created these technologies are now increasingly warning that AI risks developing darker capacities - perhaps even to take life," the King told the executives. He said there seemed to be an "urgency" in "adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands, and being used in potentially catastrophic ways". "The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world," he told the group. title: Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue act
description: Heroics and battling performances have already become a theme of Arsenal's season with Bruno Guimaraes coming to the rescue again.
body: Bruno Guimaraes scored his second Premier League goal of the season against Leeds United. For the second time in three Premier League matches, Bruno Guimaraes has come to Arsenal's rescue. Having sparked their 2-0 win at Sunderland in September with the crucial first goal, the £75m summer signing came off the bench again to have a pivotal impact against Leeds on Saturday. This time it was the winner as the Gunners came from behind for a 2-1 success in a testing encounter at Emirates Stadium. But Ecuador international Piero Hincapie was carried off during the warm-down, raising concern the defender has suffered an injury. He came on as a late substitute against Daniel Farke's side but completed extra running after the final whistle - a practice most clubs use. A fifth win in six league games put Mikel Arteta's side level on points with leaders Manchester City, but their title defence has certainly not been without its scares so far. Following on from their comprehensive 3-0 defeat at Brighton last time out, Arsenal fell behind in a league match for a third time in four league matches - and only a David Raya penalty save stopped them from trailing at Sunderland as well. For large parts of the game against Leeds, they were nowhere near their best but, after going behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori and Guimaraes - on his full home debut - secured an important three points. "It was a great game of football. Leeds were brilliant for one hour." said Ally McCoist on TNT Sports. "Mikel Arteta made changes when he needed to and the substitutions gave Arsenal what they needed. That's what champions do. Leeds can hold their heads high." By getting wins when below par the mark of champions or are there reasons for concern for Arteta and Arsenal? This video can not be played Mikel Arteta post match interview - Arsenal vs Leeds United Coming into the season as defending champions, Arsenal were looking to make a statement signing to make their rivals take notice. They did not bring in the attacker they wanted but Guimaraes looks like he could be that key arrival to help Arteta's men build on their success. The 28-year-old midfielder is a 'win-now' signing in the peak years of his career. He responded well to a disappointing performance in the defeat by Brighton, where he made his full league debut. The Brazilian international has now scored two goals that have helped his side to valuable points and justified the decision to spend big on Guimaraes, even if the Gunners are inundated with top quality options in midfield. Arteta said: "He wasn't at that level against Brighton, and this is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action, you have to be at that level. "Today was much better. That's what we have to demand, and this is what I demand to myself. I'm going to demand the same with the players, because if we do that, he will raise the standards and we will be a better team." Guimaraes was the first player to score twice from the bench this season and both goals have been from outside the box. This video can not be played Guimaraes has 'perfect' day despite jet lag Arsenal won the league last season in part because of their excellent defence. The Gunners conceded the fewest goals in the league but have already conceded five in six games. The partnership of Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba is one of the best in the world and Arsenal look to be missing the injured Frenchman's calmness. Ezri Konsa was brought in from Aston Villa for £55m and, despite his quality, is still getting used to his new surroundings. It is unclear how serious Hincapie's injury is, although he was seen clutching his right ankle as he was carried off by goalkeeper Illan Meslier. He signed for the club on a permanent deal this summer, having initially joined on loan from Bayer Leverkusen last season. Hincapie has suffered from muscular issues this term and now faces an anxious wait to discover whether he requires another spell on the sidelines. Left-back Calafiori, though, has proved integral to Arsenal's attacking threat. His equaliser against Leeds was his first league strike this term but no defender has been involved in more Premier League goals than the Italian (one goal, two assists). "The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing." added Arteta. "And we need to be very conscious of that. From being exceptional and being the champions to being extremely average, like in that game, is a really thin line. "So if you don't want it more than the opponent, you are not able to cope emotionally with certain situations, you're going to suffer. "And we all suffered and we didn't enjoy that game, but then you have to learn the lesson and we certainly done that. "We speak about it and you could sense that there was something in those tummies." Arteta made some big calls when naming his starting XI. He opted to start with German Kai Havertz up front despite the forward returning early from international duty after picking up a hamstring issue, leaving Viktor Gyokeres on the bench again. Gyokeres had scored four goals, registering in every match for Sweden, in the last international break, but looks to have work to do to win his manager round. The 28-year-old has yet to start a Premier League game and in his cameos this season has looked far from the level required as a striker who could fire Arsenal to back-to-back titles. The forward line did not click against Leeds and, with Havertz looking like he lacked match sharpness, thoughts turned towards whether Arsenal missing out on an elite attacker in the summer would haunt them. Winger Christos Tzolis, who has shone at times this season following his summer arrival, suffered a hamstring issue with Greece and, with Eberechi Eze out of form, Arteta used Noni Madueke on the left wing. title: Nobel peace laureate says US sanctions on ICC 'unacceptable'
description: Navi Pillay says the Trump administrations' sweeping penalties on the international tribunal were "unheard of".
body: The South African former ICC judge was awarded the prize on Friday Navi Pillay, the winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize, has called US sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) "unheard of" and "unacceptable". The South African former ICC judge was awarded the prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", which paved the way for a "more comprehensive global legal order", the Nobel committee said. US President Donald Trump expressed his disatisfaction with the pick and hours later the US unveiled sweeping sanctions in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it described as a "rogue" institution. The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order. Pillay, speaking via video link during an event at the Nobel Peace Center in Oslo on Saturday, said: "There is so much tension and anxiety over the continued existence of international courts, mainly the International Criminal Court in The Hague. "Most importantly, sanctions have been announced by one country against the judges, just for the judicial orders they issue. This is unheard of, unacceptable." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier said the sanctions - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans. The US has already sanctioned 17 ICC judges and officials, but this move sanctions the court itself as an institution and is intended to inhibit its ability to operate financially. However, the US has provided a six-month grace period before some of these latest sanctions kick in, meaning member states can keep paying for its operations - a move Washington says is to allow countries time to negotiate a "solution to address" US concerns. The Trump administration claims that the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty. It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar". The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in saying they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions. This video can not be played Watch: Who is Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay? Pillay, 85, also served as UN rights chief, taking part in high-profile work considering allegations of human rights violations, including in Rwanda, Myanmar and Gaza. Her early work included defending anti-apartheid activists in South Africa, and on Friday she became the country's fifth Peace Prize winner - following in the footsteps of Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. "If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," she joked after receiving the prize, a reference to last year's winner, Venezuelan opposition figure María Corina Machado, deciding to gift her prize to the US president. Trump called the announcement of Pillay as 2026's winner "disgraceful and embarassing", and an "indelible stain on the country of Norway". He has long indicated he thought he should have been awarded the prestigious prize, and was nominated by several allies for it last year. title: Saudi capital airport hit again, sparking evacuations, reports say
description: The suspected attack comes a day after Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed two deadly attacks on the Riyadh airport.
body: The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war An international airport in the Saudi capital has been attacked again, reports say, just days after Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed two successful attacks on the hub. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was evacuated after a loud blast was heard on Saturday, two international news agencies have reported. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to Reuters, citing an eyewitness. Saudi authorities have not commented, while the airport told passengers to check with their airline before travelling there. The attack comes a day after authorities said three Saudi nationals, including a pilot, were killed in two attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October. They came during a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west. The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war. The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive. That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea. A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government. A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. But the informal truce began to unravel in July. The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport. title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
description: Polish police had already deployed to schools after a female caretaker was killed and several others injured in two earlier attacks in two days.
body: A woman has been arrested after injuring three people in the third knife attack recorded at schools in Poland this week. The 21-year-old used a "dangerous object" to attack a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital Warsaw, police have told news agencies PAP and AP. It comes a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which killed a female caretaker. A Warsaw police spokesperson said they could not confirm whether the latest incident was related to the two previous attacks. Authorities told local media that the 17-year-old injured on Saturday had been taken to hospital, but her condition is not life-threatening. Two other women aged 17 and 24, who had come to submit enrolment documents were also injured, the state news agency reported. Police told local media that the suspected attacker was a student at the school and initial findings suggest she did not know the three victims. Schools in Poland had been stepping up security following knife attacks at schools across the country on 7 and 8 October. Polish police said they had arrested 76 people after deploying to schools across the country. "When it comes to the safety of Polish children and peace in our schools, there is no room for compromise," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said ahead of the operation. Local media, citing a police spokesperson, reported authorities had information to suggest incidents this past week could be related to an internet challenge. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian. A day later, a 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in Leszczydół-Nowiny, north of Warsaw. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone". title: 'Serious incident' at tiger enclosure closes Yorkshire Wildlife Park
description: The attraction near Doncaster says emergency response procedures were "immediately activated".
body: Yorkshire Wildlife Park is closed for the remainder of the weekend, say management Emergency services are responding to a "serious incident" at the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, the visitor attraction has confirmed. In a statement posted on its website, its said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened". The park, near Doncaster, will remain closed for the remainder of the weekend, it added. The BBC has contacted the park, South Yorkshire Police and Yorkshire Ambulance Service for further details. The park said the safety and wellbeing of its visitors, staff and animals "remain our highest priority". title: Verstappen beats Ferraris to Singapore pole
description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen beats the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton to pole position in qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix.
body: Max Verstappen won the sprint race earlier on Saturday Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second pole position in a week by beating the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix. Verstappen's first lap in final qualifying was enough to take pole, his time fending off a second lap from Leclerc that was 0.054 seconds off pole. Hamilton was closest to Verstappen after the first runs but was unable to improve on his second run. In fact, most of the front runners struggled to improve on their second runs, as Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli took fourth on the grid, from McLaren's Lando Norris. Antonelli's team-mate George Russell was sixth fastest but will drop to the back of the grid with a penalty for using too many engine parts. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was the only driver in the top four teams other than Leclerc to improve on his second run but could do no better than qualify seventh. Alpine's Pierre Gasly and the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. Verstappen wins sprint after Russell crashes out Verstappen came to Singapore fresh from his and Red Bull's first victory of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and he has continued where he left off. The four-time champion has looked the man to beat all weekend, and took pole for the grand prix a few hours after winning the sprint, following Russell crashing out of the lead. Verstappen said: "This was the one I really wanted. The car has been really strong all weekend. "We have been on a really on a positive trend and it's really special to take the pole here." Leclerc felt pole had been on the cards if he had not made a few small mistakes on his final lap. He said: "Q1 and Q2 were really difficult. I had some weird struggles under braking. Q3, the lap was OK. I did some mistakes. I think there was a potential to be on pole today but Max just did a better job." Hamilton, second to Verstappen in the sprint, was quickest in the first and second parts of qualifying but could not repeat that pace when it mattered during what he described as "another difficult Q3". He added: "The car was feeling much better. I really felt she had more in her, pushing her through the laps and sessions. Q1 and Q2 were awesome, but got to Q3, snaps through (Turns) One and Three (on the first lap) put me down and rest of the lap was good, and then the second lap too many snaps. "I think there's a really fine line with our car whether you are over or under the sweet spot and I didn't get it quite right today." Hamilton said he had added a little more front wing for the final part of qualifying and he thought it had "just tipped it a little over the edge". title: Drone strike by Sudan paramilitary kills 41 near Ethiopian border, rights group says
description: Eight children are said to be among those killed by the strike, which hit a gathering of displaced people.
body: A drone attack by Sudan's paramilitary forces has killed 41 people in the country's Blue Nile region bordering Ethiopia, a rights group has said. The strike by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targeted a camp for displaced people in the state's Abu Shandi area on Friday, Emergency Lawyers said. The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said it was "appalled by horrifying reports". It said initial reports suggested most of the casualties were women and children. The Sudanese army and paramilitary forces including the RSF have been locked in a power struggle since 2023, a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands and displaced more than 14 million from their homes. It has also created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, with millions of people needing medical help. The army controls much of Sudan's central and eastern regions, while the RSF is headquartered in the western region of Darfur and also controls areas in the south. Both sides have been accused of using drone attacks. Ocha said in a statement that the area reportedly struck on Friday had been "under sustained atttack in recent weeks, displacing thousands of civilians and exposing many more to grave harm". title: Barlinnie visitors unable to use toilets as water supply problems continue
description: Some inmates at two halls first experienced problems on Thursday night and had no access to bottled water.
body: HMP Barlinnie in Glasgow is Scotland's largest prison Visitors to Barlinnie prison have been unable to use the toilets as work continues to resolve water supply issues at Scotland's largest jail. Some inmates at two halls in Barlinnie in Glasgow first experienced problems on Thursday night and had no access to bottled water. On Friday the Scottish Prison Service (SPS) said the issue was proving more difficult to fully resolve and staff would continue to support people affected. But the problems have continued into the weekend and one woman, who supports a prisoner, told BBC Scotland News that laundry was mounting up. She said: "The laundry hadn't been done since before Thursday so the prisoners don't have anything clean to change into. "They haven't been allowed showers either due to the water issue." A Scottish Prison Service spokesperson said: "We are continuing to work with Scottish Water to resolve the issues being experienced in HMP Barlinnie." Barlinnie prisoners face weekend without running water in cells BBC Scotland News also spoke to another woman outside the prison who had been in visiting. She said her loved one, a prisoner, had no water at all on Friday. The supply came on again last night only to go off again later. The woman said prisoners had been give two-litre bottles of water after initially being handed flavoured water. She said: "It is ridiculous. It really should not be happening in this day and age." The woman also criticised what she described as the "poor communication" with prisoners. She said: "The visits are still allowed to go on but you can't use the toilet or anything like that. "It is no use if you have got kids." The woman said prisoners often only saw their family for 45 minutes a week but were currently unable to shower in advance. She added: "They are already in really tough conditions in there because it is so overcrowded." The reality of life behind the bars of Scotland's infamous prison. The SPS said there were no prisoner requests for bottled water overnight on Friday but supplies were distributed. It is understood that the prison reported a drop in water pressure to Scottish Water at 16:00 on Thursday. BBC News was first contacted by a concerned relative about the water situation in Barlinnie at about 20:30 on Thursday. At the time, the SPS said there was a low water pressure problem which was being addressed, but that there was no issue with drinking water. One woman, who supports an affected prisoner, said that contingency measures should have been put in place immediately. She said: "Surely distributing bottled water to prisoners should be an immediate priority when the water supply fails? "These are not luxuries. They are the most basic necessities of life, and prisoners are entirely dependent on the Scottish Prison Service to provide them." Historic Environment Scotland last year said Barlinnie was of outstanding social historical interest The woman said that she and others had contacted Barlinnie to raise concerns. The SPS could not say how many prisoners had been affected but it is understood those in A and E halls had problems with their supplies. A Scottish Water spokesperson said: "We can confirm there are no issues affecting the Scottish Water network in the area. "The matter relates to an internal issue within HMP Barlinnie and we are supporting the Scottish Prison Service as it works to resolve it." Last year the late 19th Century and early 20th Century sections of the Glasgow prison were recognised by Historic Environment Scotland (HES) as a Category A-listed building. Construction of Barlinnie started in 1880 and the site opened in 1882. It was the first new prison built in Scotland following the nationalisation of the prison system, with the Prison Act of 1877. Barlinnie was known for being a notoriously tough prison, where prisoners carried out hard labour, breaking rocks from a local quarry. It also served as a home for capital punishment, with 10 men executed by hanging at the site between 1946 and 1960. In recent years the prison has been plagued by issues of overcrowding. The Scottish government has committed to building a new prison to replace Barlinnie and construction is under way. It is due to be completed in 2028 at a cost of nearly £1bn. title: Sara Sharif's grandfather granted guardianship of her siblings in Pakistan
description: All five children have been living with him in Pakistan since 2023, when 10-year-old Sara was murdered.
body: The siblings of Sara Sharif will stay in Pakistan with their grandfather Sara Sharif's paternal grandfather has been granted guardianship of her siblings by a court in Pakistan. The decision comes after years of legal limbo following the murder of 10-year-old Sara by her father and stepmother in 2023. All five children, who are now aged between 16 and four, have been living in Pakistan since 2023. They were asked to speak to the judge in court, where the eldest said they were comfortable and the siblings were settled. Sara's grandfather, Muhammed Sharif, told the BBC he was relieved to be granted guardianship after three years of legal battles, saying his hope is that the children "stay healthy" and receive "a good education". "It is my responsibility to ensure they get the best possible education and care," he said. When told by the judge that the grandfather would become their guardian, the eldest child responded saying "that's all good". The five children have been in Pakistan since August 2023, when they were brought to the country by Sara's father, stepmother and uncle after Sara was killed. The family was in hiding for weeks before the children were discovered by police at the grandfather's house. They were initially put into state childcare. The adults flew back to the UK and were arrested at the airport. Sara's father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool were found guilty of Sara's murder. Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison and Batool received a minimum of 33 years. Her uncle, Faisal Malik, was found guilty of causing or allowing her death and given a 16-year sentence. Sara had been hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in Woking, Surrey. Sara's father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool were jailed for life over her death In Pakistan, Sara's grandfather was given temporary custody of her siblings in October 2023. All but the youngest are now attending school in Pakistan, the grandfather has said. Speaking following Saturday's decision, their grandfather said "we will help them to return to a normal life". "Hardships can happen to any person at any time, at any place," he said, adding "we will move forward". Muhammed said that he speaks to his son Urfan once a week or every second week. "Not with the children, not regarding the case. Nothing else, just to ask about each other's well-being". When asked about allegations that he had helped hide the three adults, Muhammed said they had left soon after arriving in Jhelum and that at the time he had told them to return to the UK. The children's grandfather added that the siblings will keep their British passports and go back to the UK "when they reach the right age". The children were made wards of court in England, and Surrey County council had been trying to bring them back through the courts in Pakistan. Their grandfather has been fighting for them to stay with him. Surrey withdrew from the case in June, saying it had no ability to pursue the application in Pakistan, as English proceedings are coming to an end. A final decision on their guardianship had not been made in Pakistan's courts until Saturday. body: This video can not be played Protesters were heard slamming on bus windows following their detention during an anti-government demonstration called by The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The CJP shared a video on social media showing its founder Abhijeet Dipke being detained with other leaders shortly after landing in the capital. The movement started in May after India's Chief Justice likened some unemployed young people to "cockroaches". Delhi police denied permission for the demonstration to take place, with tens of thousands of security personnel deployed and roads barricaded. But the CJP had insisted it would go ahead. title: 'What this team has been crying out for' - Renshaw 190 lifts Australia
description: After nine years and 280 days, Matt Renshaw scores epic century to put Australia on top against South Africa and push his own case for a regular place.
body: Renshaw's century was his first in Tests for nine years and 280 days First Test, Durban (day two of five) Australia 390: Renshaw 190, Cummins 43; Mulder 4-68 South Africa 27-1: Markram 15*: Hazlewood 1-9 Matt Renshaw scored an epic first Test century in more than nine years to put Australia in control of the first Test in their highly anticipated series against South Africa. After much talk about the issues among their ageing top order on day one, Renshaw ground out a majestic career-best 190 from 397 balls in Durban, emphatically pushing his case to be part of Australia's future. The 30-year-old was born in Middlesbrough and was a childhood friend of England captain Joe Root - their fathers played together in English club cricket - before his parents left the UK for New Zealand and then Australia when he was seven. As well as potentially match-defining innings, having dragged Australia from 124-6 to 390 all out, it was a statement knock from Renshaw who has had an in-out international career. "I like him as a player," former Australia batter Simon Katich said on SEN Radio. "When he first came in, I liked him as a player, even though others thought he was too defensive. "I think that is what this team has needed and been crying out for." Renshaw showed impeccable patience and resilience, leaving or defending all of the deliveries shown above Renshaw scored 184 in his fourth Test against Pakistan in January 2017 after being handed a debut aged 20, but averaged 19.41 across 10 Tests before being recalled earlier this year. Against South Africa, the left-hander hit only three boundaries on day one - he attacked only 14.2% of deliveries in making his first 50 runs, the lowest figure of the Australia's top order. A throwback innings continued as he left well throughout day two, largely scoring square or behind the wicket. He extended his partnership with captain Pat Cummins in the morning session to 86 and then expertly controlled a stand of 134 with number 10 Nathan Lyon to frustrate and tire South Africa's bowlers. Renshaw took the strike when needed, protecting Lyon from the pace of Anrich Nortje, but became increasingly aggressive to add boundaries and inflict further pain as the partnership grew. He added a further 21 alongside number 11 Josh Hazlewood before falling in the first over after tea. Renshaw's superb innings, and opener Ryan Rickelton's three-ball duck in the 8.4 overs before bad light halted South Africa's reply, has left Australia well placed to push for victory on a pitch that flattened out on day two, but is expected to take turn later in the Test. This series has been eagerly anticipated, given it is a repeat of last year's World Test Championship final, which was won by the Proteas. It is also the third in a possible 21 Tests for Australia before the end of the Ashes next summer and, while Renshaw has surely secured his immediate future at least, his knock does not alleviate all questions over the make-up of their side. When he was recalled in August it was in place of Jake Weatherald as opener, but he was moved down to number five for this Test when Cameron Green was ruled out. Nic Maddinson came in at the top of the order alongside Travis Head, giving Australia an 11th different opening partnership since the retirement of David Warner. With Green, the regular number five, expected to return and Maddinson making a 33-ball duck on day one, a solution to their top-order struggles would be to move Renshaw up again. That would reunite him with Head, who made the surprise move to opener to impressive effect in the Ashes - he flogged England for centuries in Perth, Adelaide and Sydney - but has also shown vulnerability in failing to pass 22 in his four innings since. Equally, Renshaw could stay in the middle order and Green return for fellow-all-rounder Beau Webster, meaning Australia's hunt for a settled opening pair would continue. title: Hundreds protest over data centre plans
description: Placard-waving opponents highlight concerns about a data centre development on the local landscape.
body: Protestors carrying banners saying "no" to the data centre gathered in Caernarfon on Saturday Hundreds of people have taken part in a protest against plans to build a new data centre because of concerns about its effects on the area. Developers want to construct a complex on a 101 acre site between Caernarfon and Y Felinheli, in Gwynedd, saying it could create more than 900 jobs during construction and 200 permanent roles. About 300 gathered for a rally in Caernarfon to highlight their opposition. More than 22,500 have signed a petition opposing the plan. Canolfan Ddata Menai has previously said its proposals would "transform and revitalise the long-derelict" site as well as offer significant employment. But opponent Ernest Dyson, who lives near the proposed site, said it was "basically the destruction of the most beautiful part of the Menai Strait". "It is quite incredible it should come to this. "The people of the area are custodians of it. That's what we must think of," he said. Resident Ernest Dyson and MP Liz Saville Roberts attended the rally in Caernarfon Liz Saville Roberts, the Plaid Cymru MP for Dwyfor Meirionnydd, said: "We know that we need data centres but they have to be the right size, the right technology and in the right places. "We need proper regulations and we need to make sure that communities benefit from this. "We have too long a history in Wales of extractive industries that left nothing behind and have little benefit for communities. "That mustn't happen again in the 21st Century." Canolfan Ddata Menai said the project would ensure "continued use" of the surrounding area , including Lôn Las Menai cycleway and footpath, and would have "no undue impact" on the Menai Strait and an associated site of special scientific interest (SSSI).
