title: Tuchel's England 2.0: what has changed?
description: What has Thomas Tuchel tweaked as he looks to refine his England blueprint rather than rewrite it from scratch?
body: Thomas Tuchel has won 20 of his 26 games in charge of England After the World Cup, Thomas Tuchel was asked whether he had seen his vision of England during the tournament - a question that drew a hesitant and unsure answer. Over the summer, the Three Lions found ways to win but often leaned on scrappy moments of brilliance rather than methodical dominance. Tuchel had in mind the type of team, the tactics and the patterns he wanted to see. He and his assistant coach Anthony Barry have often spoken about borrowing ideas from the Premier League. Building up short. Enticing pressure. Playing quickly across the middle of the pitch – whether through powerful carrying or long balls – to find runners in attack against fewer defenders. These were all ideas England tried to execute, to varying levels of success, in the World Cup. During the recent international break, many of the ideas we saw during the World Cup and prior have persisted. There have, however, been deliberate changes in tactics and personnel, with the 53-year-old Tuchel looking to refine his blueprint rather than rewrite it from scratch. England have continued to focus on first playing short from the back, intent on drawing opponents towards them before speeding up play to find their attackers in space. Rather than giving the build-up responsibilities to two central defenders and a holding midfielder as they did during the World Cup, England have committed an extra player to this central build-up unit. Two central midfielders and two central defenders look to solve problems against pressing attackers with a shape that fluctuates between a 2-2 or a 3-1. Here we see England's 2-2 base with Guehi and Konsa behind Lewis-Skelly and Anderson. Hall advances into a higher position on the left. Seconds later Anderson pulls wide into a position normally taken up by a wide centre-back in a back three to create what looks like a 3-1 shape. Lewis-Skelly, on the ball in the middle, finds Anderson in space. Tuchel has praised Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who took turns with Myles Lewis-Skelly to pair with Elliot Anderson in the heart of midfield in Declan Rice's absence. Either player taking the role of busy partner for Anderson - boasting technical quality and an ability to take turns playing as a lone holding midfielder - have proved successful for England. Anderson, who sat at the base of midfield for much of the World Cup has, as a result, been deployed in a more varied role. With Scott or Lewis-Skelly picking up the ball from the centre-backs, Anderson has dropped to form part of the back three alongside Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa. This has given him time and space on the ball, facing forward, allowing him to use his forward passing to find attackers quickly. Anderson is a great progressive passer. From these wide areas, facing forward, he can give the ball to attackers looking for it. Here, Anthony Gordon drops deep with Morgan Rogers making a 'counter-movement' or run behind to the vacated space. Anderson has also found himself higher up the pitch on occasion, with the protection of his midfield partner behind him, allowing him to showcase his attacking quality. An interesting knock-on effect of this, and a nod to England's overarching evolution, has been the intensity England have shown as they have attacked. "We've always played with high energy and a very aggressive style off the ball, to press high," Tuchel explained. "Now we have added another layer. "[Now, our] intensity was very high on the ball. We did a lot of high intensity runs, a lot of counter movements, and invested a lot in counter pressing. Anderson's ability to counter-press is an individual example of this improvement but more collective changes have contributed to England's increased intensity in possession. In the World Cup, the system looked like a 4-3-3 on paper. The two centre-backs and holding midfielder formed a triangle. On both flanks, a central midfielder, full-back and winger formed a triangle. Harry Kane took a roaming role. These wide triangles were the main method of chance creation. Key to this was constant movement as England looked to make it hard for opponents to track them. Although this often got England's winger one-against-one, teams could match England man for man in the wide areas, especially as they fatigued and off-ball runs that rid them of their markers became less common. In the World Cup, England focused on attacking with wide triangles. The three players on the flank were tasked with creating chances which they did via good movement to lose markers. But teams were able to match up three against three. England's recent 3-1-3-3 shape in possession has given them an extra player at the back but appears to have also provided better attacking dynamics. The wide centre-back has contributed to attacking play out wide. England's full-back, winger and number ten work together and are often also joined by one of the strikers or holding midfielders. These five players have given England a numerical advantage on the flank. This has mainly been seen down England's left. By comparison, this international break has seen England far more willing to play in an asymmetrical fashion. Here, six players are playing closer to the left flank. Defensively, this provides them extra players around the ball, capable of counter-pressing with more intensity to win the ball back quickly. Offensively, this has given them an unmarked player or two that they have often found well. By overloading the left flank, England pull opponents towards one side which has also enabled them to switch it to the opposite side for team-mates in space – often two against two. Kane has dropped into a left-back position as England overload the left side of the pitch. This drags the Czech Republic's team over towards that side. title: Zelensky condemns 'vile' large-scale Russian attacks that killed 15
description: Rescue workers are continuing a search for residents after an apartment building in Pryluky was destroyed.
body: At least 15 people have died in overnight strikes across central and eastern Ukraine, in what Volodymyr Zelensky has described as one of Russia's "most vile" attacks. Ukraine's president said a residential building in Pryluky in the Chernihiv region was destroyed as a "birthday 'gift' to Putin", who turns 74 on Wednesday. Strikes also hit Kyiv, Dnipro, Kremenchuk, Zaporizhzhia and Oleksandriya. Zelensky said Ukraine had struck targets in attacks on Russia's Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions in the past 24 hours, adding there was "also a response in the Black Sea", without providing further details. Moscow is yet to comment on the latest strikes. "The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively," Zelensky said, adding that 70 missiles were fired in total. In the social media post on Wednesday morning, Zelensky said five people had been killed and 26, including five children, injured in a strike on a five-storey apartment building in Pryluky. He added that people could still be trapped in the rubble. Chernihiv Oblast police later reported that the death toll had risen to nine after the bodies of three children were recovered, with emergency workers continuing a search operation. Emergency workers were continuing to search for residents under the rubble of the apartment building in Pryluky on Wednesday morning Two people were also killed and eight injured after Russian missile strikes damaged five apartment buildings in Dnipro and four high-rise buildings in Kremenchuk, said Zelensky. Two people were also killed in the capital, Kyiv, and two others in Oleksandriya, he added. Ukraine's national police posted pictures online showing what it says is an unexploded Russian Iskander missile in the middle of a Kyiv district. BBC Verify has confirmed the images are genuine and the apparent missile fragments came down in an area of open land surrounded by high-rise apartment buildings. A video posted by the police shows people digging through collapsed remains of a residential building in Pryluky. Another verified video shows damage to cars and what appears to be rubble and a fallen tree in an area surrounded by apartment blocks in Kremenchuk. A photograph of fragments of what police said was an unexploded Russian Iskander missile in Kyiv Zelensky renewed a call for allies to provide air defence support packages to Ukraine, saying its military only managed to shoot down "some" of the missiles launched by Russia overnight. According to Zelensky, one of the "key targets" of the attack was the country's energy infrastructure, which Moscow earlier said it would intensify strikes on following Ukraine's strikes on Moscow's energy facilities. In a separate post on Wednesday, Zelensky said Ukraine had struck four targets in retaliatory attacks in the past 24 hours, including two oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions. "There is also a response in the Black Sea," the Ukrainian president wrote. On Tuesday evening, footage emerged showing a huge plume of smoke engulfing an oil tanker off the coast of Sochi, along the Black Sea in southern Russia. The Russian transport ministry later said unmanned boats had attacked the Liberian-flagged Aframax Rio oil tanker. Authorities claim the crew was rescued. Separately, Bulgaria has halted a search for the missing crew of a ship that sank after being hit by a drone on Tuesday, Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov from the Maritime Administration Executive Agency said, as reported by Bulgarian television network Nora TV. Tracking data shows the ship was anchored at the southern end of the Bosphorus strait until Monday when it entered the Black Sea heading north. Its last reported position on ship-tracking site MarineTraffic was at 23:43 GMT on Monday in what is known as the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone of the Black Sea. Bulgarian specialist news outlet Maritime.bg reported the Alfa Watan was attacked by a drone and sank 70nm (130km) east of Byala. As well as the civilian cargo ship, a second vessel - carrying grain - was also hit within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, its Prime Minister Rumen Radev said on Tuesday. The 18 crew members on the second vessel were rescued. Bulgaria has not said who it believes was behind the attacks. It comes as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea, particularly the eastern side, as part of its war against Ukraine. In an evening address on Tuesday, Zelensky claimed Russia was responsible for the attacks. Moscow has not commented on the latest incident. title: Arteta signs new contract with champions Arsenal
description: Mikel Arteta says this is "only the beginning" of Arsenal's success after signing a new contract with the Premier League champions until 2030.
body: This video can not be played Arteta signs new deal until 2030 Manager Mikel Arteta says this is "only the beginning" of Arsenal's success after signing a new contract with the Premier League champions until 2030. BBC Sport reported earlier this month that an agreement had been made on an improved new contract. The Spaniard's deal was set to expire at the end of this season, with his time in charge of the Gunners now possibly stretching to a decade following his arrival in December 2019. Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone is reportedly paid over £20m per year, as was former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola - both of whom Arteta benchmarked his worth against. The new contract includes an increase from his current salary of £10m per year plus an additional £5m in bonuses. "This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue," Arteta said. "We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together." The 44-year-old has won a Premier League and FA Cup in charge of Arsenal, losing the Champions League final against Paris St-Germain in May. Mikel Arteta was appointed Arsenal boss in December 2019 News of Arteta's new deal at Arsenal won't come as a shock. The fact his previous deal expired at the end of the season did put a slightly greater emphasis on the speed of discussions than normal. But Arteta has been transparent about his desire to stay at the club beyond the end of this campaign. Dynasty building is what has driven Arteta's decision. Winning Arsenal's first Premier League title in 20 years last season is viewed as just the start. Coming within a penalty kick of winning their first Champions League trophy came as a gut-wrenching blow - but also a huge motivation. "We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019," co-chairmen Stan and Josh Kroenke said. "He has a deep understanding of Arsenal's values and carries them in his heart. He knows what this club means to everyone connected to it and is committed to building on everything we have achieved together." With that in mind, there was never a sense Arteta was preparing to walk away from the team he has built to become one of the best in European football. So with a deal for their manager to stay now agreed, the foundation of Arsenal's recent revitalisation into a footballing force remains in place. Does more history beckon? Arteta is committed to finding out. Tuchel's England 2.0: what has changed? title: Man admits sexually assaulting woman drugged by husband
description: The husband is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in Greater Manchester.
body: Sean Peers has admitted sexually assaulting the woman while she was unconscious A man has pleaded guilty to sexually assaulting a woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband without her knowledge for more than 20 years. The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester. Sean Peers, 38, was due to stand trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court earlier but admitted one count of assault by penetration on 15 September 2024. The husband, who has already pleaded guilty to 60 offences against his wife, also admitted a fresh charge of rape and one of sexual assault. Both offences happened last summer. One of the men accused of joining in the abuse, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee in Scotland, has already pleaded guilty to various offences. There are a further 11 men due to stand trial who have denied abusing the same woman between 2018 to November 2025. Peers, from Stockport, was granted conditional bail until sentence, which will take place at the conclusion of the trial involving the other men. The husband, who is no longer part of the trial as a defendant, will also be sentenced at the conclusion of the case and has been remanded in custody. From left: Graham Brougham, Alan Keelan, Sean Peers, Jonathan Kirk and Jordan Wallace, along with seven others, will still be tried A jury was sworn in early in September but the case has faced a series of delays for legal and practical reasons. On Tuesday the nine women and three men of the jury, plus two female reserve jurors, were told that the husband had provided a witness statement detailing "what it is he says happened" after his guilty pleas. Judge Maurice Greene said: "That statement is a long statement and that has been disclosed to all defence counsel and it contains a lot of detail." The judge said the statement contained "lots of pages and lots of documents" and that lawyers in the case were "going through it carefully", which was ongoing work. The jury were asked to return on Monday 19 October when the prosecution case against the remaining 11 defendants has been scheduled to open. title: Xbox bets on Gears of War in battle of gaming giants
description: Unlike other flagship titles, E-Day will only be available on Xbox at a time of rising console costs.
body: Gears of War E-Day was expected to be available on multiple consoles but has been released as an Xbox exclusive Gears of War, one of the video games that helped Microsoft's Xbox to win over millions of fans, is back. Prequel E-Day takes players back to where it all started, telling the origin story of humanity's conflict with The Locust - the series' horrifying enemy species. The game's been well-received by critics and players, but it's also seen as a big test of Xbox's new direction. Unlike recent flagship titles from the company's studios, which have been released on PlayStation 5 and, in some cases, Nintendo Switch, E-Day is being pushed as an Xbox exclusive. The apparent goal is to draw players back to the brand, but critics have questioned whether that's realistic at a time when console prices are higher than ever. BBC Newsbeat spoke to developer The Coalition - the makers of E-Day - about what staying exclusive means to them. Gears of War has been one of Xbox's flagship series since it launched back in 2006. Creative director Matt Searcy tells Newsbeat the sci-fi shooter is a "mix of war story with comic book-y monsters that come out of the ground". "It's a video game with a lot of heart, a lot of blood and guts," he says. First released on the Xbox 360, Gears helped to popularise "cover-shooter" gameplay, which encouraged players to shelter from enemy attacks. It brought a strategic dimension to third-person action games, and also won fans with its co-operative multiplayer modes - a feature that's returned for E-Day. But, 20 years later, Xbox finds itself in a very different position in the console space. It's seen as a third-place competitor, behind both Sony's PlayStation and Nintendo's Switch consoles. Xbox prices soared over the summer due to the rising cost of memory chips Previous CEO Phil Spencer had begun to take the division in a new direction, releasing some of its most popular games on rival consoles for the first time. E-Day was widely expected to follow other high budget series such as Halo on to other companies' machines. But new Xbox boss Asha Sharma, who took over the job in June, announced Gears of War would remain a "console exclusive", although a PC version has also been released. Her strategy has been called into question by critics. After taking six years to make and an estimated budget in the hundreds of millions, they argue that keeping E-Day away from other platforms could mean it's less likely to make back its development cost. Coalition studio head Mike Crump says E-Day is a "natural choice to be an exclusive". "Gears has been an exclusive franchise to Xbox for 20 years now. It's sort of entwined deeply with the brand," he says. "And we're proud of that." He says the series "carries the banner" for the console and gives people a "reason to be in the Xbox ecosystem" - something he says has been the company's mission since day one. However, there will inevitably be discourse around E-Day's sales figures and engagement numbers. When asked what would constitute success for the game, Crump admits the studio has financial targets and goals for the number of players it wants to reach, but insists it takes a "broader view" than that. "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? "Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware." Crump also says it's important to drive players towards Game Pass, Xbox's Netflix-style subscription service. E-Day tells the origin story of humanity's conflict with The Locust For onlookers, it's harder to ignore the wider picture at Xbox. The division has been carrying out mass layoffs and undergoing a wide-scale restructuring since Sharma's appointment. In July, she told employees there would be 3,200 job losses across Xbox-owned studios over the current financial year. Last month, the company said it was about three-quarters of the way through this plan, external. The Coalition has mostly avoided cuts so far, although one of E-Day's narrative directors announced last month he had been let go. Reports have suggested developers at the studio are worried they could be at risk now the game has been released, external. When asked about this, Crump says: "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just we need to focus on the things that we can control. "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that." He says E-Day will provide a "great foundation" for future games in the series, and insists "the next game will not take nearly as long" to make. Developers at other studios hit by layoffs previously told the BBC they were concerned about a loss of institutional knowledge - experienced staff who've been working on certain series for years and sometimes decades. Crump says: "We've got a great team here. "And the leadership team in particular has worked together for upwards of 20 years. "So there's definitely a continuity of knowledge and experience." title: Noel Gallagher and Susan Sarandon among celebrities to sign Drumcree march letter
description: The letter, addressed to NI Secretary Sir Chris Bryant, calls on an international mediator to be appointed to find a resolution to the parade dispute.
body: Noel Gallagher, Susan Sarandon and Adrian Dunbar Oasis' Noel Gallagher, Oscar winner Susan Sarandon and Line of Duty star Adrian Dunbar are among dozens to sign a letter in support of residents in a stand-off over a decision to allow a parade down a predominantly nationalist road. There has been 11 days of deadlock between Garvaghy Road residents and the local Orange Order over the proposed march in Portadown, County Armagh. While peaceful, the stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland. Other people to have signed the letter include musician Paul Weller, Derry Girls star Siobhán McSweeney and The Smiths' Johnny Marr. The letter, addressed to Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant, calls on him to work with the Irish government to appoint an "independent international mediator" to "facilitate a robust, durable solution". It added that "central to any just resolution must be the primacy and protection of the local community". It also said it was "paramount that the residents be protected from any form of forced processions that disregard their consent, safety and right to live in peace free from intimidation". The Northern Ireland Office (NIO) declined to comment on the letter but it is understood the NIO has received it. Dexy's Midnight Runners frontman Kevin Rowland, who signed the letter, told BBC News NI that it "originated from an honest response to the situation on the Garvaghy Road". "The letter speaks for itself. It came about from conversations from those of us looking on from afar. "It was an organic process inspired by the courage of the residents. "As concerned individuals, we are not seeking to build an organisation or alternative platform to the voices of the residents. We would only wish to amplify their voices." Others among the 48 signatories include Trainspotting writer Irvine Welsh, movie director Ken Loach, Graham 'Suggs' McPherson from Madness, Kneecap, Imelda May, Maxine Peake and trade unionist Mick Lynch. There have also been letters to Sir Chris from members of the Protestant community concerning Garvaghy Road, external, a group of MPs, external and Members of Congress in the US, external. In a statement issued on Wednesday morning, the Orange Order said that the "lawful 35 continue to stand ready to exercise the legal right" they "have established for the first time in 28 years". "We once more urge the PSNI to actually take positive steps to implement the determination. We have seen no such proper efforts being made, and in due course, a court will also have to scrutinise this." "We will not give up that legal right, as to do so would be to legitimise mob rule. We will continue our dignified, peaceful and lawful stand." The statement added that they "remain open to dialogue in order to find a lasting resolution". "However, that must include the law being upheld and our legal rights being given effect." Orangemen turn away from a police barricade close to Drumcree Church formed to prevent them entering the Garvaghy Road on the eighth day of a stand-off There has been more than a week of deadlock in Portadown since the decision to allow an Orange Order march down the Garvaghy Road on Sunday, 27 September. That morning, up to 1,000 people - including politicians such as Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill - blocked the road, preventing Orangemen marching from Drumcree Church a mile to the west. Since then, residents have maintained a constant presence around the road while Orangemen have also repeatedly tried to march the route before being turned back by police. The stand-off has caused considerable political fallout in Northern Ireland, with First Minister O'Neill facing a vote of no confidence over her involvement in the protest. The vote is due to fail due to it requiring cross-community support at the Northern Ireland Assembly. Police are investigating the demonstrations in a "large-scale" criminal inquiry. Politicians such as Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill - blocked the road, preventing Orangemen marching from Drumcree Church to Garvaghy Road on 27 September Drumcree was one of Northern Ireland's most serious parading disputes, when stand-offs in the mid-to-late 1990s over attempts by the Orange Order to march along the Garvaghy Road were accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings. When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995, there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years. The Parades Commission began operating in 1998 to regulate parades and try to defuse tension around marches. Its decision not to allow a march down the Garvaghy Road that summer has been challenged by the order for the past three decades. Earlier this year the Parades Commission decided that the march could go ahead with restrictions in place after its original decision to stop the march was overturned in court. Meanwhile, the Court of Appeal is considering its ruling in a legal challenge brought by the residents to block the march going ahead. title: P&R's two-pronged budget approach under fire
description: Critics of P&R say it shows there is no commitment to making savings within the States.
body: P&R has put forward two budgets for deputies to decide on Politicians have expressed dismay at Policy and Resources' (P&R) budget for 2027, stating it does not do enough to support ordinary islanders. Deputy Adrian Gabriel said "I'm disappointed" as he hit out at plans to reduce tax caps and said he "would have liked to have seen their maximum liability, their cap, increase much more". Deputy Haley Camp said P&R's approach of presenting two budgets showed it had abandoned all spending discipline. P&R Treasury Lead Charles Parkinson said he never believed the direction to reduce spending by 1% in real terms - which deputies agreed to last year - was possible. Camp disagreed: "It is clear we're only moving in one trajectory which is let's just keep on spending money with abandon and at some point down the road someone else can fix it." Deputy Lee Van Katwyk said alongside Deputy Rob Curgenven he would be bringing a proposal to freeze fuel duty to "support struggling families". More news stories for Guernsey Listen to the latest news for Guernsey Former head of Start Up Guernsey, Deputy Jennifer Strachan questioned P&R's plans to introduce an entrepreneurs' tax cap to attract new business to the island, alongside the States' decision to close the Digital Greenhouse, a centre for digital and creative start-ups. "I think they're doing an easy thing, which is to say - here's a tax cap, come live here," she said. "I think the hard work is actually developing the ecosystem for entrepreneurs to thrive." Deputy Rob Curgenven warned last week's decision on tax reform would lead to higher government spending Deputy Rob Curgenven agreed: "We've got the windfall in for pillar two and obviously GST has been agreed in principle. "It just feels now that the cap is off and the spending spree is ready for Christmas." Parkinson warned that simply bringing a budget with the spending cuts would lead to "a flood of amendments". "We're only suggesting under the Option B budget half of what States committees have requested. "We're not spending like a drunken sailor." P&R has presented a budget which includes an inflationary increase in income tax allowances, lower taxes on a pint at the pub, a new £15m fund to encourage economic growth, £6m for initiatives to encourage States savings and the abolition of mortgage interest relief. Deputy Aidan Matthews, who has fought to defend mortgage interest relief as previous P&R's have looked to remove it, said he would be looking to reverse this move to remove it by 2029. He said: "I think that really the best thing that we should be doing is encouraging people to be able to afford to buy their own homes." Alongside the Committee for Housing, P&R said it was working on initiatives to support first-time buyers. Follow BBC Guernsey on X, external, Facebook, external and Instagram, external. title: Husband appears in court accused of GP's murder
description: Mark Cain is charged with the murder of Dr Hannah Terry, whose body was found at her home.
body: Dr Hannah Terry was found dead on Sunday The husband of a GP has appeared in court charged with her murder after she was found dead at home. The body of 45-year-old GP Dr Hannah Terry, also known as Hannah Cain, was found at a property in Fern Hill in Dersingham, Norfolk, on Sunday. Mark Cain, 45, also of Fern Hill, was charged with her murder on Tuesday. He appeared in a black sweatshirt at Norwich Magistrates' Court, where he spoke only to confirm his age, name and address. He was not asked to enter a plea and is due back in court on Thursday. Prosecutor Jacqui Hanlon told the court the ambulance service contacted the police at 02:25 BST on Sunday. She said Terry was "found in an upstairs bedroom not breathing, not conscious". She said a post-mortem examination "noted blunt force injury to the right side of her head had been inflicted, also an injury that could be suggestive of compression of the neck". District judge Matthew Bone remanded the defendant in custody to appear at King's Lynn Crown Court on Thursday. Mark Cain was remanded back into custody after his court appearance in Norwich Terry was listed as a member of the practice team at Grimston Medical Centre, which had closed on Monday and Tuesday, following her death. It reopened on Wednesday and said it would not be commenting "on the circumstances surrounding the tragic death of our colleague, Dr Hannah Terry". Dersingham village is part of the Royal Family's estate of Sandringham in west Norfolk. Do you have a story suggestion for Norfolk? Contact us below. title: 'Incredible relief' as court refuses serial rapist's sentence appeal
description: Christopher Malcolm raped, attacked and abused former partners, preventing one from attending her own father's funeral.
body: Serial rapist Christopher Malcolm appealed his 16-year jail sentence, but this has been refused A violent serial rapist who challenged his 16-year jail sentence for crimes against four women has had his appeal refused. Christopher Malcolm, 37, raped, attacked and abused former partners - preventing one from attending her own father's funeral - at locations in Moray and Lothian. A court heard he subjected the first woman to abuse when he was just 19 in 2008, and carried on "terrorising" others until his arrest in 2024. One woman recently told BBC Scotland that Malcolm left her permanently injured and disfigured when he stopped her from seeking medical treatment after fracturing her wrist and breaking her foot. Amy, not her real name, had been due to marry Malcolm, but police gathered enough evidence to arrest him four weeks before the ceremony. Following a trial involving 56 witnesses, a jury found Malcolm unanimously guilty of 12 charges. He was given a 16-year jail sentence in July, but lodged an appeal a month later. Amy said she and other survivors had felt highly anxious waiting on the appeal determination, but now felt "incredible relief". She told the BBC: "We've been waiting for this and have gone through so much over the summer and over the last two years. "We got to the end of the trial and it was like we got hit with another bombshell. But this makes us feel like people believe us and trust us." Amy was due to marry Christopher Malcolm, but he was arrested four weeks before the ceremony Malcolm, originally from Cockenzie in East Lothian, denied the crimes during his trial. A court heard he subjected his first victim to repeated sexual assaults and struck her head against a wall. He subjected a second woman to physical abuse at a flat in Forres, punching, choking and pushing her. Malcolm repeatedly raped another woman at locations in Danderhall and Haddington and subjected her to abusive and threatening behaviour. He also repeatedly raped another woman and subjected her to physical assaults. After Malcolm was sentenced, Amy gave a wide-ranging interview to the BBC, detailing how her former partner systematically introduced control into their relationship. She described how he insisted she come off social media, and moved her further away from family and friends. He would also turn up at her place of work, insist she leave early, and threatened to cause a scene. The violence he introduced into the relationship took several forms, progressing from an occasional outburst to every other weekend. Amy described how, on one occasion, Malcolm was in "attack mode" for three days, ripped up their sofa with a Stanley knife, and threatened suicide. Malcolm could be among the violent criminals who are automatically released early under recent Scottish government proposals - but for now, Amy says her faith in the justice system has been restored. For at least a year her life "revolved" around trying to recover from their relationship, and she says managing the impact on her mental health will be a lifelong undertaking. "I really struggled with sleeping afterwards, because a lot of things happened in the bedroom. I had to have sleeping tablets and counselling," she said. "I struggled with weight loss, I lost who I was, I lost my home. I don't dress the same, I don't look the same, the personality I had before I met him is completely gone. "I'm still hyper vigilant, I still look for him everywhere - I look for his car. I struggle with people being confrontational with me. "It's never going to go away." More stories from Edinburgh, Fife & East Issuing Malcolm's sentence, Judge Alison Stirling described the women who gave evidence against him as "courageous and articulate". She said he described himself as being a "control freak" and that he "minimised" his violence. Stirling highlighted that Malcolm had been assaulted when he was 15, during which his skull was fractured and he had a bleed on the brain. She said risk assessments showed he was "above average risk" of reoffending. Malcolm will be supervised by the authorities for three years following his release from custody. title: Gavin and Stacey creators Jones and Corden reveal celebrity cast of new show
description: Ruth Jones and James Corden's new show also stars X-Men's James McAvoy and Harry Potter's Jim Broadbent.
body: The Choir is Ruth Jones and James Corden's first project together since the Gavin and Stacey finale on Christmas Day 2024 Gavin and Stacey co-creators Ruth Jones and James Corden have revealed details about their new TV comedy drama series The Choir. The eight-episode show will air on Apple TV and feature guest appearances by Ted Lasso's Hannah Waddingham, X-Men's James McAvoy and Harry Potter's Jim Broadbent. The series follows brother Ben (Corden) and sister Lisa (Jones), who have not seen each other for several years. The pair previously said the idea came from their family connection to choirs, with Corden's mum and Jones' sister both members of one. Ben has been living abroad, while Lisa has continued living in their small town where "nothing ever happens". But when events take a sorry turn, Ben is forced to return to "a life he never wanted, a town he never liked and a family from which he's estranged". The cast includes Tom Davis, Rosie Sheehy, Susan Brown, Jason Watkins, Alexandira Riley, Sylvestra Le Touzel, Tom Edden, Gary Lamont, Emily Lloyd-Saini, Stephen Leask, Luiis Rouf, Jo Foster, Evie Jones and Farrah Abbassy. Jones and Corden are executive producers for the series, which is now in production and set to air in 2027. Jones previously said: "We both feel that choirs, amateur choirs especially, bring people together in a way that maybe nothing else does. "There was just this idea to bring this group of characters together from different backgrounds, all sorts of different things going on in their lives." Corden added they wanted "to try and make a show about community and the importance of community". "It's just about a group of people that come together every week and enjoy and sing, and it's really about the life that's within that," he added. Gavin and Stacey ran for three series, and three Christmas specials, between 2007 and 2024 When Jones and Corden first met in 2000, they never imagined it would lead to 22 episodes of a record-breaking TV show. The pair were filming Fat Friends at the Crowne Plaza in Leeds and formed an unexpected friendship. They then co-wrote Gavin and Stacey, in which they played Vanessa "Nessa" Jenkins and Neil "Smithy" Smith, the best friends of the title characters The hit comedy ran for three series, and three Christmas specials, between 2007 and 2024. Their memoir was published on 9 October - almost a year on from the show's record-breaking finale on Christmas Day 2024. Ruth Jones has been working on another comedy with Steve Speirs about two people who strike up an unlikely friendship Alongside their new collaboration, Jones recently appeared in new Netflix series Run Away - based on the Harlan Coben novel. She has also teamed up with Steve Speirs in a six-part comedy series called Better Later, about the challenges of relationships in middle age. Jones recently portrayed Mrs Bennet in another comedy series, The Other Bennet Sister, which was inspired by Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, while Corden has just finished a stint on Broadway. title: Russell to start from back of Singapore grid after penalty
description: Britain's George Russell will start from the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix because of a power-unit penalty from last weekend's race.
body: George Russell has three wins and eight podium finishes this season Britain's George Russell will start from the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver has received a power-unit penalty from a dramatic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last Sunday. The 28-year-old qualified in eighth but was heading for a podium finish before an engine failure forced him to retire from third place with five laps remaining. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed that Russell needs to take a new power unit this weekend, putting him over the limit on several components and meaning he will be penalised in Singapore. Russell's retirement last Sunday meant Kimi Antonelli, who finished second behind Max Verstappen, took a big leap towards his first Formula 1 world title as the Italian is now 84 points ahead of his Mercedes team-mate. There are six or seven races remaining, depending on whether F1 gets the security reassurances it needs for Qatar and Abu Dhabi, in the context of the war in the Middle East. "[Russell's penalty] is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for," said Wolff. "Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport and our focus now is on giving him the best possible car and opportunities to fight back through the field." The engine penalty is a particularly large blow for Russell as overtaking is notoriously difficult in Singapore. His title hopes are already effectively over with either six or seven races still o go, even if he still has a mathematical chance of catching Antonelli. But it means his chances of cutting the Italian’s lead are drastically reduced, even if Antonelli runs into trouble. Mercedes had no choice but to fit a new engine for Russell in Singapore because he had no usable engines remaining in his allocation. After early season reliability problems, they were all either broken or too high on mileage. Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix last month having taken a similar penalty, while this is the latest setback in a season of frustrating mechanical issues for Russell, who won last year's Singapore Grand Prix. Extra points are on offer this weekend as Singapore hosts the sixth and final sprint event of the season. Russell's penalty will apply to Sunday's Grand Prix and not the sprint race on Saturday. "We have spent the days since [last Sunday] working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been," Wolff added. "Singapore gives us an immediate opportunity to continue that work. "We need to keep learning and score the strongest result we can with both cars." title: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations
description: The 73-year-old has been arrested over allegations that a charity she is linked to misused donations.
body: Rajapaksa was arrested two days after returning to Sri Lanka from Singapore Sri Lanka's former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa has been arrested over allegations that a charity she is linked to misused donations raised for a children's hospital. Anti-corruption authorities arrested the 73-year-old wife of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa at their Colombo home on Wednesday. They are questioning her over the 10 million rupees ($30,300; £22,800) of donations collected by the Siriliya Saviya charity, meant to be spent on a specialised scanner for Colombo's Lady Ridgeway Children's Hospital. But officials say such a scanner had already been donated by the Chinese government. Shiranthi Rajapaksa has denied any wrongdoing and says the money has not been appropriated. She returned to Sri Lanka on Monday from Singapore, where she was receiving medical treatment. She had filed a court petition to try to prevent her arrest, but the hearing was set for 12 October. Ex-President Mahinda Rajapaksa's spokesperson, Manoj Gamage, has said the money is safe in Siriliya's accounts and that no fraud has occurred. Mahinda Rajapaksa served as president of Sri Lanka from 2005 to 2015 and for years, his family held a tight grip over the country's politics. He was hailed by many as a hero for bringing an end to nearly three decades of civil war when Tamil Tiger rebels were crushed in 2009, during his first term as president. But in 2022, protests broke out across the country as inflation surged and Sri Lanka ran out of fuel, food and medicine. Mahinda's brother Gotabaya Rajapaksa, who was serving as leader at that time, was eventually toppled. Sri Lanka's current government, under President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, has since revived long-stalled corruption investigations involving various members of the Rajapaksa family. Mahinda and Shiranthi's eldest son, Namal Rajapaksa, was arrested earlier this year over allegations linked to an aircraft procurement deal made during his father's presidency. He is currently held in remand. His brother Yoshitha was also arrested earlier this year on corruption charges. title: California pair charged with abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children
description: Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang were arrested at their Arcadia mansion after 21 children were removed from their custody last year.
body: Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang were arrested at their Arcadia mansion on Tuesday A California pair has been charged with multiple counts of abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children - some as young as two months old - and dissuading a witness. "The number of children who were subjected to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented," Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan J Hochman said in a statement. Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang, who US media describe as a couple, were arrested at their Arcadia mansion on Tuesday. The pair pleaded not guilty at a Pasadena courthouse, the BBC's US partner CBS News reported. Xuan, 66, and Zhang, 39, are accused of conspiring to subject 15 of the 16 children living in their home to repeated physical abuse, after 21 children were removed from their custody last year. The pair ran their own surrogacy company and are accused of making false statements to at least two women who became surrogates, indicating that Zhang was struggling to conceive, according to the criminal complaint. As of May 2025, Zhang maintained a spreadsheet that tracked 21 children, including those born to surrogates. Officials said the investigation began that month when Zhang brought a two-month-old boy to the hospital with a head injury, telling medical staff that the baby had fallen from a bed. The couple's lawyer Mitchell Krems said the allegation was a "mischaracterisation" based on the evidence he has reviewed, CBS News in Los Angeles reported. Hospital staff informed law enforcement, and when police arrived at their home they discovered three different rooms called "learning centres" under the supervision of multiple nannies, which Hochman described as a "house of horrors". The mansion allegedly had 32 motion-activated cameras which Hochman said were used by the couple to monitor the discipline given by the nannies. Footage allegedly shows the nannies spanking, slapping or hitting the children. One nanny, Chunmei Li, is accused of hitting the two-month-old baby who suffered the head injury two days before he was brought to the hospital. Krems said Li was quickly fired, CBS News LA reported. Li, 58, was previously charged with one felony count of child abuse under conditions likely to cause great bodily injury or death. Hochman said she was on the run with a $105,000 (£88,800) warrant for her arrest. In July 2025, the couple's home was first raided by authorities, who took 21 children into state custody. Arcadia Police Department said at the time the couple's house was first raided that the children ranged in age from two months to 13 years old, but most were between one and three years old. Fifteen of the children were taken from the couple's home while six others were living elsewhere and also later taken into custody. Krems said his client Xuan was innocent. "He is being targeted for exercising his constitutional right to have a large family," CBS News quoted the lawyer as saying. Investigators believe the surrogate mothers were from around the country and they were unaware they were carrying embryos for the couple at the same time. Melissa Brisman, the attorney for two of the surrogates, told CBS News: "This is wonderful news that people will be held responsible for their actions and there will be consequences if you abuse the surrogacy system". If convicted as charged, Xuan faces a possible maximum sentence of 17 years and four months in state prison, while Zhang faces up to 11 years and eight months. Li faces up to 12 years. title: The candidates hoping to be London's second Tory mayor
description: The Tory party has closed applications to be their candidate for mayor and there are four hopefuls.
body: Sir James Cleverly, who is among those running for London mayor, served as a government minister under several prime ministers "We need to treat London seriously" - the words of a leading Conservative MP as his party considers its next candidate to be mayor of the capital. The party has just closed applications for the role and there are four runners who have openly declared. In 26 years, the Tories have only had one mayor in the capital, Boris Johnson, who won two elections and served from 2008 to 2016. The party has lost three elections since then to Sadiq Khan, now Lord Khan of Tooting. Gareth Bacon MP, shadow minister for London, told a meeting at the Conservative Party conference in Birmingham this week that his party had treated the mayoralty like a "paper candidacy" in the past two elections - meaning that they hadn't taken it seriously enough. Bacon said that the party had "cut Susan Hall adrift", a reference to their candidate in the last mayoral election in 2024, when Lord Khan won that historic third term as mayor. Bacon went on to describe Lord Khan as "toxic and divisive". Boris Johnson was the first - and so far only - Tory mayor of London The election for mayor of London will be held in May 2028. That is more than 18 months away, but the race is well under way. Reform UK selected their candidate, Leila Cunningham, in January. Sarah Olney, MP for Richmond Park, and Rob Blackie, who ran in 2024, are both candidates for the Lib Dem nomination. This time round, with speculation about whether the current mayor will stand for a fourth term, the Conservatives sniff a chance. On the back of local elections in May 2026 when the party won back traditional strongholds like Westminster and Wandsworth from Labour, they feel the mood may be changing. However, winning the mayoralty may be too big a task. Much of it will depend on who they choose as their candidate. So who's in the running? As the putative front runner, Braintree MP and former home secretary and foreign secretary James Cleverly has been working the conference circuit very hard. Once a London Assembly member, and former head of the London Fire Authority, he is seen by many Tories as the 'shoe-in' candidate. But he will come with baggage - he is a Brexiteer and when he was head of London's Fire Authority oversaw a big cuts programme. He told me: "I hope to be a real champion for London, not just an administrator. I would make sure people are safe on the street and can really make a life for themselves and their families and can afford to live in London." Cleverly said party political affiliations "are less important than someone with a real plan to make London a city we can be proud of again". He added: "I hope to get the candidacy and then be a real champion for London, not just an administrator but a real champion and it's the city I love and that's why I want to put myself forward." Festus Akinbusoye is a former Bedfordshire police and crime commissioner Festus Akinbusoye is a relative newcomer to London politics, though not to the city. He emigrated from Nigeria with his parents and sister at age 13 in 1991 and lived in Canning Town in east London. Akinbusoye was the Bedfordshire police and crime commissioner from 2021 to 2024 and was elected to Westminster City Council in May. He told me: "We do not have to accept that this is the best we can get. "I believe that we don't have to accept that just because we're a global city, London has got to be so unaffordable to build a life in. "I want to be the most pro-policing, pro-house building, pro-business, pro-family, pro-growth mayor London has ever had. "We can make that happen because London works when Londoners work". Andrew Boff has been on the London Assembly since 2008 Andrew Boff is the current chair of the London Assembly. Privately, Conservatives joke that it wouldn't be a mayoral selection without him in it. He's been an assembly member since 2008. They also know he thinks very deeply about the capital's issues, particularly housing. Why put his name forward again? He told me: "I've got a very ambitious programme of not telling people how much I love London - because I'm hoping all the candidates love London - but specifically what I'm going to do. "One of the things we've got to do is help the family housing crisis, so I will make sure we get more money for building those important family-sized homes. "We need more encouragement for young people to do self-building in housing, so I'll be making land available for young people to build their own homes without having to pay for the cost of the land." Boff added: "I'll get rid of the outward extension of the Ulez." Alex Challoner said he has made his home in London for more than 30 years Public affairs professional Alex Challoner told me he came to London from the West Country when he was 21 and has called the city his home for 35 years. He said: "I think as a party, we have a choice between winning and losing for a fourth consecutive time. "If we're serious about winning we have to have some of the boldest policies that will appeal to Londoners. "I'm proposing a crackdown on fair dodgers at the Tube barriers by introducing British Transport Police, as well as training up Transport for London staff to stop people breaking through the barriers." He told me his plan, called Fare Watch, would use a "simple reporting tool in the TfL Go app and online" where passengers will be able to report persistent fare dodging. Challoner also pledged to introduce "a London Plan that you can read in an afternoon" as well as VAT cut "for gyms and London breweries". The hopefuls in the race to be the Conservative mayoral candidate will have to wait until November to find out if they've made the final shortlist. title: Stephen King's Carrie returns to explore the horrors of social media
description: Another beloved classic gets a modern-day twist. Its cast and creator argue why it needed to be remade.
body: Summer H Howell plays Carrie in the new adaptation of the Stephen King novel Adaptations, remakes and reboots are all the rage right now, and there’s often one question that crops up - why? See also "what's the point?" and "do we need another one?" whenever a story is resurrected from the past. Carrie, Prime Video's new TV series based on Stephen King's debut novel, has been no exception. It's not the first time the tale of high school bullies and supernatural powers has been adapted for the screen. Director Brian de Palma's 1976 movie version is a horror classic, with some of its most famous scenes and imagery widely considered iconic within the genre. But the cast and creator of the latest version, which drags Carrie's story forward 50 years into a world of social media, have been telling BBC Newsbeat why they believe it's still relevant in 2026. Fans of the novel have been quick to complain the new version of Carrie is not "book accurate", pointing out that she was originally an abrasive, even unlikeable character. In the TV adaptation, Carrie has been raised behind closed doors by her paranoid father and deeply religious mother, and only enters school after a tragedy reveals her existence to authorities. Audiences see a different version of the character in the show - one who's naive, but open and eager to learn new things. "There's a lot of opinions, and I purposely avoided the original movie and and the book before filming because I hadn't seen it or read it," Summer H Howell, who plays Carrie, tells Newsbeat. "And I wanted to create this new, light version of Carrie that was excited to get out of her house and just curious about the world and people." However, the 22-year-old actress says the journey her character goes on is not so different, and argues it's still relevant today. "It's the story of an outsider, and bullying has not gone away in 50 years," she says. "If anything, it's just gotten worse with social media." Chris Hargensen (played by Alison Thornton, left) and Sue Snell (Siena Agudong, right), are among the first people Carrie meets when she starts school Social media plays a huge part in the adaptation by horror director Mike Flanagan, who's best known for series such as The Haunting of Hill House. In his version of Carrie, some of the most famous scenes, including the dramatic prom moment, are adapted to a world where everything is filmed and shared online. Alison Thornton, who plays chief bully Chris Hargensen, says social media "is kind of a villain in the show". "You can post something, or someone will take a video of something, and the fact that it can be permanently online is actually quite terrifying," she says. Thornton says the adaptation aims to show how online posts can have "repercussions in real life". Showrunner Flanagan tells Newsbeat it would have been "impossible to ignore the impact social media has had in changing the way we see each other". Fifty years ago, he says, bullying would have been relatively "private", and confined to "the classroom, in the halls, in the school". But that's all changed, says Flanagan. "It's happening with the audience of the entire digital world and enshrined forever, permanently on these platforms. "It's a whole different ball game that way," he says. Mike Flanagan's been behind several acclaimed horror adaptations, including The Haunting of Hill House Carrie is the latest project from Prime Video targeted at Gen Z viewers based on a popular novel. The Summer I Turned Pretty, Your Fault: London, and Off Campus have been huge hits for the streamer, and it's leaned into trends such as BookTok to generate interest in the shows. Josie Totah, who plays Chris's sidekick Tina, agrees remakes and adaptations are popular, but says she would only get involved with one if the "intention" felt right. "No one wants to just remake something for the sake of remaking it," she says. "'Why now?' - unless that can be answered thoroughly, I don't think that I would want to do it." There are worries from fans that revisiting existing works leaves less space for original stories. Totah says projects such as this year's indie horror hit Obsession also deserve to be championed. "Those are equally as important as the ones that we've already told in the past, if not maybe a little bit more," she says. Tina (Josie Totah) is part of the group that torments Carrie So far, Flanagan's version of Carrie has had a mostly positive response from critics, with an 85% positive rating on review website Rotten Tomatoes. Most praised the performances and social commentary, although some reviewers felt it wasn't as scary as earlier versions and accused it of sanding down some of the original characters' harder edges. The verdict from fans remains to be seen. Flanagan hasn't just expanded on the original story, but has also made some fairly major changes, possibly laying the ground for further series to be made. "I try to think about how fans will feel because I'm a Stephen King fan first," he says. "So I have very strong opinions about changes that are made in adaptation." Flanagan has brought other Stephen King novels to the screen before, but those have tended to be much more faithful to the source material. Some of his best-known projects, reinventions of The Haunting of Hill House by author Shirley Jackson and The Fall of the House of Usher by Edgar Allan Poe, have been based on works by long-deceased authors. "I've just never done this with an author who's still alive or one with whom I already have a very intensely productive working relationship," he says. "I hope people are going to look at these changes and say: 'Oh, this is actually why it makes good sense to tell this story again today'." Carrie will launch on Prime Video on 7 October Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 week

title: Why you could represent GB in one of newest Olympic sports
description: The Los Angeles Olympics are just two years away but you could get there with a new sport as Great Britain's flag football team is on the lookout for new talent.
body: Canada-based Angelica Tait is a recent recruit to the Great Britain team British sprinter Amy Hunt knows all about the "magic of the Olympics". Now Olympic hopefuls have another avenue to join the 2024 medallist at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. Flag football, a condensed, non-contact version of American football, is one of the world's fastest growing sports and will make its Olympic debut at LA28. Great Britain hope to qualify and in a bid to boost their chances, they are looking to identify male and female athletes from other sports who have the potential to convert. Cross-sport athletes are also being considered for a new professional flag football league, backed by the NFL and the likes of Tiger Woods and Serena Williams. "Everyone wants to go to the Olympics so I can see why people are moving sport to get there," Hunt told BBC Sport at Sunday's NFL game in London. "[LA28] is two years away so this is your last chance to really get sorted with a new sport and find your way in. "I would really encourage it because the Olympics is unlike anything else, and flag football's going to have a massive profile at LA." The GB women's team is already one of the best in the world. They won the European Championships in 2023 and 2025 and went into this summer's World Championships ranked third. The USA qualify for LA28 as hosts but two other Olympic spots were available at the Worlds and GB narrowly missed out, losing 20-19 to Mexico in the bronze-medal game. Grace Conway is a long-term member of the GB team. She used to play netball but was introduced to flag football at school when she was 14 and ended up choosing to focus on flag. Netball is not an Olympic sport but now Conway, 27, has the chance to become an Olympian through flag football. "I think it's every athlete's dream to play their sport at the highest level, and what's higher than the Olympics?" asked Conway. "We never thought [flag football becoming an Olympic sport] could be possible. I remember looking up other sports and whether I could transfer, so when the announcement came it was amazing. Now I hope that we can get there." This video can not be played Do you have what it takes to make an Olympic team? Flag football is now played by 20 million people in more than 100 countries and the rapid growth of the women's game was key to it becoming one of five optional sports for LA28. The sport has been backed heavily by the NFL, which aims to help it earn selection for Brisbane 2032 too. The decision is due before the end of 2026 so flag football could head into its Olympic debut knowing it will feature in back-to-back Games. Participation has boomed in Australia and scores of athletes are switching from Australian rules football, netball and rugby, while the American team has recruited basketball players. GB's Brittany Botterill (football/softball), Phoebe Schecter (equestrian), Marta Mathews (football), Jochebed Frimpong (athletics), Jess Allen (badminton) and Angelica Tait (athletics/snowboarding) all competed in other sports before playing flag football. US-born Emily Kemp even became an ultimate frisbee world champion last year, in the same summer she helped GB win the flag Euros. "We are an elite team already, we're a potential medal threat at LA28, but we're really aspirational so we're looking to widen our talent pool," said Chad Ehlertsen, chief executive of the British American Football Association (Bafa). "If you look at the top flag players around the world, they've generally come from certain sports. They have good hand-eye coordination, agility, speed, decision-making under pressure. These are the qualities we're looking for. "In many ways we're not looking for elite flag players, we're looking for elite athletes that have the potential [to transfer] and then our coaches will help them understand the game." Grace Conway works as a recruitment consultant but could soon become a pro flag football player The NFL announced in March that it would launch a professional flag football league for women and men, in partnership with TMRW Sports. Pronounced 'tomorrow', the company was co-founded by Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods and its first major venture was the TGL (TMRW golf league). Investors in the new league include NFL legends Tom Brady and Joe Montana, plus Billie Jean King, Serena Williams and Alex Morgan. The league's first season could begin next summer and its first 'talent qualifier' was held at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Tuesday, with GB players among the 57 international hopefuls showcasing their skills. "We're casting a wide net," said Champ Kelly, TMRW's senior vice president of flag football operations. "We want flag football's elite, and we want the cross-sport athlete who doesn't even know yet that flag is their sport." Some of those selected will feature in a Pro Flag Showcase during Super Bowl week in February while an increasing number of flag football scholarships are being made available at US colleges. "We're a part of history," added Australia's Kodie Fuller. "We couldn't ever have imagined this but every day there's something new happening in flag football that blows my mind." GB's Emily Kemp was the Most Valuable Player at the 2025 Euros and was invited to TMRW's first 'talent qualifier' GB are starting their next training cycle building up to the 2027 European Championships, before the final LA28 spots are available in June 2028. The women's programme is holding trials at Loughborough College this Saturday and Sunday, where athletes will be assessed across a range of performance pillars. About 70 people have already registered and current GB player Conway welcomes the competition. "That's top-level sport, you're always fighting for your spot," she said. title: Ex-Welsh Green Party deputy says Zionism motion 'pointless' after quitting party
description: Phil Davies told BBC Wales the motion would not improve the lives of the Palestinian people.
body: Phil Davies was a youth activist and campaigner when he was chosen to be the Greens' deputy leader in Wales in 2024 The Green Party's former deputy leader in Wales says he resigned over the motion to declare 'Zionism is racism' because it was "pointless" and some of the statements made were "disgraceful". Phil Davies had been a Greens member for seven years, but had announced on social media on Tuesday his decision to quit the party had been "accelerated" by the motion over the weekend. In the post he had described the motion as "imperialistic" and "idiotic", and that it "doesn't materially achieve anything in the real world". Speaking to BBC Radio Wales Breakfast on Wednesday, Davies said he "doesn't know why it was discussed as it doesn't do anything to materially improve people's lives in Palestine". What is Zionism? A very brief history He said Welsh Greens leader Anthony Slaughter had been supportive of his decision to quit, and also said he hoped Welsh party members would vote to split from those in England at a conference next month. The motion, which was passed on Sunday to become party policy, called for a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel. In response, Israel banned Green leader Zack Polanski from entering the country, while Jewish groups described it as an "attack" on their community and some Labour and Liberal Democrat MPs reported the party to Great Britain's equality watchdog. Welsh first minister says Green Party Zionist motion was ill-judged Green member behind Zionism motion named as 'close friend' of jailed al-Qaeda supporter in court Davies said it was "not the sort of politics" he wanted to be associated with, and that Green Party Wales leader Slaughter had been supportive of his decision to leave the party. He said: "Our views are exactly the same to be honest with you. "He sent me a very nice message yesterday as well. I class Anthony as a close friend and that will remain." When asked on whether Slaughter would follow him in quitting the party, Davies said he did not agree with any elected official resigning and staying in the Senedd. "You weren't voted in as an individual member under this system. You're voted in under your party banner," he added. He suggested that Welsh members of the party should consider splitting from the Green Party of England and Wales (GPEW) to "stand on our own two feet as a Welsh party" in light of the motion. Davies said he was "hoping they'll vote to leave" at their party conference next month. In an Instagram post, Davies said he had not been treated with respect or been "given enough support from the GPEW". He added: "I have often felt like the token Welshman moaning at various points, but have not seen enough action taken by GPEW. "I also feel the position of Wales deputy leaders is ignored rather than supported by GPEW." Anthony Slaughter, who revealed he had been diagnosed with cancer last month, said his former colleague had brought a "much needed new perspective to Welsh politics." He said: "I am positive he will contribute a great deal to Welsh public life whatever his next steps are. "While the recent motion is not the only reason for Phil's resignation, I know it has stirred emotions across our party as people express their positions on this issue." First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth said on Tuesday that the Green Party policy was "ill-judged", saying that he had always advocated the two-state solution. He had been responding to Reform Wales leader Helen Jenner, who had accused "left-wing parties" of having a "sickening antisemitism problem". Speaking in the Senedd on Tuesday, ap Iorwerth said he always advocated the two-state solution and stood "shoulder to shoulder with the Jewish communities in Wales". title: New global guidelines warn against obesity drugs for children under 10
description: Care should focus on healthy eating and exercise, not medicines such as weight-loss injections, says the World Health Organization
body: Children under 10 should not be given obesity drugs or GLP-1 weight-loss injections such as Mounjaro and Wegovy, new global guidelines, external from the World Health Organization say. Most of these medications are only licensed for children or adolescents older than this, but some doctors prescribe them off-label, and drug companies are testing them in children as young as six. WHO says the care should focus on healthy eating and exercise, not medicine or surgery, although they do not oppose drug trials. Some digital technology, such as activity trackers and any online games that encourage the player to be more active and move, might be useful, it says, based on the limited evidence available. Estimates suggest 170 million children and adolescents worldwide are obese. That includes 70 million children aged 5–9. Obesity prevalence in this age group has quadrupled since 1990, rising from 2% to 8%. In 2024, 35 million children under the age of five were overweight. Obesity increases the risk of many different diseases, including type 2 diabetes. Dr Luz De Rigil, Director of Nutrition and Food Safety at WHO, said: "For children under 10, WHO does not recommend obesity medicines, bariatric surgery or weight-management devices. This is a strong recommendation." These might be appropriate for older children and adolescents when lifestyle approaches have failed and if the individual is "mentally and physically prepared" for the treatment, she added. She said WHO recognises this is an evolving field and will continue to evaluate the evidence. WHO's head of Nutrition and Food Safety Actions, Laurence Grummer-Strawn, said: "We are particularly concerned in this age group, if you are starting children very early on to using a GLP-1 or drugs like this, when does that stop? "We don't really have evidence that you can use this as a temporary treatment and then turn to something dietary later on in life. "We are very cautious about jumping in without clear evidence," he said. title: Pidcock angry after team-mates hit by police vehicle
description: Tom Pidcock wanted to "stop racing" after he says two of his team-mates were hit by a police vehicle travelling the wrong way down the course at the Tre Valli Varesine.
body: Tom Pidcock finished the race second to Belgium's Jarno Widar Tom Pidcock wanted to "stop racing" after saying that two of his team-mates were hit by a police vehicle travelling the wrong way down the course at the Tre Valli Varesine in Italy. Pidcock finished second at the one-day race in Varese but was left "mad" after Pinarello-Q36.5 team-mates Marcel Camprubi and Thomas Gloag were knocked off their bikes with six laps of the finishing circuit to go. Spain's Camprubi was able to continue in the race but Pidcock's fellow Briton Gloag stopped and required stitches on his knee. "First of all, I wanted to stop the race, stop racing myself," Pidcock told Eurosport after the race, which was won by Belgium's Jarno Widar in a sprint finish. "I was mad. I had guys all riding in front of me, for me, and then two of them are on the floor. "This shouldn't happen. But we continued and got back into the race and I'm happy that I could be on the podium." BBC Sport has contacted race organisers and local police for comment. In August, two-time Olympic mountain bike champion Pidcock won his second cross-country world title at the Mountain Bike World Championships. He dedicated that win to British cyclist Finlay Tarling, 19, who died on 14 August during the Volta a Portugal following a high-speed collision with a van that had strayed on to the closed road. Camprubi posted a picture of a broken bike on Instagram Stories, with a caption that read: "Sad that you have to risk your life to race, one month after a tragic accident." title: Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102
description: She starred opposite Marlon Brando in On the Waterfront, then alongside Cary Grant in Hitchcock's North by Northwest.
body: Eve Marie Saint has two stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar-winning actress who starred in Hollywood classics such as On the Waterfront and North by Northwest, has died aged 102. Saint won the Academy Award for best supporting actress for her movie debut in director Elia Kazan's 1954 crime thriller On the Waterfront, playing Edie Doyle, the love interest of Marlon Brando's conflicted ex-boxing docker. Five years later, she portrayed femme fatale Eve Kendall, dangerously seducing Cary Grant in Alfred Hitchcock's action thriller North by Northwest. She died on Tuesday of natural causes, surrounded by family and loved ones at her home in Los Angeles, family representative Jeff Sanderson confirmed. The star pictured in around 1960 Until her death, Saint was the oldest surviving Oscar winner and one of the last remaining stars of Hollywood's golden age. She also won an Emmy in 1990 for her role as a rich widow in the acclaimed TV miniseries People Like Us. Saint alongside Marlon Brando in On the Waterfront Born in Newark, New Jersey in 1924, Saint had originally intended to become a teacher before developing a passion for theatre. She trained in New York at the Herbert Berghof Studio and then the Actors Studio - the home of method acting - co-founded by Kazan. Saint burst on to the Hollywood scene with her performance in Kazan's classic, On the Waterfront. Brando was known as an intense method actor and Saint admitted to having found him "adorable" but "a little frightening". "I felt that he could see right through me," she told Turner Classic Movies (TCM) in a 2013 interview. The actress opposite Cary Grant in North by Northwest (above and below) She was considered a surprise choice, though, to play one of "Hitchcock's blondes", as they were known at the time, in his masterpiece North by Northwest. Her co-star Grant was known for being very demanding of his leading ladies. "He worked with me from the outside in," said Saint. "My hair, my makeup, my shoes, my jewellery, my purse, my gloves, everything. And just from creating that exterior for me, he gave me the sense of a spy lady." Saint also starred opposite Paul Newman in Otto Preminger's Exodus in 1960, and she was Warren Beatty's love interest in John Frankenheimer's All Fall Down. But she then stepped away from the limelight to raise a family with director Jeffrey Hayden. Eva Marie Saint (centre) pictured with co-stars for the 2006 premiere of Superman Returns in California Half a century later, Saint - by then in her early 80s - made a big screen comeback as Superman's adoptive mother in the 2006 blockbuster Superman Returns. And she later had parts in the supernatural fantasy Winter's Tale, alongside Colin Farrell and Russell Crowe, and another in the 2019 nun drama Mariette in Ecstasy. Saint, who has two stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, said her longevity in acting had given her work extra depth. "The longer you live, the smarter you get, because you've been around, you've seen things," she told TCM. "You've gone through different emotional experiences in your own life, and hopefully, you understand things better. "And that makes you a better actress." Saint's marriage to Hayden lasted for 65 years, until his death in 2016, and she is survived by their two children.
