title: Tens of thousands of fridge freezers left at docks as household collections suspended
description: A recycling firm collapsed in 2025, leaving the appliances in limbo until a takeover is complete.
body: The closure of the Newport site is thought to have taken away about 30% of the fridge recycling capacity in the UK People have reported storing broken fridges and freezers in their gardens for months because some council collections have been suspended. It follows the closure of specialist treatment facilities and a wider shortage of capacity to process cooling appliances, the Local Government Authority (LGA) said. Recycling company Unimetals, which had dozens of sites in the UK, filed for liquidation in 2025 leaving tens of thousands of fridge freezers at Newport Docks. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it was working to manage the capacity shortages. Almost a quarter of Welsh councils say they have suspended household collections of fridge-freezers due to a shortage of space at disposal sites. Cardiff is one of these and Lee Young, who lives in the city, has been trying to get rid of his broken fridge-freezer for two months. "I tried to take it to the recycling centre in July but was told it wasn't accepted. Someone said the council would collect it, but they won't either." It has been sitting in his back garden ever since and he does not know when council collections will resume. Lee Young has repurposed his old fridge freezer for plant storage overnight until he can get rid of it Lee said he was also confused by the different policies in neighbouring councils. "If I lived in Barry or Penarth (Vale of Glamorgan) they would be able to collect it from the kerb. I don't know why I can't in Cardiff." The Welsh Local Government Association has been asked why some councils are still able to carry out the collections while others are not. Michael Enea, a campaigner in Newport who blogs about fly-tipping, said he often saw the old appliances at the side of the road and thinks this could now get worse. "I think there'll be a lot of people in local communities where they don't have the ability to dispose of their fridges and freezers, who will end up literally dumping them in the street. "We see it quite a lot in Newport and right over Wales." Michael Enea has seen fridge freezers fly-tipped around Newport in recent months The LGA said it had identified dozens of councils across Wales and England that had been forced to stop or restrict collections, with more expected to follow suit. Oxfordshire County Council has urged the UK government to reopen the Newport plant to help with the "crisis". Associated British Ports, which took over the running of the Newport site, said it was "in discussions with third parties" about the future of the site and materials. A spokesperson added: "In the interim, the material is being managed responsibly as part of the site's transition and will be transferred to another specialist recycling operation in due course." APB said appliances will be transferred to another specialist recycling operation in due course Dr David Santillo, a research scientist at Greenpeace, said it was possible that some of the fridges and freezers at Newport Docks still contained "some of the most harmful chemicals" such as hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs). HFCs are mainly used in air conditioning, industrial chillers and fridges, but are also powerful greenhouse gases. Chemicals such as isobutane, pentane and ammonia can also be found in commercial-type fridges, Dr Santillo added. "None of these chemicals are benign. They all have the potential for harmful effects, or they can be toxic if they leak," he said. Santillo said some older chemicals could have a "much wider impact" on the environment and leaving appliances out for long periods had the potential to produce "toxic smoke" if a fire breaks out. Dr David Santillo has urged the UK government to improve the recycling capacity for appliances Santillo said the recycling of fridges and freezers was a national issue and he urged the UK government to "step in and find a solution". Defra said it appreciated the "challenges" facing local authorities, and was working to manage the impact of treatment capacity shortages. It added: "This includes allowing the storage of fridge and cooling equipment on temporary sites provided certain conditions set out by the Environment Agency are met." Regulator Natural Resources Wales said it was "aware of the pressures" affecting operators across the UK. It added that it was providing "regulatory flexibility" to help manage temporary storage pressures and would "continue to support efforts across the sector to restore treatment capacity and minimise disruption". The Welsh government said it was working with NRW, local authorities and the UK government to "manage the situation and support a return to normal capacity." title: Matthew Rhys' sister 'so proud of him' after historic Emmy wins
description: Rhys, from Cardiff, became the first person to win two lead acting Emmy prizes in one night.
body: Matthew Rhys's sister Rachel was there with him at the Emmy Awards for his historic double win The sister of Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys said her family had been "pinching ourselves all week" following his historic Emmy success. Rhys became the first person to win two lead acting Emmy prizes in one night, after he was named best lead actor in a limited series for the psychological thriller The Beast In Me, and best lead actor in a comedy for his role in Widow's Bay. His older sister Rachel Evans, who accompanied Rhys to the ceremony in Los Angeles, said she was starstruck seeing Hollywood royalty at the event, and revealed that she and her brother called their parents afterwards, who were sat at home in their dressing gowns. "I think we just all giggled for a long time." Rhys, who grew up in Cardiff, made history at the Emmy Awards, becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night Speaking to Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales, Evans said watching Rhys win the awards was "an experience I will never ever forget or probably match". She said that as the "bossy" older sister, she told him that morning that he needed to prepare, adding: "If you win, you cannot wing it." "We're so proud of him," she said. She also recalled the emotional moment when he thanked her during one of his acceptance speeches, calling her "the brains of the outfit". Rachel and Matthew as children Evans described the moment he won as "insane". "Keri [Russell, Rhys' partner] and I just looked at each other and we just could not believe it. "Matthew's described it as surreal and it just really was." Evans said that Russell "loves to celebrate him and she's his biggest supporter", and was "just cheering, whooping, hands in the air" after his award wins. This video can not be played "Luck and timing": Matthew Rhys on his historic Emmy Awards double win Evans said that she saw many Hollywood stars that evening, and was starstruck by Harrison Ford. "I'm a bit nervous about these things. I was just happy gaping and remembering things," she said. Despite attending multiple after-parties that evening, Evans said they made sure to video call their parents who were sat at home in their dressing gowns. "They were so far away, but they were so proud of him, as we all are... and they were pleased that I was there with him really." Evans told Owen that she unexpectedly burst into tears while watching his Emmy awards being engraved, saying that was the moment it "sank in". Matthew Rhys' sister Rachel celebrates his Emmy success Rachel Evans joins Lucy to look back on a proud week for the family. Evans told Owen that the response back in Wales had been "overwhelming". "We were just thrilled by the response when we woke up in the morning from home. It was just everything we could wish for," she said. In his acceptance speech, Rhys paid tribute to the "great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurturer as anyone else". "We are a small but mighty nation," he said, ending his speech with "diolch yn fawr iawn", which means "thank you very much" in Welsh. Evans said her brother has lived abroad for 25 years, but Wales "is absolutely in his heart and is his home", adding that he was "really keen to speak to everybody" the day after his wins. "Wales had been so supportive of his career all along and had really cheered him on," she added. title: Hear'Say, 'Snake' & Tony Blair: A Coventry win 25 years in the making
description: Coventry City's win over Nottingham Forest - thanks to Jay Dasilva's goal - was a victory which was over 25 years in the making following some dark days for the Sky Blues.
body: Jay Dasilva's goal was Coventry's first since Mustapha Hadji netted in a 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa on 5 May 2001 Hear'Say were top of the pops, a mobile phone game called 'Snake' was all the rage and Tony Blair was Prime Minister. Wind the clock back to April 2001 and things looked rather different. It was also the last time Coventry City tasted victory in English football's top flight. That came courtesy of a 1-0 win over Sunderland - John Hartson heading in the winner for Gordon Strachan's side in front of 20,946 fans at Highfield Road. Much has happened in the life of Coventry since that moment 9,287 days ago. A rollercoaster journey might be understating it. They were relegated at the end of the 2000-01 campaign and would spend the next 11 seasons in the second tier before dropping down to League One in 2012. Then followed a particularly dark and turbulent period in the club's history featuring points deductions and a stint in administration. Having left Highfield Road in 2005 they became embroiled in a bitter dispute over the Ricoh Arena in 2013 and its rent. The nadir, arguably, was when they were forced to play matches away from Coventry, at Northampton Town, before later plummeting down to the fourth tier for the first time in 59 years in 2017. Doubtless there were those packed into the Bridgford Stand at the City Ground on Saturday who were present during those years of Sky Blue hell. So the explosion of emotion at the full-time whistle - after Jay Dasilva's goal settled matters - felt like Sky Blue heaven. "It's been a tough opening for us, so those first Premier League points feel great," Coventry boss Frank Lampard told BBC Radio 5 Live. "I thought the players were brilliant. The fight, work ethic and togetherness but also the tactical side of it. They dug and fought for each other which is what you need to win a Premier League game." This video can not be played Coventry defeat Forest for first win since Prem return Coventry had been stranded on 99 Premier League wins for over a quarter of a century before this victory ticked them over to three figures at long last. Lampard hopes this victory could be a key staging post in a campaign where avoiding relegation will be the main aim. "It's really important for some of the players," he told BBC Match of the Day. "For many of them it is their debut in the Premier League, they haven't been here before and they need to feel like they belong and play like that." Lampard acknowledged his players must have thick skins to come through the slog of a Premier League season. The fact this victory came off the back of a 5-0 drubbing at home to Brighton makes it all the more rewarding for the Coventry boss. "There are lots of things we can learn and sometimes this year we may take those hits, it's a reality for teams that get to the Premier League," added Lampard. "It's important we overcome them in terms of how we take it on board and stay together. "It is easy to point in different directions when you lose but the group's really strong, really together, there'll have a good feeling from this one. But we'll keep our feet on the ground because it is one win, but it was needed for us." title: Premier League fans and players honour Noah Woods
description: Everton and Ipswich supporters and players pay tribute to the three-year-old, who died this week.
body: Ipswich and Everton fans stood to applaud in Noah's memory as a picture of him was shown on the big screen A tribute to three-year-old Noah Woods was shown on the big screen ahead of the Everton vs Ipswich Town Premier League match, while players wore black armbands in his memory. The toddler became separated from a relative after visiting a playground in Merriam Close, Brantham, on Tuesday afternoon, Suffolk Police said. About 1,300 members of the public joined a search to find Noah, who police said was non-verbal, partially deaf and had been undergoing an assessment for autism. Met Police divers recovered his body from a lake, known locally as Decoy Pond, on Wednesday afternoon and Suffolk Police said his death was not being treated as suspicious. Ipswich Town defender Leif Davis donated £2,000 to a fundraising appeal set up in aid of Noah Woods's family Three minutes into the game, won 1-0 by the home side, both sets of supporters stood to applaud in memory of Noah, Everton said in a post on X, external. Town defender Leif Davis donated £2,000 to the fundraising appeal set up to support Noah's family and captain Dara O'Shea and goalkeeper Christian Walton were among the club delegation who laid flowers at the playground where he went missing. On Thursday, Noah's father Rhys Woods paid tribute to his son in a message shared on a community Facebook group. He wrote: "There are no words to describe the pain of this loss, we are all absolutely heartbroken, Noah was the sweetest and most innocent little boy, with nothing but love to give, and we are going to miss him so very much." Noah Woods was at a playground with a relative before he went missing Suffolk Police said on Thursday that the body of the child recovered by police divers had been formally identified as Noah, subject to confirmation at formal inquest proceedings. The force said police still have a number of inquiries to complete before submitting a file for the coroner. Meanwhile, a fundraising page set up by Good Dads Club, a community of fathers based in nearby Colchester, had received more than £100,000 in donations from a total of more than 6,000 supporters by Saturday evening. title: Olid's Man Utd take big step forward after 'intense week'
description: A week ago, the picture at Manchester United looked bleak. Then on Saturday, victory was snatched away from them at Arsenal. But have we seen signs of improvement from Eva Olid's side?
body: Swedish midfielder Julia Zigiotti joined United from Bayern Munich last year A week ago, the picture for Manchester United looked a lot bleaker than it did at the full-time whistle on Saturday. Regardless of the stoppage-time equaliser they conceded at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, United's performance marked a major sign of progress. Defeats in their opening two matches, including a 5-0 thrashing by Chelsea, meant the list of questions for new manager Eva Olid seemed endless. United were disorganised, lacking in identity and were wide open at the back as their new era under Olid began in disappointing fashion. Those early displays did little to fill supporters with confidence, and Olid faced criticism for her decisions despite being in the job just a matter of weeks. However, a gutsy defensive display against Arsenal delivered a well-earned 1-1 draw and they were only denied victory by a 95th-minute leveller. While United's wait for a first Women's Super League win of the season continues, this performance suggested there may not be quite the cause for concern many suspected. Arsenal earn point with late leveller against Man Utd Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed Olid, 41, took over as manager in the summer, joining from Hearts, and promised to implement a new attacking style of play that focused heavily on possession. However, in their opening two games, United had just two shots on target and less than 40% possession in both matches. In the second of those games, they suffered the five-goal humbling at home by Chelsea. Few expected them to come away with anything against an Arsenal team who many tipped to win the title before the season kicked off, albeit they have struggled to score goals efficiently. Olid knew it would be a test but said on Friday she wanted her players to believe in themselves, show confidence, and to go back to the defensive roots they knew and built so well under her predecessor Marc Skinner. "It has been an intense week because there were a lot of emotions from players and staff. Nobody wants to lose 5-0," said Olid. "We grew as a team. The first day after losing 5-0 is not easy for anyone. We spoke and said we needed energy this week and a positive mindset. "The focus was the defensive shape. It's trying to get them more confidence." Olid ultimately wants her United team to dominate the ball and create more chances in front of goal, but this time they delivered on her plea to be defensively solid. They looked well organised in an even first half in which United midfielder Simi Awujo stood out, while Andrea Medina tracked back effectively. They won more duels than Arsenal, put in more tackles and completed more interceptions than their opponents - but still had only 40% of possession. Former England midfielder Izzy Christiansen told Sky Sports: "Manchester United have done a terrific job defensively. Overall, it's just been solid. "It looks so much better. The addition of Awujo has added some running power and they look so much freer in the final third." Arsenal's pressure grew in an edgy second half, but United held on for as long as they could and were unfortunate to concede with seconds left on the clock. They had led from midway through the half, after Julia Zigiotti seized on a mistake from Georgia Stanway. Smilla Holmberg's late volley denied United the spoils, but Olid saw foundations she could build on. "I think the attacking will come," she said. "If you implement a new style of play, you need time. "That effort, that intensity, can never be missed. We deserved three points for the hard work and the effort. "Of course, we need to create more chances. That is why I'm here. We need time, but today is the minimum that we have to deliver. I hope we can improve the attacking side." Manchester United lost their opening two matches of the season The biggest question is whether United really can build on this performance. They were already a difficult team to break down under Skinner but came up short in previous big games against WSL title rivals. In three Women's FA Cup finals, United won once against Tottenham, falling to higher-placed Chelsea on the other two occasions. Four years have passed since they won a game at Emirates Stadium against Arsenal, and their heavy defeat by Chelsea last week showed the gap to the elite still remains. Olid was brought in to transform their style by implementing an attacking philosophy that the club hope will deliver them long-term success. Patience was already beginning to wane after their demoralising early defeats, so conversations took place and they had to revert back to what they already knew. The result of that is significant progress from last week, but is it progress for the long term? "We are a team who need to press high, but at the same time we want to be better with the ball," Olid said on Sky Sports. "We lose simple passes and we cannot recognise the free player. Those things need to improve. It will come, I'm sure. "But we need to keep this [defensive structure], then from there, little by little, be an attacking team, create more chances, score more goals. "I cannot pretend it's happening in four weeks, but I'm sure it will come." title: Celtic win 'changes game' - but can they reverse Rangers' derby dominance?
description: Former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes a win for the Scottish champions against Rangers on Sunday "changes the game" after a turbulent week for Martin O'Neill's side.
body: Celtic and Rangers meet for the second Sunday in a row Former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes a win for the Scottish champions against Rangers on Sunday "changes the game" after a turbulent week for Martin O'Neill's side. Rangers triumphed 3-0 at home in last Sunday's Old Firm League Cup quarter-final before Celtic opened their Europa League campaign with a 3-1 defeat at home by Ferencvaros on Thursday. However, Celtic's early season domestic form has them going into Sunday's match in the east end of Glasgow - which like last week will have no visiting supporters in attendance - with a five-point advantage over their Ibrox rivals. "If Celtic win and they're eight points clear, it changes the game," Brown said on BBC Scotland's YouTube channel. "Can [Rangers] go to Celtic Park and do they exact same thing as last week? "Celtic now have had a week to understand how that game went. They are going to have to make sure that they match that energy but also match that willingness to go and win the match." Celtic seek spark as Rangers aim for further derby joy Scottish Premiership: Celtic v Rangers Listen on Sportsound, highlights on Sportscene 20/9/26 from 11:00 BST (radio), 19:15 (TV) Brown was impressed by Rangers manager Derek McInnes' change of approach in the season's first derby, change to a 3-5-2 shape and going man for man with Celtic's front three. "They went after Celtic from the get go," Brown said. "They looked like they wanted the win more. For him to change his tactics, nobody expected him to do that. That is a very, very good manager to pick that out." Brown also pondered Celtic's tactical plan. "Martin O'Neill when he was manager [from 2000-05], loved a 3-5-2 and it was fantastic to watch," said the former Scotland captain. "He had two big guys up front. That was an unbelievable team. He's not got those players that probably can be suited to a 3-5-2." This video can not be played Hogh needs a 'big game performance' With Yang Hyun-jun still on Asian Games duty with South Korea, Sebastian Tounekti and James Forrest have both been used on Celtic's left flank. But Brown believes the club's problems go beyond that. "Rangers got in their face, they blocked Callum McGregor off and as soon as you block Callum McGregor off and you man-mark Cal, it's hard for anyone else to go and dictate. "That's when you need a [Benjamin] Nygren to drop under, a [Mika] Baur to go and drop under and them do their job as well. You can't always keep looking at Cal to do everything." And Brown believes who starts best could be crucial. "Rangers were up for the fight," he added on Sportsound. "The first 15 minutes, it should be a battle. If you can go and win that battle, you can get the ball down. "Celtic started very, very slow last week. They need to go back to basics, make sure they've got the fight, make sure they've got the hunger because they've got the talent - I know they've got the talent. "You cannot have just one of those days against your biggest rivals, ever." title: Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta
description: An uncharacteristic performance from Arsenal saw the Gunners ship three goals in the defeat to Brighton - but could the loss be the "big lesson" they needed?
body: This video can not be played Highlights: Brilliant Brighton batter Arsenal in shock first defeat as champions An uncharacteristic performance from Arsenal saw them ship three goals at Brighton - but boss Mikel Arteta believes their first Premier League defeat this season could prove a "big lesson". The defending champions have been tipped by many to retain the title they won last season for the first time in 22 years. An impressive seven-match winning start to this campaign in all competitions - nine in successive league games dating back to April - backed up that belief. But Arsenal were humbled on the south coast as a well-drilled and clinical Brighton outfit beat them comfortably 3-0 to go third in the table. Arteta, whose side did not lose by more than a single goal in the top flight last term, acknowledged the Seagulls "deserved" the success and there were lessons the Gunners needed to take heading into the international break. The manner of the defeat - Arsenal's heaviest in a season where they were the reigning top-flight champions since 1989 - will also offer hope to their title rivals that they are not invincible. Arsenal handed first loss by brilliant Brighton Since taking charge in 2019, Arteta has made a point of reiterating how much he values physicality and the demands he puts on his side to win duels. But against Brighton, Arsenal were dominated all over the pitch and lost challenges which they would usually be expected to win. Arteta said he was "extremely disappointed" as his side were "very far" from doing the basics he expected, with uncertainty in defence, a loss of midfield control and lack of attacking creativity. Asked why they were below par, the Spaniard added: "Well, the first one because Brighton they were really good, and they had another bite, and at the times it was better. "There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50-50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them. "Sometimes there were some technical errors very much involved that opened us up in a really difficult way, but that's something to learn." He was quick to remind the media in his news conference after the game that it was still a good start to the season. The Gunners had 15 players at the World Cup which meant that a large part of the squad joined up for pre-season later than the rest of their team-mates. "That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," added Arteta. "What we've done and the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable, but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level." Arsenal lost their first game of the Premier League season against Brighton Brighton are currently the Premier League's top scorers with 16 goals - hitting eight of them in the past week - and could have had more against an Arsenal side who pride themselves on keeping clean sheets. The Gunners conceded the fewest goals of any side last season and just one got past David Raya in their first four league games before Saturday's defeat. "It should have been more, the chances Brighton created, they were that good," said former Newcastle striker Alan Shearer on BBC Radio 5 Live. "They absolutely battered Arsenal. How many times have we said that recently? From start to finish today Brighton were magnificent, every single one of them played their part. "They were strong, they were fit, they went after Arsenal. They had no fear and it worked brilliantly for them, it should have been six or seven goals." The Gunners were 2-0 down at the break and have not recovered to win from such a position in a league game since March 2008 at Bolton. "Every time Brighton chased down the ball, they got it absolutely spot on. They did it as a team, they didn't do it individually," added Shearer. "They thought, 'we respect Arsenal but we're not going to give them any space to play'. "The organisation was great and that just doesn't happen on it's own and you've got to give [manager] Fabian Hurzeler credit for that." Arsenal spent around £200m in the summer transfer window in a bid to strengthen the squad to challenge for more honours, and Arteta was asked if they needed reminding how tough the Premier League can be. He said: "I think they knew, I think we knew how tough it was going to be today, and the first thing that we had discussed was about the first part. "If you don't get out of that first part as winners, it will be extremely difficult to dominate the game and to have any probability of winning the game. "We knew that, but that's again credit to them for what they've done because they've overcome us and they had another edge than we did. "And that's something that at this level it's extremely important to respect and to understand before anything else." Former Premier League defender Curtis Davies believed the Gunners could put the result and display down to a "blip". "Their form this season has so far been good, this has been a really shocking performance," he said on 5 Live. "That defence today was nowhere near what it's used to being. The disappointment will be a set-piece goal conceded, Arsenal will have a real long look at themselves. "They didn't lay a glove on Brighton, and didn't make anything of their attacking situations." title: 'Greater things to come,' says Mitchell after England winning run ends
description: Head coach John Mitchell says England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.
body: This video can not be played Watch highlights: England 26-26 Canada Head coach John Mitchell believes England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak. England had won their past 39 Tests before Saturday's fixture. Canada, who had lost their 13 previous meetings with the Red Roses on English soil, held England to a 26-26 draw in a nail-biting, physical battle at Exeter's Sandy Park. It was only the second game domestically or internationally for England's players this season and, for Mitchell, one result is not justification to tear up the playbook. Instead, he views it as a building block towards future success. "It was just a matter of scoring across the white line," Mitchell said. "We were applying huge pressure. We just didn't convert." Avoiding defeat means the Red Roses have extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, a record they will hope to extend with WXV Global Series games against New Zealand, two more fixtures against Canada and another against the United States still to come. This video can not be played Watch: England coach John Mitchell on draw with Canada Mitchell said: "There was such good stuff in there. I'm very patient because we're just starting and we're still alive in this Test series. "I'm a realist. There will be greater things come as a result of this. There's a greater purpose and one Test match is not going to take us away from our purpose." For the opening 10 minutes, the match followed the script of last year's World Cup final between the two sides, with Canada breaking the deadlock and England immediately hitting back. But unlike last September, when they roared on to win 33-13, the Red Roses could not maintain control, with the two teams never separated by more than one try and England unable to convert 20 minutes of sustained pressure into the crucial score. While acknowledging England would have to review their "game management", captain Meg Jones hailed the spectacle the two sides delivered. "It was definitely tit for tat and definitely a game of momentum swinging," said centre Jones. "It was two good teams going at each other. "It was an amazing contest and competitive as we imagined. This is the first Test. We get another two shots at it [against Canada]." Echoing Jones' defiance before October trips to Toronto and Ottawa, Mitchell added: "We're in a Test series. It's 1-1. That's it." England's 39-game winning run started under former head coach Simon Middleton, who, after the World Cup final defeat in 2022, led the Red Roses to a Women's Six Nations Grand Slam in 2023. Mitchell then took charge midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign and had won every game until this one. England beat Scotland in the World Cup quarter-finals last September to claim their 31st straight Test win, surpassing their own record winning streak across both men's and women's international rugby union, which was set in 2022. World Cup glory, another Women's Six Nations title and victory over Australia last weekend extended that record further. "It's not necessarily something we speak about as a group; it's something that's just been there," Jones said of the winning run. "We're very process-driven, so the outcome tends to look after itself." title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins
description: Lib Dem leader Ed Davey claimed the party was aiming to beat its 2024 record of 72 MPs in any snap election.
body: This video can not be played Ed Davey says the Lib Dems have "a historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform" Sir Ed Davey said the Liberal Democrats are "a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform" as the party's conference began in Brighton. The Lib Dem leader sought to strike a combative stance as he faced down some criticism from MPs, including one who said publicly that they felt the party was struggling for relevance. On the first day of the autumn conference, Sir Ed warned an "unholy alliance" between Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Farage could turn the UK into a "Trump satellite state". Addressing speculation about a possible snap election, he said the party was ready to fight and would build its so-called orange wall even higher by winning more than its 2024 record of 72 MPs. Sir Ed's attention-grabbing stunts helped raise the party's profile ahead of the last election, but recent polling showed 43% of respondents were unclear what the Liberal Democrats stand for, with just over half describing them as "weak". In an essay, external written ahead of conference, South Cotswolds MP Roz Savage asked: "Why are we as a party struggling for relevance at precisely the moment when so many people feel powerless?" She urged the party to rediscover its "insurgent spirit" rather than being the "polite custodians of a system that leaves people feeling powerless". Asked about her comments, Sir Ed said: "No, I heard Roz [Savage], and I really value her, but I think she's wrong on that. "If you look at our election results up and down the country, we now run more councils than the Conservatives." He added: "Listen, MPs get elected and they get frustrated because they can't change the world. "I'm afraid that's the political system. I've been used to it for a little while and people are learning about that frustration." Speaking on the pebbles of Brighton Beach, Sir Ed told reporters the Liberal Democrats would fight to stop a Reform government. "One of the things that makes us unique is that we are a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform," he said. "Many of the seats he needs to get himself into No 10 are seats that we will defend and indeed win - and we are also able to take seats off the Conservatives, because I really fear that Kemi Badenoch will give the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage, so we have got to stop the Conservatives as well. "We have got an historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform." He added a manifesto working group had already been set up in case of an early election "so we'll be ready if it comes early, but, you know, it still could be up to three years away". Sir Ed insisted his party has a "distinctive position" in British politics, and will use the four-day conference to position it to take on the challenge from Reform as well as its typical rivals the Conservatives, talking up their focus on the NHS and goal of re-joining the EU single market and customs union. The Lib Dem leader highlighted how six former Conservative cabinet ministers were among 25 Tories to have defected to Reform in the last two years, claiming they were now competing with each other to see who can divide the country more, rather than looking to fix the country's problems. "An unholy alliance between Farage and Badenoch is the only way either can get into power," he said. "Together, they want to turn Britain into a Trump satellite state which would trash our NHS, turn our communities against each other, cause untold damage to our environment, and trample over traditional British values of fairness, tolerance, and decency. "A bigger Orange Wall is the only thing that can stand between Britain and this dangerous experiment, and we will not let them pass." Davey also attacked the Labour government as having no plan for growth, failing to support families struggling with the cost of living and taxing small businesses "to the brink". Ahead of a speech to party members, Davey urged Liberal Democrats not to look away from injustice or "human dignity under attack" but to fight back. title: Eagle leaves McIlroy two off Wentworth lead
description: Rory McIlroy stands two strokes behind the third-round leaders heading into the final day after a three-under 72 at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
body: This video can not be played McIlroy bags a birdie to apply pressure on PGA Championship leaders BMW PGA Championship - round three -13 M Elvira (Spa), F Celli (Ita); -12 J Veerman (US), A Del Rey (Spa) JJ Spaun (US) Selected others: -11 R McIlroy (NI), A Scott (AUS); -10 S Bairstow (Eng), M Wallace (Eng), R MacIntyre (Sco); -9 J Smith (Eng), M Fitzpatrick (Eng), A Rai (Eng); -7 R Fisher (Eng), S Lowry (Ire); -6 A Fitzpatrick (Eng); -5 D Law (Sco), J Rose (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), T Hatton (Eng) Rory McIlroy finished with a superb eagle to move two shots off the lead heading into the final day of the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth. Northern Ireland's world number two made a three on the par-five 18th to stay in contention with a three-under 69 leaving him on 11 under. Spain's Manuel Elvira and Italy's Filippo Celli share the lead after both made birdies on the final hole to leave them 13 under. But there is a congested leaderboard with 20 players within four strokes of the lead. Alejandro Del Rey, JJ Spaun and Johannes Veerman are one shot behind with an exciting finish in store on Sunday. McIlroy is attempting to win a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title and can boost his hopes by securing the second Wentworth title of his career. "There are a lot of people around the leaders," he said after another round in blustery conditions. "I think the conditions over the last couple of days are the reason why no-one has got away from the pack, just because it has played so tricky and difficult. "I'll probably try not to look at the leaderboards on the front nine, and if I need to play a little bit more aggressively on the back, I'll do it." title: Frenetic draw with Canada ends England's 39-game winning run
description: England's remarkable winning run comes to an end as they are held to a nail-biting 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park.
body: This video can not be played Watch highlights: England 26-26 Canada Tries: Moloney-MacDonald 2, Botterman, Field Cons: Harrison 3 Tries: Gibson, Menin 2 Cons: De Goede 3 England's remarkable 39-match winning run came to an end as they were held to a nail-biting 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park. The Red Roses were unable to escape the clutches of a relentless Canada, who they beat in last year's World Cup final, with the two sides sharing four tries apiece in front of a raucous 14,573 crowd in Exeter. Canada are the first team to avoid defeat against England since New Zealand beat them in the 2022 World Cup final, but John Mitchell's side are now unbeaten in 40 Tests. The draw also ended England's 100% home record against Canada, having won each of their previous 13 home meetings. In a pulsating opening 25 minutes, England were twice required to come from behind, with tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and Hannah Botterman cancelling out scores by Lizzie Gibson and DaLeaka Menin for Canada. Exeter winger Moloney-MacDonald had a try disallowed before giving England the lead for the first time in the 32nd minute, getting on the end of a surging run from Sadia Kabeya for her second of the match. However, Canada - who had earlier had a brilliant solo effort from Asia Hogan-Rochester chalked off for a forward pass - hit back on the stroke of half-time when Menin crashed over from close range. England weathered 10 minutes of sustained pressure at the beginning of the second half before the two sides exchanged tries again, prop Bryony Field restoring the lead for the hosts before Canada scrum-half Olivia Apps scored under the posts after a dancing run from Sophie de Goede down the left wing. England looked the most likely to win in a chaotic final 10 minutes, including being held up over the line, but were left to a rue a turnover in front of the posts and a loose carry as Canada battled through for the draw. The two sides will resume their rivalry with two Tests in Canada in October. Before then, England face New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday, 26 September. Canada kept 2024 World Player of the Year Ellie Kildunne off the scoresheet on Saturday England's run of 39 consecutive wins, which started in March 2023, encompassed four successive Women's Six Nations crowns, two WXV1 successes and a home World Cup triumph in 2025. But all things must come to an end. It is not that England have not been tested in that time. A week earlier, Australia led 10-5 at half-time, marking the first time the Red Roses had trailed at the interval since 2020. France have often been a thorn in their side in Six Nations deciders too, while Canada ran them close in a WXV meeting in 2024. The challenge for opponents has been sustaining that pressure for a full 80-minute performance, and Canada did not let up at Sandy Park. Twice they led, twice they were pegged back. There was an ominous feeling when Moloney-MacDonald put the hosts in front, but Canada seized their opportunity, capitalising on back-to-back penalties in England's 22 to level. On the back foot as England - energised by their replacements - pressed for the win, they responded twice more, first cancelling out Field's try and then doggedly defending in their own half for much of the final 20 minutes. As impressive as Canada were in defence, England were also left to rue the lack of a clinical touch in Canada's 22 and opted against kicking for three points when awarded a penalty in the closing stages. But rather than be disappointed, head coach Mitchell hailed the opportunity that the result presents. "Canada were good and we were also good," he said. "At times it was a real arm wrestle. "We are really in a Test series, which is great for us. Canada need to be congratulated on their performance. "For us, it's about getting better and there is a greater purpose than just one Test match. This is ideal for us and allows us to stay focused on what's necessary to get a better performance." Speaking before the match, Canada captain De Goede said recollections of last year's World Cup final defeat has kept her awake "four to five nights a week". Even after snapping the world champions' record unbeaten run, De Goede contemplated what might have been. "There's definitely some frustration that we didn't get the win in the end, but also we're moving in the right direction from the last time we played them," said the second row forward. "We need to be critical of ourselves after the game because I do think we could have got the win. "We know we can get it across the line and that's where the disappointment comes from. There's a lot of pride in our defensive stance in the last 20 minutes, but we really struggled to exit, so we'll have to watch back what we were doing on the attacking side of the ball." With the clock in the red, Canada had a scrum near to their own 22 and De Goede said the players on the field were keen to keep the game alive, but afterwards the skipper reluctantly conceded that coach Kevin Rouet made the right call by instructing them to kick to touch and end the match. "The plan on the field - we were like 'let's go for the win'," said De Goede. "Then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. "I do trust Kevin, he has the cooler head in that moment. If we gave away a penalty off the next breakdown, we'd be sitting here going 'why didn't you kick it out?'" title: Analysis: Trump ramps up feud with media after week of setbacks
description: An embattled Trump has injected his fight with the news media with new acrimony, writes the BBC's Anthony Zurcher.
body: President Donald Trump has infused his ongoing feud with the White House press with a new level of acrimony. Journalists from three major media outlets - CNN, Politico and MS Now - were denied access and had their press credentials confiscated on Saturday morning as they attempted to enter the White House grounds for work. As media watchdog organisations and the White House Correspondents Association cry foul, Trump appears set to press ahead with a sweeping effort to punish these outlets. In his Truth Social post announcing his decision on Friday, he said he was "banning" the organisations because "of their constant 'reporting' of fake news". In remarks later that day, he complained that "something is wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories". "If they want to write them, that's fine," he continued. "I don't have to let them into the people's house", he said, referring to the White House. Journalists denied White House access after Trump banned some media outlets The president's frustration at the media, however, came after a week of setbacks in which major institutions handed him a series of losses across his agenda. First, the Supreme Court blocked his plan to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterms. This prompted Trump to lash out at the court's justices including those he had appointed. "These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court," he said. The Federal Reserve, the US central bank, then raised interest rates after Trump had spent months arguing they should be cut. This was followed by a judge ordering his administration to give 30 days' notice before making any changes to the Kennedy Center arts venue in Washington DC after the president warned it could be "ripped down". These headlines, combined with approval ratings that recently sunk to record lows for his second term, suggest Trump is facing challenging political headwinds. His latest attack on the press, however, raises clear legal questions. The First Amendment to the US Constitution forbids Congress from "abridging" the freedom of the press. It is language that courts have long interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage. All three targeted news outlets have promised to file lawsuits challenging Trump's decision. Although the breadth of this move is unprecedented, it is far from the first time the Trump administration has attempted to limit or deny access to the White House to members of mainstream media outlets. In his first term, the administration revoked CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press credentials, setting off a legal battle that was ultimately resolved in the journalist's favour. It also temporarily suspended the pass of a reporter who had a heated argument with White House adviser Sebastian Gorka – a move that also was subsequently blocked by the courts. Last year, the White House banned reporters for the Associated Press from participating in the president's press pool - which allows media outlets access to smaller in-town and travelling presidential appearances - because the newswire service would not follow Trump's move to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America. That dispute also led to a protracted - and yet to be fully resolved - legal battle, prompting the White House to change press pool rules to drop the guaranteed spot for all wire services. This video can not be played Watch: Trump says ban on some news outlets from White House is "because they're fake news" The White House bans, however, represent a dramatic escalation. The restrictions include access to the entirety of the White House grounds, not just the press pool. And they target entire news organisations, not just a single disfavoured correspondent. While Trump has been clear about the motives behind his decision, he has shed little light on why he has acted now. He has regularly criticised his press coverage since he first entered national politics more than a decade ago, but he said on Friday there was no specific incident that prompted his announcement. At the moment, however, the president is embattled. Even beyond the week of clear setbacks, he is in the midst of an unpopular and difficult-to-resolve war of choice in Iran, which has led to a surge in energy and other consumer prices, deflating his standing with the American public. Polls also suggest his party faces an uphill battle to retain control of the House of Representatives and perhaps the Senate in November's crucial midterm congressional elections. His attempts to improve the public's mood by touting his accomplishments in campaign events and at his Republican Party's convention earlier this month in Texas have, at least so far, proven ineffective. There may be more behind the Trump's decision to lash out at the media this weekend. But it could also simply be an indication of presidential frustration in the face of events and circumstances, some of his own making, that are turning against him. title: From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style
description: From obscurity and near oblivion to Premier League and Europe - Brighton celebrate their 125th anniversary.
body: This video can not be played Highlights: Brilliant Brighton batter Arsenal in shock first defeat as champions Brighton's 125th anniversary celebrations could not have gone much better. Decked out in specially-made commemorative kit, Fabian Hurzeler's side produced a performance befitting the occasion. A home game against Arsenal had the potential to put a dampener on the festivities but instead Brighton marmalised the defending Premier League champions. A record crowd of 31,944 were at the Amex Stadium to witness it, roaring their side on to the most comprehensive of 3-0 wins. Pascal Gross fired them in front, Charalampos Kostoulas drilled in the second on the stroke of half-time and Chema Andres' header made it three after the break. They had the chances to add to that lead but three was more than enough and the celebrations in the stands had started long before the final whistle. "It was a special one, not only because we played against maybe the best team in England but because of the performance," Hurzeler told BBC Match of the Day. "The boys started really intense, they won their personal duels, played good in possession and created chances. "I'm really proud of my team, hopefully they enjoy it today because these kind of moments are important to enjoy." From near oblivion to Europe and beating the champions of England on the club's milestone day, this is the Seagulls' remarkable story... It is Thursday, 9 November, 2023. Brighton manager Roberto de Zerbi is addressing his players in the Amsterdam Arena before their Europa League tie with Ajax. "There's 3,000 Brighton fans in this stadium tonight," said the Italian. "But there's more than twice that number in the city who have travelled over. Remember that when you go on to that pitch." A long-standing senior Brighton official was in the dressing room that day. A fan first and foremost, but someone who has spent almost three decades working for the club. "It made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up," he said. For some clubs, an encounter with Ajax is commonplace. Not Brighton. "The royalty of European football," says the official. "From where we've come from, to be in that environment. It was a pinch-me moment." Brighton won 2-0. It was the high point of the first European campaign in the club's history. Ask Paul Samrah for his single most memorable moment as a Brighton fan and a very different answer comes back, which goes to the heart of why, as they celebrate their 125th birthday around the visit of Arsenal, the Seagulls are almost unique among English clubs. August 2007. "After the years of campaigning, the days and nights I spent fighting for regime change and then for the stadium, the moment I heard we'd actually got planning permission, that our objectors had decided not to continue their fruitless efforts to stop the stadium," he explained. The two stories highlight the before and after reality of Brighton & Hove Albion. Brighton's final game at the Goldstone Ground in April 1997 was an emotional occasion Brighton fans raced on to the pitch after the final match at the Goldstone Ground Brighton spent 12 years playing at the Withdean Stadium from 1999 Formed in 1901, Brighton were a Southern League club for almost two decades before they were voted into the Football League. They had experienced only seven seasons in Division Two when they were promoted to the top flight for the first time in 1979. For years, they were known outside Sussex chiefly for "And Smith must score..." - the BBC radio commentary, delivered by the late Peter Jones, at a critical point during the 1983 FA Cup final, late in extra time. It was the moment when Gordon Smith, clear on goal with a chance to earn Brighton their first major trophy, saw his shot saved by Manchester United goalkeeper Gary Bailey. United won the replay. But in 1995, chairman Bill Archer sold Brighton's Goldstone Ground, their home since 1902, because of escalating debts that there was no obvious way of paying. Fans were not consulted and no alternative stadium was put in place. Brighton did not leave until 1997, although their final season at the Goldstone was only confirmed by the property company who owned the stadium, after the final game of the 1995-96 campaign, which had to be abandoned as thousands of furious fans spilled on to the pitch to demonstrate against the ownership. Both crossbars were snapped amid the tumult. After two seasons playing 70 miles away at Gillingham, and with the idea of a new stadium in the Toad's Hole Valley area of Brighton a non-starter, the club returned to the city in 1999 and started playing at Withdean Stadium, most famous for being the home athletics track of Olympic middle distance gold medallist Steve Ovett. That brings us back to De Zerbi's pre-match team-talk at Ajax. Brighton had more than 7,000 fans in Amsterdam that night. When they moved into the Withdean, its capacity was only 6,000. The modern Brighton really is a totally different club to the one that existed before. "After the 1983 FA Cup final, players were sold, there was no investment, the Goldstone was decaying and the crowds were dipping," said Samrah. "There was no communication between board and fans, directors came and went. There was no continuity, no leadership, no direction. We were just rudderless." There are some notable figures in the Brighton story. Former Football Association executive director David Davies got involved, Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott overturned a rejected planning application for Brighton's current stadium in Falmer. Former chairman Dick Knight stabilised a club that in 1997 came within 27 minutes of being relegated out of the Football League. Without that trio, and many more, it is quite possible Brighton would not exist. title: England crush Sri Lanka to top T20 world rankings
description: England steamroller Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.
body: This video can not be played Highlights: England take the series with 6 wicket win and seven overs to spare Third T20 international, Old Trafford Sri Lanka 124 all out (18.5 overs): Nissanka 36 (24), K Mendis 35 (28); Baker 2-17, Archer 2-23, Jacks 2-31 England 126-2 (9.4 overs): Buttler 62* (32), Brook 33 (21) England won by eight wickets, won series 3-0 England steamrollered Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings. Watched by new Test coach Stephen Fleming, England once again outclassed the tourists to conclude a one-sided series played on the fringe of autumn. England's pace bowlers were outstanding in dismissing Sri Lanka for a paltry 124, then the home side chased the target in 9.4 overs. Jamie Overton conceded only 15 runs in his four overs, including taking a wicket. Sonny Baker's improvement continued with 2-17 and Jofra Archer recovered from an expensive start to return 2-23. England's fielding was sharp, best demonstrated by Liam Dawson's direct hit to run out Eshan Malinga. The target was never likely to pose a challenge to an England batting line-up that remains powerful despite Phil Salt and Jacob Bethell being absent injured. Though opener Aneurin Donald was out for 13, Jos Buttler and Harry Brook strolled the pursuit with a second-wicket stand of 85. Brook was run out for 33, leaving Buttler to wrap it up with a six that left him unbeaten on 61. The victory by eight wickets was concluded with 62 balls to spare - the most for England in a home T20 international. The success was England's 23rd win in 26 completed T20s since Brook took charge in the summer of 2024. They have reclaimed their number one ranking from India. The pity for this group is a rare lengthy wait until the next global T20 tournament. The next men's T20 World Cup is not until 2028, the same year T20 cricket makes its debut in the Olympics. England are instead building towards a 50-over World Cup in southern Africa in the autumn of 2027. Three one-day internationals against the Sri Lankans begin in Durham on Tuesday. This video can not be played Brook dives brilliantly to make catch Buttler crunches 62 not out as England seal 3-0 series win - as it happened A feature of England's success in this format has been captain Brook's heavy use of spin bowling. On this occasion the spinners took a backseat – Adil Rashid and Dawson sent down only four overs between them. Instead, it was the seamers to the fore, even without the variations of Sam Curran, another England player absent injured. Baker endured difficult debuts in all three international formats, yet in this series has started to show his potential. After Archer's first over went for 15, Baker had Lahiru Udara sky to wicketkeeper Buttler. He later returned to wrap up the innings, taking the final wicket when Dilshan Madushanka skied to Brook. Archer was a spectator for some time after his initial struggle. When he returned, he got the dangerous Kamindu Mendis to pull to deep mid-wicket for 35. Archer's second wicket was curious – Wanindu Hasaranga out hit-wicket attempting a slog, his bat almost placed on top of the bails. Overton was the pick, returning his most economical figures when bowling his full allocation of four in a T20 international. Though Tom Banton dropped a catch slipping on the greasy outfield, England's fielding was otherwise exceptional. Brook took a sharp catch at mid-wicket to remove Pathum Nissanka for 36, Rashid was alert enough to run out Charith Asalanka and Dawson's direct hit was the coup de grace. This video can not be played Bizarre wicket sees Hasaranga dismissed for hitting own stumps At the age of 29, Donald has been given an international opportunity in this series as a replacement for Salt. He has shown only glimpses of his excellent domestic form, returning a high score of 21. On this occasion, he tried to wallop the spin of Tharindu Rathnayake over long-on and was stumped by a distance. In Buttler and Brook, the captains past and present, England have two men in supreme form. Buttler is England's best white-ball batter of all-time, while Brook is on the way to being one of their greats. Such is their quality, the second-wicket pair turned the remainder of the chase into little more than a glorified net. Sri Lanka were scruffy – they conceded 17 runs in wides. The hapless nature of the visitors' display was epitomised when Brook should have been caught off Madushanka, only for keeper Kamil Mishara and point fielder Nissanka to look at each other as the ball dropped to the ground. There was no need for Brook to attempt a single that Hasaranga fielded in his follow-through, the bowler hitting direct with a throw at the non-striker's end. Buttler won it in the following over, clubbing 18 from four Malinga deliveries, with two maximums hammered over the leg side. title: No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat
description: Tottenham look no closer to solving their problems as they slip to a home defeat by Aston Villa to add to their Premier League misery.
body: Tottenham have lost three of their opening five Premier League games It was all so predictable. The closer Tottenham went to scoring the more it seemed likely they would concede. "Too fragile" was how boss Roberto de Zerbi described his side after the 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa. Comfortable and on top until Johan Manzambi's scrappy opener for the visitors - while Spurs were temporarily down to 10 men as Micky van de Ven had treatment - they never recovered. It only got worse as goals from Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia put the visitors 3-0 up. De Zerbi's men now go into a three-week international break still waiting for a first Premier League win this season as Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke's late goals - the club's first in the league - were of little consolation. In the bottom three after spending over £300m in the summer there appears to be no end in sight to Spurs' struggles. Tottenham scored their first Premier League goals of the season against Aston Villa Tottenham have failed to win any of their last 36 Premier League matches when conceding first so the writing was on the wall at half-time. They dominated the opening 20 minutes and Villa keeper Zion Suzuki denied Savio and Archie Gray but, without a goal, they were always going to be vulnerable at the other end. And so, in first-half injury time, a Villa goal was almost inevitable. Andy Robertson tried to stop a corner but only gifted the ball to John McGinn and, after Boubacar Kamara's effort, Manzambi prodded in from close range. It added the insult to Van de Ven's injury, a blow to the face that kept him off the pitch. Some Tottenham fans missed the goal as they headed for their half-time refreshments but several thousand did not bother to stay until the end. They streamed out of the stands after Buendia's brilliant 25-yard bullet found the top corner in the 79th minute, missing Gallagher and Van Hecke's late efforts. De Zerbi said: "My focus is why we concede the first goal with 10 players, we can stay stronger, communicate more and more, defend in a compact way. "I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur as a centre-back in that minute and Mateus Fernandes as a midfielder. If we have a red card we can play 70 minutes with 10 players. "In the second half we scored the goal with [Mohammed] Kudus, offside, I don't know if some players lost energy but we conceded an unacceptable goal. We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season. "We had many meetings [about it] and we have to explain another game like Newcastle where we played the first half well and then we lose. It's my responsibility. "I take my responsibility but in that moment of the game we have to defend, we have to defend compact, the leaders have to be leaders. "I am very sad and frustrated with the performance. We cannot lose this game in this way. The second goal we conceded was incredible." "Sacked in the morning" chanted the Villa fans to De Zerbi who, at times, looked out of ideas once his side fell 2-0 behind. It was Tottenham's worst start to a top-flight season since 2008-09, when they also had two points after five games. Juande Ramos was dismissed as manager after three more defeats before Harry Redknapp lifted them up to eighth. Spurs have also now gone five league games without a win at the start of a season for the first time since 1986. Former Brighton striker Glenn Murray, however, says De Zerbi needs time. "He is trying to build something, it will take time," he told BBC's Final Score. "Taking the emotion out of it, looking at the stats, they have had more shots in three of the past four games, more possession and more touches in the opposition box. "They are positives, be patient, the metrics are there to say he will turn it around. They need to be patient with Roberto De Zerbi, with all the signings, it takes time to gel and get to know each other." Emi Buendia scored twice at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last season - in the Premier League and FA Cup A decisive moment came when Kudus thought he had levelled on the hour, but Robertson was ruled just offside having delivered the cross. Seven minutes later Jackson scored from Suzuki's long launch downfield and it was game over. Villa's rebuild, the club committing to spending more than £250m was out of necessity because of their own high-profile exits. There was an expectation change was forthcoming and the Europa League winners were always going to go through a period of transition. But a first league victory was vital for them too after three defeats in their opening four games. While Villa look in better shape as new players settle, Spurs have thrown money at their problems after two relegation battles, but are no closer to solving them. Sandro Tonali, the £100m midfielder from Newcastle, was overshadowed by Villa's tenacious skipper McGinn - a £2.75m buy from Hibs eight years ago. Brazil winger Savio was denied three times by the impressive Suzuki but faded, while Omar Marmoush was signed to bring goals, but provided nothing. De Zerbi added: "I didn't speak with the players [afterwards], I didn't want to say anything. The players who go to the national team, they have to play and work. "The others, [James] Maddison, Gallagher, [Dominic] Solanke, Tosin [Adarabioyo, [Marcos] Senesi, Savio have to work more because their physical condition, I didn't like in this game." Villa survive late Spurs fightback to earn first Premier League win Manzambi catches eye as Villa beat Spurs - player ratings Former Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole questioned Tottenham's transfer business after their spend of around £302m. After Tonali, £85m went on bringing in Mateus Fernandes from West Ham. The Portuguese midfielder was subbed at half-time and De Zerbi said he "didn't like" Fernandes' performance, while £75m was spent on Savio from Manchester City. Marmoush will cost £60m

title: Ratcliffe 'must go' says Man Utd Muslim fan group
description: The Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club says United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe "must go" after he spoke out against immigration and said the country was "on the slide".
body: Ratcliffe acquired a 27.7% stake in Man Utd in 2024 The Manchester United Muslim Supporters group says club co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe "must go" after he spoke out against immigration levels and said the country was "on the slide". Billionaire Ratcliffe, who is one of Britain's richest people and founder of petrochemical giant Ineos, made the comments in an interview with the BBC on Saturday. Ratcliffe said the UK was in decline because of a combination of high taxes and high immigration. He has previously apologised for "offending some people" with his language after saying the UK had been "colonised by immigrants". At the time, in February, United responded by saying the club "prides itself" on being "inclusive", while BBC Sport cited a source familiar with the Glazer family as understanding the club's majority shareholders were "horrified" by his initial remarks and saw them as showing "disregard for their ownership". "We condemned those comments then," said the Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club (MUMSC) on Saturday, in a statement of no confidence in the club's ownership. "He [Ratcliffe] subsequently apologised for his choice of language. We hoped a lesson had been learned. Clearly, it has not. "This week, Sir Jim has again placed immigration and people receiving benefits at the centre of his explanation for Britain's problems, arguing that nobody is 'tough enough' to deal with either. "We find these latest comments deeply disappointing and completely unacceptable." Ratcliffe campaigned for a Leave vote in the 2016 European Union referendum and has been a tax resident in Monaco since 2020. He acquired a 27.7% stake in Man Utd in 2024, and has since restructured the organisation, overseeing 450 redundancies, overhauling senior management and sacking two managers. MUMSC highlighted that United's "players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds". The group added: "Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them. That diversity isn't a weakness of Manchester United. It is part of Manchester United." In the statement, the MUMSC also called on the Glazer family to go. MUMSC said its members were among the club's fans who hoped Ratcliffe's arrival "would finally signal meaningful change" after the Glazer family had "presided over Manchester United's decline". However, the group pointed to "higher ticket prices" and "a stadium allowed to deteriorate", along with "a football team that continues to fall further behind where Manchester United should be", among their concerns which "now extend beyond the pitch". Manchester United entered the weekend sitting 13th in the Premier League after gaining four points from their first four Premier League games, and they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday with a 3-2 home defeat by Brighton. "After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club," MUMSC concluded. "Enough is enough. It is time for change. The Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe must go." title: CNN and MS NOW say reporters denied White House access after Trump banned some media outlets
description: The reporters' badges were confiscated, the outlets reported.
body: CNN and MS NOW journalists have been denied access to the White House after US President Donald Trump announced he was banning the outlets. An MS NOW reporter and a photographer tried entering the White House grounds on Saturday morning, but their badges would not scan and an officer confiscated them, the outlet reported. CNN also said Saturday morning that one of its reporters was denied access and had her badge seized. Trump said on Friday he was barring MS NOW, CNN, and Politico - three major US media outlets - from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration. Press freedom advocates called the move "unconstitutional". "The officer asked me to hand over my badge. He said that it was disabled," MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner said. "I asked why I was not able to get inside. He said it was above him." Gardner added that while her and her colleague's badges were disabled, an MS NOW producer was still able to scan her badge to get in, though she was not given an explanation as to why the producer's badge still worked. CNN reporter Betsy Klein said a Secret Service agent told her her badge had been deactivated. An MS NOW spokesperson said in a statement that the White House "belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars". "MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy." It was not clear whether Politico reporter were at the White House on Saturday. Following Trump's ban, all three outlets have spoken out against the decision, accusing Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press. "We have a right under the US Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right," CNN said. In his announcement, Trump did not mention specific stories or reporting from the three outlets that prompted the move, but later said "it's really just cumulative stories over the last few years". Trump added that there "may be others to join them", but has not given a directive banning additional news outlets. When later asked by a reporter what he meant by others to come, Trump responded: "Others to come in terms of fake news? Well, you know, the New York Times is fake news, the Washington Post is fake news." Several groups dedicated to the freedom of the press have called out Trump's White House ban as illegal and unconstitutional. A major group that provides legal services to the media - the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press - said it expected Trump's ban to be struck down quickly by the courts because it was "flatly unconstitutional". "The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," said Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, which provides legal services to the media. It's the latest in a series of moves by the administration to target media outlets Trump says are critical of him, including legal action against US and international outlets like The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and the BBC. Some of the lawsuits have resulted in media organisations agreeing to pay multimillion dollar settlements. Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is ongoing. Additional reporting from Bernd Debusmann Jr and Max Matza. title: Smoke seen near Riyadh airport after air raid alerts in Saudi capital
description: The King Khalid International Airport incident caused hours of flight disruptions and comes amid an escalating conflict with Houthi rebels in Yemen.
body: This video can not be played Watch: Thick black plumes of smoke rise from near Riyadh's international airport A column of black smoke has been seen near Riyadh's international airport hours after air raid alerts were issued in the Saudi capital. It was the first time residents had been given an alert and urged to stay indoors since a recent escalation in the conflict with Iran-backed Houthi militants in neighbouring Yemen. A number of apparent explosions were heard in the capital and major problems were reported at King Khalid International Airport, with the tracking website FlightRadar24 reporting delays and cancellations earlier in the day, external. One report suggested a fuel tank had been set on fire near the airport. There has been no official comment from Saudi authorities. How escalating Saudi oil crisis could drive up prices everywhere Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks An AFP news agency journalist reported that firefighters could be seen trying to extinguish the flames of a burnt-out fuel tank belonging to state oil and gas company Aramco. The Saudi Civil Defence had sent out phone alerts overnight warning of potential danger in Riyadh and other regions, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning. Residents told AFP on condition of anonymity that they had heard what sounded like a round of explosions echoing through the city after the alerts. "I heard the alarm, then my windows shook," said a resident of northern Riyadh, 27. "It was definitely scary. I was not expecting this." On Friday, the Houthis announced that they had thwarted Saudi attacks on the Yemeni capital Sanaa which they said bore the hallmarks of an Islamic State operation. Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said Saudi Arabia had carried out 300 strikes across Yemen during the past week. He warned the reported attacks on Sanaa would "not go unanswered". The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia. They have attacked targets inside Saudi Arabia on several occasions in recent months, and said this week that they were responsible for downing a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen. According to an unconfirmed report from AFP, quoting military sources on both sides of Yemen's civil war, fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces claimed 48 lives on Saturday. The Houthis said 31 of their fighters had been killed while government sources said their side had lost 17 soldiers, according to the news agency. On Friday, the International Organization for Migration, a UN body, reported that the number of people displaced as a result of recent fighting had passed 104,796, external. The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to a key shipping route used by the Gulf state to export to Asia and Europe. The group said the naval blockade was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen. Saudi vessels have relied on that stretch of the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. On Friday, investment banking giant JP Morgan said it was struggling to predict how oil prices would be impacted by the war, telling investors in a rare note that "we simply don't know how to model the endgame". title: Nature reserve to double in size, thanks to gift
description: Staffordshire Wildlife Trust acquires an area of wet woodland, marsh and pastureland due to the will.
body: Staffordshire Wildlife Trust has secured more land on the reserve due to the gift in will A nature reserve will double in size due to a generous gift left in a will, a wildlife trust has said. The donation has secured more land at Jackson's Coppice and Marsh Nature Reserve near Eccleshall, Staffordshire. An area of wet woodland and marsh has been acquired alongside pastureland south of the River Sow. Public footpaths and a scheme to slow the flow of the river in heavy rainfall are being planned. "This is fantastic news for wildlife and a wonderful example of how gifts in wills can create lasting change for nature," Jeff Sim of Staffordshire Wildlife Trust said. The donation was made by trust supporter David Aldred. Plans for the floodplain land include coppicing mature alder trees and managing willow growth to support a greater diversity of plants and wildlife. Under the trust's ownership, the floodplain will enable the river to flow slower during heavy rainfall and will alleviate flooding downstream. The reserve's expansion provides public footpaths over the new land, so visitors will be able to explore different trails, the trust said. "We can restore habitats on a much bigger scale, making more of a difference to the wildlife that relies on these places to live, feed and breed," Sim added.
